params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W1-GEN — STATEMENT (target statement)
   2| 
   3| Ticket W1-GEN, Theory Wave 1. Lead: Claude Opus 5.5.
   4| Status of this file: **v2.3** (v2 LOCKED 2026-11-08; v2.1 (C6) design, v2.2 (C1′) added, v2.3 (C5)(d) layout and (C1′) energy — all logged in LOG.md) after statement-lock review R01 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol high,
   5| LOCK-WITH-CHANGES; all nine required changes applied, see `reviews/R01_statement_lock_sol.md` and its disposition
   6| `reviews/R01_disposition.md`). Later changes are logged in LOG.md and flagged in REPORT.md.
   7| 
   8| SoP = `Theory_work/State_of_Project/sections/`; NBH = `Theory_work/Old_Projects/New_BVS_Headquarters/`;
   9| BS = `NBH/branch_snapshots/`; T22iii = `Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/`.
  10| 
  11| ## 0. Target and how this statement answers it
  12| 
  13| Goal (HQ brief): consistency of the method's **reported** HPM Ŝ⁺ on a general, checkable class of correlated designs,
  14| p ≤ n^A (A > 1 allowed), masking allowed, of the form "on 𝒟(...), P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) → 0", with LH, W, LH-iid as
  15| instances. Starting point, M5(0) (SoP `04_theory.tex:464-539`, T38-(0) "PROVED (SF: VERIFIED (W3-VT38E); XF:
  16| VERIFIED* (A-REV5))"), at every n and any X:
  17| 
  18|   P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] + D_n,   D_n := P(𝒪̄ ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝒮̄⁺})  (potential-run notation).     (M5-0)
  19| 
  20| S-T (TH09, T03♯) gives 1 − π(S₀) → 0 in probability, hence E₀[1 − π(S₀)] → 0 (bounded convergence). **The new
  21| content: a general design class on which D_n → 0.** This is a sufficient class, substantially narrower than "any
  22| correlated design" (CE169; non-identifiable designs; see §4).
  23| 
  24| ## 1. Setting
  25| 
  26| * **D0** as in SoP `04_theory.tex:69-74`: shipped g = n score, a₀ = b₀ = 0.01, normalized capped BB(1,p) prior,
  27|   K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋), Ω = {S : |S| ≤ K}, tables r_b(U) = m(U)/m(∅), start γ₀ ∝ w(|S|)∏_b r_b(S ∩ C_b) on Ω, π₀,
  28|   start mode S̃₀ = argmax_Ω γ₀ with the size-then-lex tie rule.
  29| * **G**: fixed raw design X^r (n × p, nonconstant columns), y^r = α1 + X^rβ + ε, ε ~ N_n(0, σ²I), σ² > 0 fixed;
  30|   X = CX^rD_x⁻¹ (‖x_j‖² = n − 1), μ := CX^rβ = Xθ*, θ* := D_xβ, S₀ := supp β, s₀ := |S₀| ≥ 1 fixed, p = p_n ≤ n^A
  31|   (A ≥ 1 fixed; p ≫ n allowed).
  32| * **Notation.** P_T: projection on span X_T; Λ_T := ‖(I − P_T)μ‖²; Δ_T := Λ_T/(n − 1); v_T := σ² + Δ_T;
  33|   R̂_T := X_TᵀX_T/(n − 1); θ*_min := min_{j∈S₀}|θ*_j|. For a pair (T, l), l ∉ T, **only on the families named below,
  34|   where the relevant SE guarantees (I − P_T)x_l ≠ 0**: u_{T,l} := (I − P_T)x_l/‖(I − P_T)x_l‖, δ_{T,l} := u_{T,l}ᵀμ,
  35|   so that Λ_T − Λ_{T∪{l}} = δ²_{T,l}. For T with λ_min(R̂_{T∪{l}}) = 0 we use the projection form
  36|   Λ_T − Λ_{T∪{l}} (always defined).
  37| * **Blocks** C₁, …, C_J: the method's actual partition (complete linkage on 1 − |r̂|, top-down cut at B, next-fit
  38|   packing; B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16)), SoP `02_method.tex:187-211`; under G a deterministic function of X.
  39| * **Method:** v3.1 with LS0 as specified (SoP `02_method.tex:490-506`); local search M §6.10 (SoP `02_method.tex:463-467`);
  40|   cap ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n + p + 1)⌉. A *move* is a strict improvement to the best scanned neighbour (lexicographic ties);
  41|   every scanned neighbour is scored; after ℓ moves one further scan; the LS0 centre is emitted (scored).
  42| * **Implementation premises** (named, not proved here; M5's list, SoP `04_theory.tex:86`): EX-A, EX-S, CAL, SR,
  43|   GUARD-W, OP-LS0, **e4** (emitted LS0 centre = the prescribed start-mode maximiser; DP invariant N3 OPEN, owned by
  44|   W1-N3), complete scans; for R′ > 4 also IND-T and the extra search from c₄ (nested scored set).
  45| 
  46| ## 2. Hypotheses
  47| 
  48| **(H0) = the hypotheses of S-T/T03♯** (SoP `04_theory.tex` TH09 card, from NBH TLF:448-451), written out:
  49| * R1: fixed s₀ ≥ 1, p ≤ n^A, s₀ ≤ K eventually; G;
  50| * R: ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn for a fixed M; λ_min(R̂_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀² for a fixed φ₀ > 0;
  51| * SE_λ(j₀), j₀ := ⌈(2A + 1)s₀⌉ + 1: λ_min(R̂_{S₀∪J}) ≥ φ₀² for every J with |J| ≤ j₀ (normalized);
  52| * SE_w(m♯_n; g₀): λ_min(X_{S₀∪J}ᵀX_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g₀ for every |J| ≤ m♯_n (unnormalized; fixed g₀ > 0), where
  53|   m♯_n := min{m ≥ s₀ : R_m ≤ n^{−(s₀+2)/2}}, R_m := Σ_{k=max(m+1,0)}^{K} C(p,k) w(k)/w(s₀) (deterministic, data-free);
  54| * BM-∞: θ*²_min n φ₀²/(σ² log n) → ∞. (BM(c > c₀) is not used.)
  55| 
  56| **(H1) Bounded, separated relevance set (descent).** Deterministic sets 𝒱_n ⊇ S₀ with |𝒱_n| ≤ v̄ (fixed) such that
  57| * (H1a) SE on 𝒱: λ_min(R̂_{𝒱∪{l}}) ≥ φ₀² for every l ∈ [p];
  58| * (H1b) SEP(c_S): ζ_n := max{Λ_S − Λ_{S∪{l}} : S ⊆ 𝒱, l ∉ 𝒱} ≤ c_S (n − 1) φ₀⁴ θ*²_min eventually, for a fixed
  59|   c_S ∈ [0, 1). Convention: ζ_n := 0 if 𝒱 = [p].
  60|   Variables outside 𝒱 may be correlated among themselves (subject only to (H0)'s anchored sparse-eigenvalue
  61|   conditions and (H2a)); they only must not carry, given any subset of
  62|   𝒱, more partial signal than the fixed fraction c_S of the guaranteed best-truth decrement (n − 1)φ₀⁴θ*²_min.
  63| 
  64| **(H2) Centre (on the actual blocks).** A deterministic reference S* ⊆ 𝒱 (S* ∈ Ω, s* := |S*| ≤ v̄,
  65| U*_b := S* ∩ C_b) such that
  66| * (H2a) within-block SE: λ_min(R̂_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T ⊆ C_b, every b;
  67| * (H2b) VIS(S*): for a deterministic M_n → ∞, g_{b,U} := ‖(P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)μ‖² ≥ M_n v_U log n for every b and every
  68|   U ⊆ C_b with U*_b ⊄ U;
  69| * (H2c) NL(S*): with the leakage family 𝓛(S*) := {(b, T, l) : l ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b, U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}},
  70|   (i) δ²_{T,l} ≤ C_L σ² log n on 𝓛(S*) for a fixed C_L < ∞, and
  71|   (ii) NL_avg(κ) for a fixed κ > 0: if p > s*, eventually
  72|   (p − s*)⁻¹ Σ_{l∉S*} max_{T:(b(l),T,l)∈𝓛(S*)} exp(E_{T,l}) ≤ n^{1/2−κ}, where, for a fixed ε₀ > 0 and
  73|   h_n := √(2(A + ε₀) log n), E_{T,l} := min{δ²_{T,l}/(2Δ_T), δ²_{T,l}/(2v_T) + |δ_{T,l}|σh_n/v_T}, with E_{T,l} := 0
  74|   when δ_{T,l} = 0 (in particular when Δ_T = 0); the average is omitted when p = s*.
  75|   (NL_η(S*): δ²_{T,l} ≤ ησ² log n on 𝓛(S*) with 0 ≤ η < (√(2A+1) − √(2A))², implies (i) and (ii), as in T22iii §2.)
  76| 
  77| S* is an **existential certificate** depending on (X, β, σ², partition): it is not required to be the exact minimiser
  78| of Λ in each block (exact minimisers can contain nulls with negligible gain and violate VIS; R01 item 2). Masking is
  79| allowed: true variables with no block-level signal given U*_b are omitted from S* (they lie in 𝓛(S*)), and S* may
  80| contain nulls (block-level proxies).
  81| 
  82| ## 3. Claims
  83| 
  84| **(C1) Centre law (generalized T22(iii)).** [G, R (bounded energy only), p ≤ n^A, (H2), s* ≤ v̄]: 1 − π₀(S*) → 0 in
  85| probability; on {π₀(S*) > ½} the maximiser of γ₀ is unique, so S̃₀ = S*; hence P(S̃₀ = S*) → 1. The proof re-runs
  86| the locked T22(iii) argument (reference S₀) with reference S*, with (H2c) in place of NL_η, and with EXP′ **proved**
  87| (uniform score expansion, L1) instead of assumed.
  88| 
  89| **(C1′) Canonical certificate (added after R05, v2.2; sufficient condition for (H2b)–(H2c), no hypothesis changed).**
  90| Under (H2a), let γ_b be the coefficients of the projection of μ on span X_{C_b} (the regression of μ on the block's own
  91| columns). Assume also ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn. If every γ_b = γ^L_b + γ^S_b (disjoint supports) with, for a fixed
  92| η ∈ [0, (√(2A+1) − √(2A))²) and some M_n → ∞, (i) ‖X_{C_b}γ^S_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n and (ii)
  93| √((n − 1)φ₀²)·min_{j∈supp γ^L_b}|γ^L_{b,j}| ≥ √(ησ² log n) + √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) whenever supp γ^L_b ≠ ∅,
  94| then S* := ∪_b supp γ^L_b

   1| # L2 — Centre law with a general reference S* (generalized T22(iii)); claim (C1)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R03 (Codex Sol): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS, amendments
   4| applied (v2, reviews/R02_R04_disposition.md).
   5| Inputs: T22(i) "PROVED-LOCKED" (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T22_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md` §2(i): deterministic,
   6| any partition with |C_b| ≤ B ≤ K, positive tables, **any feasible reference S°**); the proof text of T22(iii)
   7| (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/PROOF_v2.tex`, "PROVED-LOCKED CONDITIONAL", reference S₀, EXP′
   8| assumed), cited below as [P:line]; L1 of this folder.
   9| 
  10| ## Statement
  11| 
  12| **Theorem L2.** Assume G; ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn; p ≤ n^A; and (H2) with a deterministic reference S* ∈ Ω, s* = |S*| ≤ v̄ fixed,
  13| s* ≤ K eventually. Let U*_b := S* ∩ C_b and, for p > s*,
  14| 
  15|   u_n := (p − s*)⁻¹ Σ_{l∉S*} max_{T : (b(l),T,l)∈𝓛(S*)} r_{b(l)}(T ∪ {l})/r_{b(l)}(T),
  16|   e_n := 2p max_{b, U⊆C_b : a := |U*_b∖U| > 0} [r_b(U)/r_b(U ∪ U*_b)]^{1/a}
  17| 
  18| (u_n := 0 if p = s*; e_n := 0 on an empty index set). Then with a_n := 2^B √(log n) n^{−κ}:
  19| u_n = O_P(a_n), e_n = o_P(n^{−m}) for every fixed m > 0, and 1 − π₀(S*) = O_P(a_n) → 0. On {π₀(S*) > ½} the
  20| maximiser of γ₀ over Ω is unique and equals S*; hence P(S̃₀ = S*) → 1, whatever the tie rule.
  21| 
  22| ## Proof (substitution list against [P])
  23| 
  24| The proof of [P] uses the truth S₀ only (i) as the reference defining U*_b, the leakage family, u_n, q_n, e_n, and
  25| (ii) through "s₀ fixed, eventually feasible". It never uses μ ∈ span X_{S₀}, nor that leakage indices are nulls, nor
  26| that missing reference variables are true: residual control uses only ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn ([P:149-203]); the leakage integral
  27| allows any δ_{T,l} ([P:249-280]); completion uses VIS only ([P:334-401]). We re-run it with S* in place of S₀:
  28| 
  29| 1. **Setting [P:35-131].** Replace U*_b = S₀ ∩ C_b by U*_b = S* ∩ C_b; 𝓛 := 𝓛(S*) = {(b,T,l) : l ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b,
  30|    U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}} (note: [P:85] writes l ∉ S₀; here l ∉ S*, which may include true variables — masked truths);
  31|    averages over l ∉ S* with denominator p − s*; VIS (H2b) and E_{T,l}, NL_avg(κ) (H2c)(ii) as in STATEMENT §2.
  32|    The directions u_{T,l} exist for every within-block addition by (H2a) ([P:48-64]).
  33| 2. **EXP′ is proved, not assumed.** Apply L1 to 𝔉_blk := {T : T ⊆ C_b for some b}: |𝔉_blk| ≤ p2^B ≤ 2^{16}n^A
  34|    (fixed J = 16 ≥ B_n, C_F = 2^{16}, D = A, C_V = 2·2^{32}, D_V = 2A), Gram floor by (H2a), 𝒱𝒱 := {r_T} ∪ {r_T − r_{T′}} over 𝔉_blk. L1.3 gives, on 𝒟₁ ∩ 𝒟₂ ∩ 𝒟₃
  35|    (probability → 1) and n ≥ n₀, for every within-block addition (b, T, l):
  36|    log[r_b(T ∪ {l})/r_b(T)] = −½ log(n + 1) − ν log(1 − x_{T,l}) + R_{n,b,T,l}, |R_{n,b,T,l}| ≤ 2κ_E.
  37|    With the remainder defined on the whole space as in L1.3 (R := log[r_b(T+l)/r_b(T)] + ½log(n+1) + ν log(1 − x_{T,l}),
  38|    finite a.s. for n large), ρ_n := max|R| satisfies P(ρ_n > 2κ_E) → 0, so ρ_n = O_P(1): the strict version of
  39|    [P]'s EXP′ ([P:73-80]) holds; the score identity holds a.s. by definition, also off the event.
  40| 3. **Lemma residual [P:149-203]** holds verbatim (it uses only ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn, |𝒯| ≤ p2^B and Gaussian tails).
  41| 4. **Lemma quad [P:205-245]** with NL_C in place of NL_η: on ℋ_n := {max_𝓛 |Z_{T,l}| ≤ h_n} (probability ≥ 1 −
  42|    2^{17}n^{−ε₀}, [P:220-226]), (H2c)(i) gives max_𝓛 (δ_{T,l} + σZ_{T,l})² ≤ σ²(√C_L + √(2(A + ε₀)))² log n; with
  43|    Lemma residual this gives max_𝓛 x_{T,l} = O_P(log n/n), max n x² = o_P(1), and d_n = o_P(1), exactly as in [P:226-243]
  44|    (only "O(log n)" of the numerator was used there; its constant is irrelevant).
  45| 5. **Lemma integral [P:249-280]** is a statement about a single Gaussian and is unchanged.
  46| 6. **Proposition u_n [P:282-329]** holds verbatim with the sums over l ∉ S*, denominator p − s*, and the average
  47|    bound (H2c)(ii) in place of [P]'s (eq:avg); at most 2^B terms per l; Markov; the product bound
  48|    u_n ≤ (n + 1)^{−1/2}exp(ρ_n + d_n)V_n on ℋ_n uses EXP′ (step 2) and step 4. Result: u_n = O_P(a_n).
  49| 7. **Proposition e_n [P:334-401]** with VIS(S*): for (b, U) with a = |U*_b ∖ U| > 0, P := P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U is a
  50|    deterministic projection of rank a (nested subspaces; rank a by (H2a)), 1 ≤ a ≤ B. The telescoping along a fixed
  51|    ordering of the a missing **reference** variables uses EXP′ (step 2); ‖Pμ‖² = g_{b,U} ≥ M_n v_U log n by (H2b);
  52|    [P:368-399] then gives e_n ≤ 2n^A(n + 1)^{1/2}e^{ρ_n}n^{−cM_n/16} on an event of probability → 1, with
  53|    c = σ²/(8C_R), so e_n = o_P(n^{−m}) for every m. (The words "missing true variables" at [P:362] read "missing reference variables" here.)
  54| 8. **Aggregation [P:427-468].** T22(i) with the feasible reference S* (locked; any feasible reference): q_n ≤ u_n and,
  55|    on {u_n < 1}, 1 − π₀(S*) ≤ (s* + 1)u_n/(1 − u_n) + s*e_n. On {u_n ≤ ½}: 1 − π₀(S*) ≤ 2(s* + 1)u_n + s*e_n.
  56|    With s* ≤ v̄ fixed, steps 6–7 give 1 − π₀(S*) = O_P(a_n + e_n) = O_P(a_n) → 0.
  57| 9. **Uniqueness of the mode.** On {π₀(S*) > ½}: every S ∈ Ω ∖ {S*} has π₀(S) ≤ 1 − π₀(S*) < ½ < π₀(S*), i.e.
  58|    γ₀(S) < γ₀(S*). So S* is the unique maximiser of γ₀; any tie rule returns it; under premise e4 the emitted LS0
  59|    centre is S*. Hence P(S̃₀ = S*) ≥ P(π₀(S*) > ½) → 1. ∎
  60| 
  61| **What changed relative to [P], in one list.** Reference S₀ → S*; leakage indices l ∉ S* (may be true variables);
  62| NL_η → (NL_C, NL_avg(κ)) (NL_η implies both for admissible κ and sufficiently small ε₀, [P:404-425]); EXP′ assumed → proved (L1, needs (H2a) and bounded energy);
  63| "s₀ fixed" → "s* ≤ v̄". Nothing else.
  64| 
  65| **Remark (masking).** A masked truth j ∈ C_b ∖ U*_b is a leakage index: (H2c)(i) asks δ²_{T,j} ≤ C_Lσ² log n for
  66| U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {j} — at most O(log n) squared partial signal on the leakage family (exact masking, δ = 0, is the
  67| special case η = 0) — while posterior consistency (H0) and the descent
  68| (L3) still recover it. This is the masked regime of M3(f)/M5 in general form.

   1| # L4 — What the production local search does on the event of L3 (deterministic part of (C2))
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R04 (Codex Sol): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS, amendments
   4| applied (v2). Deterministic, from the search semantics M §6.10
   5| (SoP `02_method.tex:463-467`; LS0: SoP `02_method.tex:490-499`).
   6| 
   7| **Search semantics used (verbatim content of M §6.10, as restated in SoP 02_method.tex:463-467).** From a centre:
   8| scan every feasible flip and swap (additions beyond K excluded), the centre frozen during the scan; every scanned model
   9| is scored; if the best scanned score strictly exceeds the centre's, move there (exact ties among scanned models: the
  10| lexicographically smallest index set) and count one move; at most ℓ moves, then one further scan; stop earlier at the
  11| first scan with no strict improvement (`local_certified`: the returned model is a scanned centre with no improving
  12| neighbour); if the last scan still improves, set `local_limit`. For LS0 the centre is the start mode S̃₀, emitted
  13| (scored) (SoP `02_method.tex:490-494`; premise OP-LS0).
  14| 
  15| The **uncapped greedy path** from C is the sequence C = S⁰, S¹, … where S^{t+1} is the scan-maximiser at S^t (tie rule
  16| as above) if it strictly improves F(S^t), and the path stops otherwise. τ(C) := min{t : S^t = S₀} (∞ if never).
  17| 
  18| **Lemma L4.1.** Suppose the conclusion of Corollary L3.4 holds (for the data at hand) and |𝒱| ≤ min(v̄, K) (if S misses
  19| a truth then |S| ≤ |𝒱| − 1, so the designated truth addition is feasible; extra deletions are always feasible; swaps
  20| preserve size).
  21| Then for every centre C ⊆ 𝒱:
  22| (i) every state S^t of the uncapped path lies in 2^𝒱, F(S⁰) < F(S¹) < …, and τ(C) ≤ 2^{v̄} − 1;
  23| (ii) the uncapped path stops at S₀ (no strict improvement there);
  24| (iii) the capped production search from C performs exactly the scans and moves of the uncapped path up to its cap; it
  25| scores S₀ if ℓ ≥ τ(C) − 1 (if τ(C) = 0, S₀ = C is the emitted centre); and if ℓ ≥ τ(C) the **search endpoint** is
  26| S₀, its completed scan finds no strict improvement (the search certifies its endpoint), and the search does not end at
  27| `local_limit`. (The public flag `local_certified` is evaluated on the finally returned HPM, SoP 02_method.tex:505-506;
  28| it refers to S₀ only when the reported Ŝ⁺ equals this endpoint, e.g. on {π(S₀) > ½}. Not needed for D_n.)
  29| 
  30| *Proof.* (i) Induction: S⁰ = C ⊆ 𝒱. If S^t ⊆ 𝒱 and S^t ≠ S₀, Corollary L3.4 says every maximiser of F over the
  31| feasible neighbours lies in 𝒱 and strictly exceeds F(S^t); the tie rule selects one of these maximisers, so S^{t+1}
  32| exists, S^{t+1} ⊆ 𝒱 and F(S^{t+1}) > F(S^t). Strict monotonicity makes the states pairwise distinct; they lie in
  33| 2^𝒱, which has at most 2^{v̄} elements; the path cannot stop at a state ≠ S₀ (each such state has a strict
  34| improvement) and cannot have more than 2^{v̄} distinct states, so it reaches S₀ after τ(C) ≤ 2^{v̄} − 1 moves.
  35| (ii) By Corollary L3.4, S₀ has no feasible neighbour with F ≥ F(S₀), so the path stops there.
  36| (iii) The capped search and the uncapped path make identical decisions while the move count is below ℓ (same
  37| centres, same scans, same tie rule); the cap only truncates. S₀ = S^{τ} is a scanned neighbour of S^{τ−1}, hence scored
  38| in the scan at S^{τ−1}. That scan is performed iff τ − 1 < ℓ (inside the loop) or τ − 1 = ℓ (the one further scan
  39| after ℓ moves). If ℓ ≥ τ, the τ-th move is made, the centre is S₀, and the next scan (inside the loop if τ < ℓ, else
  40| the final scan) finds no strict improvement by (ii): the search stops with S₀ a scanned centre without improving
  41| neighbour (endpoint certified), and `local_limit` is not set. ∎
  42| 
  43| **Remarks.** (1) Only *centres* stay in 2^𝒱; scanned neighbours outside 𝒱 are scored (and enter the all-scored set),
  44| which is harmless. (2) The bound 2^{v̄} − 1 is crude. A sharper count on LH (Φ(S*) = c moves) needs the separate LH lattice argument
  45| (BS/W4-T38FULL/T38_PROOF.md:217-269, LH-LAT; its own status) and is not claimed here.
  46| (3) Exact ties: the argument holds for any selection among maximisers, because all maximisers lie in 𝒱.
  47| (4) Nothing about the HPM centre of the original final local search is claimed (Lemma 0(b) of W1-T37R: that search
  48| cannot move to S₀ unless F(S₀) exceeds every pre-search score).

   1| # L8 — A canonical, checkable certificate for (H2): block projection coefficients
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**. Added after the mid-point review R05 (item 4: "give one worked
   4| non-LH/non-W certificate"; item 2 of the statement lock R01: the exact Λ-minimiser is not a valid certificate in
   5| general). This is a sufficient condition for (H2b)–(H2c); it changes no hypothesis of STATEMENT.md.
   6| 
   7| Setting: fixed design, notation of STATEMENT §1, (H2a) on the actual blocks, and bounded energy ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn with the
   8| same fixed M used in the thresholds below (sweep R10 item 1). Minima over empty supports are +∞ (conditions on blocks
   9| with empty support are vacuous). The certificate supplies (H2b)–(H2c) only; using it in Theorem GEN still requires
  10| S* ⊆ 𝒱, s* ≤ v̄, feasibility and the relevance-set hypothesis (H1) (or S* = S₀). For each block b, since X_{C_b} has full
  11| column rank, the block projection of μ has unique coefficients
  12| 
  13|   P_{C_b}μ = X_{C_b}γ_b,   γ_b ∈ ℝ^{C_b}   (γ_b = G_{C_b}⁻¹X_{C_b}ᵀμ: the regression of μ on the block alone).
  14| 
  15| ## L8.1 Exact certificate
  16| 
  17| **Lemma L8.1.** Let U*_b := supp(γ_b) and S*_can := ∪_b U*_b. Then:
  18| (a) the minimisers of U ↦ Λ_U over U ⊆ C_b are exactly the sets U ⊇ U*_b (so U*_b is the unique ⊆-minimal one);
  19| (b) every leakage residual vanishes: δ_{T,l} = 0 for all (b, T, l) ∈ 𝓛(S*_can) (NL_η with η = 0);
  20| (c) for U ⊆ C_b with U*_b ⊄ U and M := U*_b ∖ U: g_{b,U} ≥ (n − 1)φ₀²‖γ_{b,M}‖² ≥ (n − 1)φ₀² min_{j∈U*_b} γ²_{b,j}.
  21| Hence (H2b) holds for S*_can as soon as the **block beta-min** condition holds:
  22| 
  23|   (n − 1)φ₀² min_{b} min_{j∈supp γ_b} γ²_{b,j} ≥ M_n (σ² + 2M) log n,  M_n → ∞   (empty minima = +∞).      (BBM)
  24| 
  25| *Proof.* For U ⊆ C_b, Λ_U = ‖μ‖² − ‖P_Uμ‖² and ‖P_Uμ‖² = ‖P_U P_{C_b}μ‖² ≤ ‖P_{C_b}μ‖², with equality iff
  26| P_{C_b}μ ∈ span X_U. As X_{C_b} has independent columns, X_{C_b}γ_b ∈ span X_U iff supp(γ_b) ⊆ U. This is (a).
  27| (b) If U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}, then P_{C_b}μ = X_{U*_b}γ_{b,U*_b} ∈ span X_T, and u_{T,l} ∈ span X_{T∪{l}} ⊆ span X_{C_b}
  28| with u_{T,l} ⊥ span X_T; so δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀμ = u_{T,l}ᵀP_{C_b}μ = 0. (c) U ∪ U*_b ⊆ C_b contains supp γ_b, so
  29| P_{U∪U*_b}μ = P_{C_b}μ and (P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)μ = (I − P_U)P_{C_b}μ = (I − P_U)X_Mγ_{b,M} (the columns in U*_b ∩ U are
  30| annihilated). Its squared norm is γ_{b,M}ᵀ[X_Mᵀ(I − P_U)X_M]γ_{b,M}, and the bracket is the Schur complement of G_U in
  31| G_{U∪M}, with λ_min ≥ (n − 1)φ₀² by (H2a). Finally v_U ≤ σ² + ‖μ‖²/(n − 1) ≤ σ² + Mn/(n − 1) ≤ σ² + 2M for n ≥ 2, so g_{b,U} ≥ M_n v_U log n. ∎
  32| 
  33| ## L8.2 Thresholded certificate (near-zero coefficients)
  34| 
  35| **Lemma L8.2.** Suppose each γ_b splits as γ_b = γ^L_b + γ^S_b with disjoint supports, and for fixed
  36| 0 ≤ η < (√(2A + 1) − √(2A))² and some M_n → ∞:
  37|   (i) ‖X_{C_b}γ^S_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n for every b;
  38|   (ii) √((n − 1)φ₀²) min_{j∈supp γ^L_b}|γ^L_{b,j}| ≥ √(ησ² log n) + √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) for every b with
  39|        supp γ^L_b ≠ ∅.
  40| Then S* := ∪_b supp(γ^L_b) satisfies (H2b) and NL_η(S*), hence (H2c).
  41| 
  42| *Proof.* Put U*_b := supp γ^L_b and write P_{C_b}μ = X_{U*_b}γ^L_{b,U*_b} + s_b, s_b := X_{C_b}γ^S_b. For U ⊆ C_b,
  43| projections of μ onto subspaces of span X_{C_b} equal those of P_{C_b}μ. VIS: (P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)X_{U*_b}γ^L =
  44| (I − P_U)X_Mγ^L_M with norm ≥ √((n − 1)φ₀²)‖γ^L_M‖ (L8.1(c)), and ‖(P_{U∪U*_b} − P_U)s_b‖ ≤ ‖s_b‖ ≤ √(ησ² log n);
  45| so √g_{b,U} ≥ √((n − 1)φ₀²)‖γ^L_M‖ − √(ησ² log n) ≥ √(M_n(σ² + 2M) log n) ≥ √(M_n v_U log n) (n ≥ 2). Leakage: for
  46| U*_b ⊆ T ⊆ C_b ∖ {l}, u_{T,l} ⊥ X_{U*_b}, so δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀs_b and δ²_{T,l} ≤ ‖s_b‖² ≤ ησ² log n. ∎
  47| 
  48| ## L8.3 Reading and examples
  49| 
  50| * **Interpretation.** (BBM) is a beta-min condition on the **block-level regression coefficients** of the mean on each
  51|   block's own columns (with the response's full signal, as the tables see it). A true variable is *masked* exactly
  52|   when its block coefficient vanishes (or is negligible, L8.2); a null enters S* exactly when it carries a non-
  53|   negligible block coefficient (a block-level proxy). This is the block analogue of the marginal-correlation condition
  54|   that Song–Liang's Condition 5 imposes globally: here it is imposed per block, and violations (masking) are allowed
  55|   and repaired by the descent (L3) instead of being excluded.
  56| * **Checkability.** Given (X, β, σ², actual partition): one least-squares solve per block (B ≤ 16 columns), then
  57|   (BBM)/(L8.2) are explicit inequalities. For iid designs the population version uses Σ_{C_bC_b}⁻¹Σ_{C_b,·}θ.
  58| * **LH (exact Gram).** γ for an a-group = β_i(1 − ψ_i²)e_{a_i} (only the hub; L6(a)), b-groups γ = 0 (masked), visible
  59|   groups γ = θ_he_h, null groups γ = 0: S*_can = S₀ ∖ M, (BBM) with fixed coefficients. Recovers L6(a)'s (H2).
  60| * **W.** In a signal group C ∋ j₁, P_Cμ = θx_{j₁} + θP_Cx_{j₂}; take γ^L := γ_{j₁}e_{j₁} (the actual coefficient on the
  61|   active coordinate, θ(1 + O(ε_n))) and γ^S := the coefficients on the other coordinates. The off-active part of P_Cμ is
  62|   part of θP_Cx_{j₂}: writing P_Cx_{j₂} = c x_{j₁} + X_{C∖j₁}γ′, X_Cγ^S = θX_{C∖j₁}γ′ = θ(P_Cx_{j₂} − c x_{j₁}), so
  63|   ‖X_Cγ^S‖ ≤ θ(‖P_Cx_{j₂}‖ + |c|√(n − 1)) with ‖P_Cx_{j₂}‖² ≤ (n − 1)·9ε_n²·(4/3) and |c| ≤ (4/3)·3ε_n (λ_min(Σ_C) = ¾,
  64|   ‖Σ_{C,j₂}‖ = 3ε_n); hence ‖X_Cγ^S‖² = O(nθ²ε_n²) → 0;
  65|   null groups: γ^L = 0, ‖X_Cγ^S‖² = ‖P_Cμ‖² = O(nθ²ε_n²). So L8.2(i) holds for any η > 0 eventually. Recovers L6(c).
  66| * **A worked non-LH, non-W instance ("finite-core designs").** Exact Gram; a core 𝒦 of fixed size k̄ ≥ s₀ containing
  67|   S₀ with an arbitrary fixed correlation matrix Σ_𝒦 (λ_min(Σ_𝒦) ≥ φ₀²) and fixed θ; all remaining columns orthogonal to
  68|   𝒦 (arbitrary correlations among themselves, subject to (H0)'s anchored sparse-eigenvalue conditions and (H2a)).
  69|   Then: (H1) holds with 𝒱 := 𝒦, ζ_n = 0 (outside columns are orthogonal to μ and to 𝒦); for any actual partition,
  70|   a block's γ_b is the regression of μ on (C_b ∩ 𝒦) (outside columns in the block get coefficient 0), a fixed
  71|   function of Σ_𝒦, θ and the core's block pattern; if every nonzero entry of every such γ_b is nonzero in the limit
  72|   (generic in (Σ_𝒦, θ)), (BBM) holds with M_n ≍ n/log n and L8.1 gives (H2) with S* = S*_can ⊆ 𝒦. So (C3) holds, with
  73|   masking whenever some truth has zero coefficient in its core block. Example: 𝒦 = {1, 2, 3}, Σ_𝒦 with r₁₂ = r, r₁₃ =
  74|   r₂₃ = 0 (0 < |r| < 1), θ = (1, −r, 0), so μ = x₁ − rx₂ and S₀ = {1, 2}. If 1 and 2 lie in different blocks, the
  75|   block of 2 has γ = 0 on x₂ (Cov(x₂, μ) = r − r = 0, and its other members are orthogonal to μ): x₂ is masked, while
  76|   the block of 1 has γ = (1 − r²)e₁; S*_can = {1}, and the descent adds x₂ (one move). If 1 and 2 share a block,
  77|   γ = (1, −r) on them: no masking, S*_can = S₀. Both cases are covered.

   1| # Corollary E (clause M1(e)): islandwise accuracy of every bounded summary
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED under the named premises of STATEMENT §2 — cross-family checked (Codex gpt-6.1-sol: LC1, MP1 CONTINUE, SW1, council C1 9.3) and council-passed (Claude Opus 5.5: C1 8.9), round 1, 2026-11-08. Inherits the premise statuses START/KERNEL (N9: PROVED (candidate), code-checked; CHK_INHERITED: VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT) and T12 (PROVED-LOCKED). Given Theorem N1. v3; history: v2, 2026-11-08 (v1 → v2: localised form; numerics citation; LC1 issues 4–5). Statement: STATEMENT.md v2 §4 (locked).
   4| 
   5| ## Statement
   6| 
   7| Premises of Theorem N1. Let S₀ ⊆ [p] be fixed, δ₁ := 1 − π(S₀) (π(S₀) := 0 if |S₀| > K), and let h be as in STATEMENT §1
   8| with values in [0, 1], defined on Ω ∪ {S₀} (jointly measurable in (S, c)). Then a.s. on 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}, with W_r = Ẑ_r/Z,
   9| 
  10|   E[W_r · |H_r(h) − h(S₀; 𝓒)| | 𝓒] ≤ E[W_r · H_r(1{S ≠ S₀}) | 𝓒] = δ₁ ≤ 2δ₁.
  11| 
  12| ## Proof
  13| 
  14| Pointwise: for S ∈ Ω and c, h(S; c), h(S₀; c) ∈ [0, 1], so |h(S; c) − h(S₀; c)| ≤ 1 if S ≠ S₀ and = 0 if S = S₀; i.e.
  15| |h(S; c) − h(S₀; c)| ≤ 1{S ≠ S₀}. Averaging over the 4N_e endpoints (triangle inequality),
  16| |H_r(h) − h(S₀; 𝓒)| = |(4N_e)^{-1}Σ_{q,i}(h(S_{rqi}; 𝓒) − h(S₀; 𝓒))| ≤ (4N_e)^{-1}Σ_{q,i} 1{S_{rqi} ≠ S₀} = H_r(1{S ≠ S₀}).
  17| Multiply by 1_{E₀}W_r ≥ 0 (E₀ = 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}) and take E[· | 𝓒] (monotonicity of conditional expectation; on E₀ every
  18| integrand is bounded by Z₀e^{max d}/Z, as in Lemma F, and the localised integrands are zero off E₀). All statements are in
  19| the localised form of Lemma F. The function
  20| h₀(S) := 1{S ≠ S₀} on Ω (extended by h₀(S₀) := 0) is deterministic with values in [0, 1], so Theorem N1 gives E[W_r H_r(h₀) | 𝓒] = π(h₀) =
  21| Σ_{S∈Ω, S≠S₀} π(S) = 1 − π(S₀) = δ₁ (if S₀ ∉ Ω, h₀ ≡ 1 on Ω and π(h₀) = 1 = δ₁). Finally δ₁ ≤ 2δ₁. ∎
  22| 
  23| Remarks.
  24| - The card prints the constant 2δ₁ (`THEOREM_LIST_FINAL.md:111`); the plain measured-endpoint average satisfies the sharper
  25|   δ₁ (the NEW-SYNTH form for the plain average, `NBH/ID_REGISTRY.md` TH412 (a)). The factor 2 is not needed.
  26| - No posterior-concentration, design or regime assumption is used; δ₁ carries all the statistics. "Every regime and frozen
  27|   grid" (card) holds.
  28| - The bound is tight: equality for h = 1{S ≠ S₀}.
  29| 
  30| ## Numerical check
  31| 
  32| Equality part E[W H(1{S ≠ S₀})] = δ₁: exact enumeration (an instance of N1; `numerics/RESULTS.md` §3, h = "1{S!=S0}").

  29| `v3_blocks.h` identical; `v3_engine.h` differs only by the write-only plain-PIP lines (v2.2.1 `:39-40, 352, 359-361, 370-371`);

  34| 
  35| (B-a) **Structure.** Φ(c, u) is a realisation of T12's frozen island I(c) (T12 STATEMENT §2) with N = N_e, M = 4,

  44| 
  45| ## Proof
  46| 
  47| **(B-a) Control flow.** The final island is called with `init_states = nullptr` (`CODE/cpp/v3_core.cpp:471`), so each of
  48| the N_e particles is initialised by `draw_start`, i.e. `draw_pi0` (`v3_engine.h:290`, `:109`). `run_island` sets only
  49| `sch.grid` (`:268-273`), so `sch.adaptive = false` and T = grid.size() − 1 (`:281`). The stage loop (`:304-341`) does, for
  50| t = 1, …, T: φ_{t−1} = grid[t−1], φ_t = grid[t] (`:308-309`); log-weights lw_i = (φ_t − φ_{t−1})·d(S_i) of the current
  51| population (`:318`); inc_t = LSE(lw) − log N (`:319-320`), added to logZ (`:323`); ancestors a = resample(lw) (`:325`) and
  52| Pn[i] = P[a[i]] (`:327-328`); one `population_round` at φ_t (`:332`). There is no round before the first reweighting
  53| (flag unset). After the loop: L rounds at φ = 1 (`:344-346`), then 4 rounds at φ = 1 (`:353-357`, Hm = 4 from
  54| `measured_rounds = 4L`, `CODE/v3_run.R:87`). No resampling occurs after stage T. logZ starts at log m(∅) + log Z̄₀
  55| (`:300`; `D.logm0` = log m(∅), `st.logZbar0` = log Z̄₀ by START). Under EX-A, LSE(lw) − log N = log((1/N)Σ_i e^{Δ_t d(S_i)}),
  56| so Ẑ_r = e^{logZ} = m(∅)Z̄₀∏_t (1/N)Σ_i G_t(S_i^{(t−1)}) = T12's Ẑ_T with Z₀ = m(∅)Z̄₀ and G_t = e^{Δ_t d} (T12 STATEMENT §2).
  57| The d and γ_φ the code uses are T12's: `eval` sets lg0 = log ϖ(|S|) + Σ_b log r_b, d = (log m − log m(∅)) − Σ_b log r_b
  58| (`v3_engine.h:98`), `lgphi(φ) = lg0 + φ d` (`:14`), matching T12 STATEMENT §0. On the success set the grid starts at 0
  59| (`CODE/cpp/v3_calib.h:71`), increases strictly (`:90`, validated `:91-92`), and ends exactly at 1 (`:73` loop while u < 1, `:89` snap), so
  60| T ≥ 1 and q_{φ_T} = π; this is T12's grid hypothesis.
  61| 
  62| **(B-0) The statistical record is a function of (c, u).** Every quantity that feeds a state transition, a weight or log Ẑ
  63| is one of: the frozen c (grid, N_e, L), the fixed data (through `eval`'s log m(S), lg0, d), and uniforms read from u. The
  64| clock reads only set `seconds_*` and the guard argument; the guard is absent in the potential run. Scores: `eval`
  65| (`v3_engine.h:90-102`) takes log m(S) either from the scorer or from the cache; a cache hit requires equal hash **and** equal
  66| model (`v3_score.h:277`, helper `:271-272`), insertion stores the scorer's value for that model (`:283-290`), and an
  67| eviction (`:284`) only causes a later miss, i.e. a fresh scorer call. Under EX-A the scorer is a deterministic function of
  68| S, so the cache returns that value whatever its history (in particular whatever earlier islands left in it). The ledger
  69| only records events and never feeds a proposal or acceptance (`v3_engine.h:99-105`; `v3_ledger.h:105-114`). The RB
  70| accumulation `if (rb_on) rb_acc[j] += oj` (`:129`) writes `rb_acc` only; it neither changes the particle nor reads a
  71| uniform. Engine members that persist across steps and islands (one `Engine` serves all islands, `v3_core.cpp:435`) carry
  72| no information between steps: `tmpQ` is written before it is read in every step (in `step_gibbs` it is read only when
  73| `include != in`, which requires the branch `in || add_ok` that wrote it, `v3_engine.h:119-131`; the swaps and the
  74| independence step write it before reading it); `rb_acc` is reset before the measured rounds (`:351`); `scratch` is workspace
  75| for `st.comp`; `ms`, `ev` are bookkeeping. Hence Φ(c, u) is determined by (c, u) (the data being fixed).
  76| 
  77| **(B-b) Randomness.** Write F_k = σ(u₁, …, u_k). By (B-0) the record's variables are computed by reading uniforms one at a
  78| time through `vs->u(·)`; whether and how many uniforms an operation reads is decided by the values already read and by the
  79| fixed data and c. Hence the index τ at which any given operation (an initial draw, a resampling, a particle's round, an
  80| elementary step) starts is a stopping time of (F_k). Each operation reads a bounded number of uniforms: `draw_pi0`
  81| ≤ 1 + 2J (`v3_start.h:160, 163-170`); a resampling N_e; a particle's round at most
  82| κ_max := (m − 1) + p + 3(B + 1) + (2 + 2J) (order m − 1; Gibbs 1 each; uniform swap ≤ 3; B neighbour swaps ≤ 3 each;
  83| independence ≤ (1 + 2J) + 1). So τ < ∞. By the strong Markov property of an iid sequence, (u_{τ+1}, u_{τ+2}, …) is iid
  84| U[0,1) and independent of F_τ. Every statistical-record variable produced before the operation (states, weights, Ẑ so far,
  85| earlier orders and paths) is F_τ-measurable. Therefore, conditionally on F_τ, the operation acts on its F_τ-measurable
  86| inputs through fresh iid uniforms. Applying this to each operation:
  87| - (R1) Each initial `draw_pi0` call, given F_τ, has law π₀ by START (N9 Claim S: the sampler maps fresh iid uniforms to an
  88|   exact π₀ draw); the N_e draws are therefore iid π₀.
  89| - (R2) `resample` (`v3_engine.h:235-260`) reads N fresh uniforms u_i. With W_k the normalised cumulative weights
  90|   (W_{N−1} := 1), it returns the smallest k with W_k ≥ u_i for u_i > 0: `guide[b]` is the smallest k with W_k ≥ b/N (or N − 1)
  91|   (`:243-247`); with b = ⌊u_i N⌋ we have b/N ≤ u_i, so `guide[b]` ≤ k* := min{k : W_k ≥ u_i}; the forward loop (`:255`) stops
  92|   exactly at k* (all indices in [guide[b], k*) have W < u_i, and W_{k*} ≥ u_i), and the backward loop (`:256`) does not move
  93|   because W_{k*−1} < u_i. The event u_i = 0 has probability 0. Under EX-A, P(a_i = k | F_τ) = W_k − W_{k−1} = w_k/Σ_l w_l,
  94|   and the a_i are conditionally iid given F_τ (disjoint fresh uniforms). This is (R2).
  95| - (R3) `population_round` (`:216-219`) runs `one_round` for particles i = 1, …, N_e in turn. The entering states are fixed
  96|   before the round. Particle i's round starts at a stopping time τ_i; its order is drawn from m − 1 fresh uniforms by
  97|   Fisher–Yates (`:196-201`): the choices ⌊u·(i + 1)⌋ are independent and uniform on {0, …, i}, so each of the m! choice
  98|   vectors has probability 1/m!, and the map to permutations of the canonical label list is a bijection (N9 row 5); hence
  99|   σ_i is uniform and independent of F_{τ_i}. Each subsequent step reads fresh uniforms and, by
 100|   KERNEL (N9 rows 1–4; T12 STATEMENT §1), moves the particle's current state according to K_{σ_i(k)}, given everything
 101|   before it. Particle i's (order, path) depends on the past only through its entering state X̃^i. Let H be the σ-field of
 102|   everything before the round. By the chain rule over i = 1, …, N_e, the conditional law of the N_e pairs given H is the
 103|   product of the laws Q(X̃^i, ·), where Q(x, ·) is "σ uniform; path Markov from x with kernels K_{σ(1)}, …, K_{σ(m)}".
 104|   Here H := F_{τ_1}, the stream σ-field at the round's first uniform; σ(record before the round) ⊆ H, and T12's statements
 105|   for that smaller σ-field follow by the tower property. Explicitly: for bounded f_i of (order, path), conditioning on
 106|   F_{τ_i} (which contains H and particles 1..i−1's pairs)
 107|   gives E[f_i(σ_i, path_i) | F_{τ_i}] = (Q f_i)(X̃^i), and iterated conditioning gives E[∏_i f_i | H] = ∏_i (Q f_i)(X̃^i).
 108|   This is (R3). The labels are p Gibbs labels, one U, B labels N (all calling the same `step_nswap`, whose argument b is used
 109|   only for a label string, `:163-165`), and one I; m = p + B + 2 (`:73`), as in T12 STATEMENT §1.
 110| 
 111|   Side effects that neither change states nor consume uniforms (B-0): the RB accumulation (writes `rb_acc` only),
 112|   `ev`/`ms` bookkeeping, `distinct`, the score cache, the ledger, the clock. They do not affect (R1)–(R3).
 113| 
 114| **(B-c) Endpoints.** In the measured loop (`:353-362`), `population_round(P, 1.0)` is called, then the counts are read from
 115| P (`:360`) before the next round. The populations read are therefore those after post-terminal operations L + 1, …, L + 4,
 116| all rounds at φ = 1, with no resampling in between. With the order of (B-a), this is T12's I(c) after its L′ = L burn-in
 117| rounds and its M = 4 measured rounds.
 118| 
 119| **(B-d) Measurability.** For fixed (T, N_e, L), by (B-0) and (B-b) the statistical record is computed by a finite program
 120| whose branches are comparisons of finitely many Borel functions of (grid values, data constants, u₁, …, u_k), with k bounded
 121| by a constant κ(T, N_e, L) (initial draws, T resamplings and T + L + 4 population rounds, each with the bounds of (B-b));
 122| hence it is a Borel function of (grid, u₁, …, u_κ) on each cell {T(c) = T, N_e(c) = N, L(c) = L}. These cells, with the
 123| complement of the success set (where Φ ≡ o†), form a countable measurable partition, so Φ is jointly measurable. Its values
 124| (finitely many reals and finite sequences of subsets of [p] and of permutations) lie in a countable disjoint union of
 125| Euclidean spaces times finite sets, a Polish space. (The calibration space E need not be Polish.) ∎
 126| 
 127| ## What this lemma uses and does not use
 128| 
 129| Uses: EX-A, H-U, START (N9 Claims S, Z), KERNEL (N9 rows 1–5, PROVED (candidate), code-checked; CHK_INHERITED VERIFIED WITH

  20|   K_φ = (1/m!)Σ_σ K_{σ(1)}⋯K_{σ(m)} satisfies q_φ K_φ = q_φ (`:54-81`; N9 rows 1–6 for the coded steps).
  21| - (resampling) under (R2), E[(1/N)Σ_l w^l · (1/N)Σ_i f(X^{A^i}) | 𝓕] = (1/N)Σ_k G(X^k) f(X^k) (`:100-106`).

  24| ## Statement

  29| ## Proof

  34| t − 1 → t: let 𝓕 be everything before the stage-t resampling; Ẑ_{t−1} and the population X^{(t−1)} are 𝓕-measurable. Let
  35| Y^i = X^{(t−1),A^i} be the resampled particles and 𝓗 ⊇ 𝓕 everything before the stage-t round. By (round),
  36| E[q̂_t(f) | 𝓗] = (1/N)Σ_i (K_{φ_t} f)(Y^i). Ẑ_t = Ẑ_{t−1}(1/N)Σ_l w^l is 𝓗-measurable, so
  37| E[Ẑ_t q̂_t(f) | 𝓕] = Ẑ_{t−1} E[(1/N)Σ_l w^l (1/N)Σ_i (K_{φ_t}f)(Y^i) | 𝓕] = Ẑ_{t−1} (1/N)Σ_k G_t(X^{(t−1),k})(K_{φ_t}f)(X^{(t−1),k})
  38| by (resampling) with G = G_t and the function K_{φ_t}f. This is Ẑ_{t−1} q̂_{t−1}(G_t·K_{φ_t}f). Taking expectations and using
  39| the induction hypothesis with the function G_t·K_{φ_t}f: E[Ẑ_t q̂_t(f)] = Z_{t−1}q_{t−1}(G_t K_{φ_t}f) = Z_t q_t(K_{φ_t}f) (bridge)
  40| = Z_t q_t(f) (invariance at φ_t).
  41| 
  42| (P-b): induction on s. s = 0 is (P-a) at t = T, since q_T = q_{φ_T} = q_{φ=1} = π (stage index T, temperature 1) and Z_T = Z. Step: the (s)-th post-terminal operation
  43| is a round at φ = 1 with no reweighting, so Ẑ is unchanged and 𝓗_s-measurable (𝓗_s = everything before that round); by
  44| (round), E[Ẑ q̂^{(s)}(f) | 𝓗_s] = Ẑ q̂^{(s−1)}(K_1 f); by the induction hypothesis with the function K_1 f,
  45| E[Ẑ q̂^{(s)}(f)] = Zπ(K_1 f) = Zπ(f) (invariance at φ = 1). ∎
  46| 
  47| Remark. Only full rounds occur between the measured endpoints, so κ ≡ m suffices; the within-round prefix identity
  48| (T12 (i.c)), which the Rao–Blackwellised record needs, is not used. No stationarity of the particles is claimed: the
  49| identity is for the evidence-weighted population (Ẑ inside the expectation).
  50| 
  51| ## Numerical falsification (numerics/RESULTS.md §2–§4)
  52| 
  53| Exact floating-point enumeration on production-extracted kernels, 10 designs (d0–d9), N = 1 on all designs and N = 2 on
  54| the six designs with |Ω| ≤ 130 (d2, d3, d5, d6, d7, d9), three grids (production, {0,1}, {0,½,1}) plus L = 0 stress cases,
  55| every basis indicator 1{S = s} and every measured round q separately: worst residual 9.3e-15 (RESULTS §3; tolerance 1e-10).
  56| Round kernels: row sums, q_φ-invariance and (|Ω| ≤ 130) detailed balance to ≤ 5.6e-16 (RESULTS §2). Negative controls
  57| NC1 (terminal rounds with the φ = ½ kernel) and NC2 (bridge stopped at φ_{T−1}, then the same rounds at φ = 1) give
  58| discrepancies from 3.2e-3 to 7.7e-1 (RESULTS §4).

   1| # Lemma F (conditioning on the frozen calibration, with calibration-dependent bounded h)
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED under the named premises of STATEMENT §2 — cross-family checked (Codex gpt-6.1-sol: LC1, MP1 CONTINUE, SW1, council C1 9.3) and council-passed (Claude Opus 5.5: C1 8.9), round 1, 2026-11-08.    4| `Docs/Theory/proofs/T12_T8_frozen_run_identities/PROOF_v6.tex:157-162`).
   5| 
   6| ## Setting
   7| 
   8| Fixed data. 𝓒 is a random element of a measurable space (E, 𝓔) with 𝒜 ∈ σ(𝓒) the success event (CAL: 𝓒 is a function of
   9| streams 0–9). For a fixed index r ≥ 1, U_r := final stream 9 + r, a random element of the sequence space
  10| (Υ, 𝓤) = ([0,1)^ℕ, Borel), iid U[0,1) coordinates (H-U), independent of streams 0–9 and hence of 𝓒 (premise SI).
  11| R′ is σ(𝓒)-measurable. Φ is the statistical record of Lemma B, extended by the dummy record o† off the success set, so it is
  12| defined and jointly measurable on all of E × Υ (MEAS, Lemma B (B-d)). On 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}, island r's statistical record is
  13| O_r = Φ(𝓒, U_r). **Localisation convention.** Island-r quantities (Ẑ_r, the endpoints S_{rqi}) are defined on
  14| E₀ := 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′} ∈ σ(𝓒); every identity about them is stated in the localised form E[1_{E₀}Y | 𝓒] = 1_{E₀}ψ(𝓒), with Y
  15| any extension (its value off E₀ is irrelevant, since 1_{E₀}Y is then defined globally); "a.s. on E₀" means this form.
  16| h : Ω × E → ℝ jointly measurable with |h| ≤ B_h (deterministic). For a record o, write Ẑ(o) for its evidence and
  17| η_q(o)(f) for the empirical measure of its q-th measured population.
  18| 
  19| ## Statement
  20| 
  21| For every q ∈ {1, …, 4}, almost surely,
  22|   E[1_{E₀} Ẑ_r · η_{rq}(h(·; 𝓒)) | 𝓒] = 1_{E₀} ψ_q(𝓒), where ψ_q(c) := E[Ẑ(Φ(c, U)) · η_q(Φ(c, U))(h(·; c))] for c ∈ A₀
  23|   (U an iid U[0,1) sequence), and ψ_q(c) := 0 otherwise.
  24| 
  25| ## Proof
  26| 
  27| Write E₀ = {𝓒 ∈ A₀} with A₀ ∈ 𝓔 (possible since E₀ ∈ σ(𝓒)); take A₀ := A_s ∩ {c : R′(c) ≥ r} ∩ A_𝒜 with A_𝒜 ∈ 𝓔 a set such that 𝒜 = {𝓒 ∈ A_𝒜} (success set A_s as in Lemma B). Define
  28| g : E × Υ → ℝ piecewise: g(c, u) := Ẑ(Φ(c, u)) · η_q(Φ(c, u))(h(·; c)) for c ∈ A₀, and g(c, u) := 0 for c ∉ A₀ (so the
  29| dummy record o† is never evaluated).
  30| *Measurability.* (c, u) ↦ Φ(c, u) is jointly measurable; Ẑ and the q-th population are measurable coordinates of the
  31| record; η_q(o)(h(·; c)) = (1/N_e)Σ_i h(S_i(o); c) is a finite sum of compositions of the jointly measurable h with
  32| measurable maps (N_e is a measurable integer coordinate of c, so the sum is measurable cell by cell on the countable
  33| partition {N_e(c) = N}). Hence g is 𝓔 ⊗ 𝓤-measurable.
  34| *Boundedness.* For c ∈ A₀ with grid (φ_t), every factor (1/N)Σ_i e^{Δ_t d(·)} lies in [e^{Δ_t min_Ω d}, e^{Δ_t max_Ω d}] and
  35| Σ_t Δ_t = 1, so Ẑ ∈ [Z_0 e^{min_Ω d}, Z_0 e^{max_Ω d}] with Z_0 = m(∅)Z̄₀ — a bound depending only on the fixed data, not on c
  36| (as in T12 PROOF_v6.tex:172). With |h| ≤ B_h, |g| ≤ B_h Z_0 e^{max_Ω d} < ∞ uniformly in (c, u).
  37| By the T12 freezing lemma (bounded measurable g; 𝓒 independent of U_r), E[g(𝓒, U_r) | 𝓒] = ḡ(𝓒) a.s. with
  38| ḡ(c) = E[g(c, U)] = ψ_q(c) (zero off A₀). Since g(𝓒, U_r) = 1_{E₀} Ẑ_r η_{rq}(h(·; 𝓒)) everywhere (both sides vanish off E₀;
  39| on E₀, O_r = Φ(𝓒, U_r)), E[1_{E₀} Ẑ_r η_{rq}(h(·; 𝓒)) | 𝓒] = ψ_q(𝓒) = 1_{E₀}ψ_q(𝓒) a.s. ∎
  40| 
  41| Remark (why the bound is needed). Without a deterministic bound on h over c, g need not be integrable and the
  42| conditional expectation needs a separate convention (SL1 item 1). Only island r's stream enters; no independence between
  43| islands is used (premise SI, weaker than IND-T).
  44| 
  45| ## Numerical falsification
  46| 
  47| Not separately falsifiable beyond Lemma B/P (measure-theoretic step). The numerics fix c (a production grid per design) and
  48| draw fresh final streams, which is the right-hand side ψ_q(c).

   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED under the named premises of STATEMENT §2 — cross-family checked (Codex gpt-6.1-sol: LC1, MP1 CONTINUE, SW1, council C1 9.3) and council-passed (Claude Opus 5.5: C1 8.9), round 1, 2026-11-08.    4| 
   5| ## Statement (verbatim from STATEMENT.md §3)
   6| 
   7| Under the premises of STATEMENT §2 (EX-A, EX-S/H-U, START, KERNEL, CAL, SI, MEAS, potential run; worker equivalence for
   8| v3.1's concurrent workers), for every fixed index r ≥ 1, every q ∈ {1, …, 4} and every h as in §1 (jointly measurable in
   9| (S, c), |h| ≤ B_h deterministic, fixed before stream 10), almost surely on 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}:
  10| 
  11|   (N1-q) E[Ẑ_r · (1/N_e)Σ_i h(S_{rqi}; 𝓒) | 𝓒] = Z · π(h(·; 𝓒));
  12|   (N1)   E[Ẑ_r · H_r(h) | 𝓒] = Z · π(h(·; 𝓒)),   H_r(h) = (4N_e)^{-1} Σ_{q=1}^{4} Σ_{i=1}^{N_e} h(S_{rqi}; 𝓒).
  13| 
  14| In particular E[W_r | 𝓒] = 1 and E[W_r H_r(h) | 𝓒] = π(h) with W_r := Ẑ_r/Z. "Almost surely on E₀ := 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}" means
  15| the localised form of Lemma F: E[1_{E₀}Y | 𝓒] = 1_{E₀}·(right side) a.s., Y the island-r integrand.

  17| ## Proof
  18| 
  19| By Lemma F, E[1_{E₀} Ẑ_r η_{rq}(h(·; 𝓒)) | 𝓒] = 1_{E₀}ψ_q(𝓒) a.s., with
  20| ψ_q(c) = E[Ẑ(Φ(c, U)) η_q(Φ(c, U))(h(·; c))] for an iid U[0,1) sequence U. Fix c ∈ A₀ (the set with E₀ = {𝓒 ∈ A₀}). By
  21| Lemma B, Φ(c, U) is a realisation of T12's frozen island I(c) with N = N_e(c), L′ = L(c), M = 4, flag unset, satisfying
  22| (R1)–(R3), with Ẑ(Φ(c,U)) = Ẑ_T and η_q(Φ(c,U)) = q̂^{(L+q)} (B-a, B-c). The function f := h(·; c) : Ω → ℝ is fixed (c is
  23| fixed). By Lemma P (T12 (i.b)), ψ_q(c) = E_c[Ẑ q̂^{(L+q)}(f)] = Zπ(f) = Zπ(h(·; c)). Hence the left side of (N1-q) equals
  24| Zπ(h(·; 𝓒)) a.s. on E₀, i.e. E[1_{E₀} Ẑ_r η_{rq}(h) | 𝓒] = 1_{E₀} Zπ(h(·; 𝓒)) a.s. (N1) is the average of (N1-q) over q = 1..4 (linearity of conditional expectation; H_r(h) =

   1| # Remarks: scope, sharpness and what breaks N1
   2| 
   3| Status: remarks (no new claims beyond those cited). v2, 2026-11-08 (numbers from RESULTS.md v2).
   4| 
   5| 1. **Route.** The charter route (resample–move recursion; the "terminal-round prefix identity") is used only in its
   6|    κ ≡ m (full-round) form. Measured endpoints are read after complete rounds (`v3_engine.h:357-360`), so the within-round
   7|    prefix identity (T12 (i.c)), which the Rao–Blackwellised record needs, plays no role. Seat A's reading — "(a2) for the
   8|    plain average is the base case of the same terminal-round unbiasedness [...] so N1 should be a short extension of the
   9|    locked lemma" (`NBH/branch_snapshots/MEET-v31/R3_A.md:38`) — is confirmed: N1 = T12 (i.b) + Lemma B (code bridge) +
  10|    Lemma F (conditioning with 𝓒-dependent h) + linearity.
  11| 
  12| 2. **Non-triviality.** The identity is for the evidence-weighted endpoint average. The unweighted average H_r(h) is biased
  13|    for π(h) (exact bias up to 0.16, `numerics/RESULTS.md` §3); E[Ẑ_r H_r(h)] = Zπ(h) holds to ≤ 9.3e-15 on the same cases. "Neither normalised estimate is generally unbiased at a finite budget" (`METHOD_v3.1_FINAL.md:158`) is
  14|    consistent with this.
  15| 
  16| 3. **What breaks it.** Exhibited numerically (`numerics/RESULTS.md` §4–§5): the first three items. The conditioning
  17|    items are supported by the cited locked results, not by this companion.
  18|    - A terminal kernel that is not π-invariant (NC1, rounds with the φ = ½ kernel): discrepancy 3e-3 to 0.77.
  19|    - Measuring without the final reweighting to φ = 1 (NC2): discrepancy ≥ 3e-3 even after L + 4 invariant rounds at φ = 1.
  20|    - An h chosen after the run (NC3, the indicator of the island's most frequent endpoint): N1-centred discrepancy
  21|      E[W H(h_ω) − π(h_ω)] up to +0.17, resolved (|z| > 6) on 18 of 20 runs; the other two runs do not detect a discrepancy. This is why the M9 declaration requires h fixed before stream 10 and excludes "the measured-round
  22|      frequency of the returned HPM" (`METHOD_v3.1_FINAL.md:159`).
  23|    - Conditioning on completion need not preserve it (clause (c), CEX-guard); conditioning on a favourable final
  24|      diagnostic breaks the evidence identity (T12 (iv.e)). N1 is a potential-run statement.
  25| 
  26| 4. **Sharper constant in (e).** For the plain average the islandwise bound is δ₁, attained by h = 1{S ≠ S₀}; the card's
  27|    2δ₁ is implied (`lemmas/E_corollary.md`).
  28| 
  29| 5. **Downstream (not proved here).** Clauses M1(f), (g), (i) take N1 as their premise ("PC1c3: PROVED (PC1 claim 3), 'E[W_r ĥ_r]
  30|    = π(h) is still a premise'", card TH01). With N1 proved, that premise is discharged **islandwise** (given 𝓒, on 𝒜 ∩ {r ≤ R′}) for every bounded declared h
  31|    under the named premises; pooled clauses keep their own premises; the clauses' own proofs, statuses and remaining premises (IND-T extension for R′ > 4, GUARD-W,

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # Lemma CR — elementary sample-correlation tails; consequences [CONC′] and (R′)
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED (by this seat); XF VERIFIED (R19, Codex gpt-6.1-sol) — v1, 2026-11-08. Note (R19): the complement of
   4| the margin event uses error ≥ δ*; apply [CONC′] at δ ↑ δ* (the bound is continuous in δ). Purpose: (1) a self-contained, explicit replacement for
   5| the classical citation [CONC] (PROOF.md:27-28) used by P2 / P8♯; (2) a fallback for dependency point D2: a summable,
   6| explicit partition-recovery bound that does not use Hotelling's density or W7 Corollary B. Only Laurent–Massart [LM]
   7| and the Gaussian tail are used. NBH = `Theory_work/Old_Projects/New_BVS_Headquarters/`.
   8| 
   9| [LM] (Laurent & Massart 2000, Lemma 1): for k ≥ 1, x > 0, P(χ²_k ≥ k + 2√(kx) + 2x) ≤ e^{−x}, P(χ²_k ≤ k − 2√(kx)) ≤ e^{−x}.
  10| 
  11| ## Lemma CR
  12| Let (u_i, v_i), i ≤ n (n ≥ 3), be iid bivariate normal with correlation r ∈ (−1,1), and r̂ the Pearson sample
  13| correlation (centred, as computed from the standardised Gram matrix; W7 §0.1, `NBH/branch_snapshots/W7-PART/PROOF.md:14-15`).
  14| Then for every δ ∈ (0, 2]:
  15|   P(|r̂ − r| > δ) ≤ 6 exp(−(n−1)δ²/1024).
  16| 
  17| *Proof.* r̂ is invariant under positive affine maps of each coordinate, so take means 0, variances 1, and write
  18| v = ru + sw, s := √(1−r²), with w iid N(0,1) independent of u. Let C be the centring matrix, N := n−1, and
  19| α := ‖Cu‖²/N, β := ‖Cw‖²/N, γ := ⟨Cu, Cw⟩/N, M := [[α, γ], [γ, β]], x := (r, s)ᵀ (‖x‖ = 1), e₁ := (1,0)ᵀ. Since
  20| Cv = rCu + sCw,
  21|   r̂ = e₁ᵀMx / (√(e₁ᵀMe₁) · √(xᵀMx)).
  22| Let η ∈ (0, ¼] and E_η := {|α − 1| ≤ η, |β − 1| ≤ η, |γ| ≤ η}. On E_η, Δ := M − I has entries bounded by η, so
  23| ‖Δ‖_op ≤ ‖Δ‖_F ≤ √(4η²) = 2η ≤ ½ (four entries, each of absolute value ≤ η). Then
  24| |e₁ᵀMx − r| = |e₁ᵀΔx| ≤ 2η, and e₁ᵀMe₁, xᵀMx ∈ [1−2η, 1+2η], so the denominator d ∈ [1−2η, 1+2η]. Hence
  25|   |r̂ − r| ≤ |e₁ᵀMx − r|/d + |r|·|1/d − 1| ≤ 2η/(1−2η) + 2η/(1−2η) ≤ 8η.
  26| Probability of E_ηᶜ: Nα and Nβ are χ²_N. Upper tail with x = Nη²/16: 2√(Nx) + 2x = Nη/2 + Nη²/8 ≤ Nη (η ≤ 1), so
  27| P(α − 1 > η) ≤ e^{−Nη²/16}. Lower tail with x = Nη²/4: P(α − 1 < −η) ≤ e^{−Nη²/4}. Same for β. Given u, Nγ =
  28| ⟨Cu, w⟩ ~ N(0, Nα) (w ⊥ u, ⟨Cu, Cw⟩ = ⟨Cu, w⟩); on {α ≤ 1 + η} ⊆ {α ≤ 2}, P(|Nγ| > Nη | u) ≤ 2e^{−N²η²/(4N)} = 2e^{−Nη²/4}.
  29| So P(E_ηᶜ) ≤ 2(e^{−Nη²/16} + e^{−Nη²/4}) + 2e^{−Nη²/4} ≤ 6e^{−Nη²/16}. With η := δ/8 ≤ ¼:
  30| P(|r̂ − r| > δ) ≤ P(E_ηᶜ) ≤ 6e^{−Nδ²/1024}. ∎
  31| 
  32| ## Corollary [CONC′] (replaces the cited [CONC])
  33| For the LH-iid design (any p, rows iid N(0, Σ), Σ a correlation matrix) and any δ ∈ (0, 2]:
  34|   P(max_{j<k} |r̂_jk − Σ_jk| > δ) ≤ 3p² e^{−(n−1)δ²/1024}.
  35| With p ≤ n^A and δ_n := 32√(2(A+1) log n/(n−1)) (≤ 2 for n ≥ n₀(A)): the bound is ≤ 3n^{2A}n^{−2(A+1)} = 3n^{−2}, summable.
  36| So max_{j<k}|r̂_jk − Σ_jk| ≤ C₁√(log p ∨ log n)/√n-type control holds in the explicit form
  37| max|r̂ − Σ| ≤ δ_n = O(√(log n/n)) w.p. ≥ 1 − 3n^{−2}. *Proof.* Union bound over ≤ p²/2 pairs. ∎
  38| *Use.* P2(a) / P8♯ step 2(a): ‖R̂_T − Σ_T‖_op ≤ |T|·δ_n ≤ L_n δ_n = O((log n)^{3/2}n^{−1/2}) → 0, so λ_min(R̂_T) ≥ λ₀/2 for
  39| all |T| ≤ L_n once L_nδ_n ≤ λ₀/2, on an event of probability ≥ 1 − 3n^{−2}.
  40| 
  41| ## Corollary (R′) (fallback for D2)
  42| On LH-iid with (SIZE) at n: within-group population correlations equal ρ; cross-group ones are 0, ψ_i, ψ_iρ, ψ_iρ²,
  43| all ≤ ψ̄ < ρ in absolute value (W7-PART §0.2 example, PROOF.md:41-44 of W7). Put δ* := (ρ − ψ̄)/2 ∈ (0, ½) and t := (ρ+ψ̄)/2.
  44| On {max_{j<k}|r̂_jk − Σ_jk| < δ*}: every within |r̂| > ρ − δ* = t and every cross |r̂| < ψ̄ + δ* = t, i.e. the global
  45| margin of W7 Theorem B's proof holds, and W7 Theorem A (A4 ⇒ A1 ⇒ A3; status "PROVED (W7-PART); XF VERIFIED* (A-REV9:
  46| A1-A4 VERIFIED ...)", `NBH/ID_REGISTRY.md:310`) — equivalently PXN Lemma P1 (XF VERIFIED, A-REV3) — gives blocks = groups.
  47| Hence, for every n ≥ 3 at which SIZE holds,
  48|   P(𝒜_nᶜ) ≤ 3p² exp(−(n−1)(ρ−ψ̄)²/4096).
  49| Consequences: with p ≤ n^A, Σ_n P(𝒜_nᶜ) < ∞, and for every C > 0, P(𝒜_nᶜ) ≤ p^{−C} once
  50| log 3 + (2 + C)A log n ≤ (n−1)(ρ−ψ̄)²/4096 (using p ≤ n^A for p^{2+C}); this is the first-line form of (R) that (C), (P)
  51| use. The exponent (ρ−ψ̄)²/4096 is far from W7's I* (crude constants); it is explicit and needs no Hotelling density.
  52| 
  53| ## Remark on what is (not) claimed
  54| - The 1/1024 constant is not optimised. Only the exponential-in-n form and the explicit constants matter.
  55| - This lemma does not touch W7 Theorem A (deterministic); it replaces only the probabilistic step (Lemma 2 / Corollary B).

   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED (by this seat); XF VERIFIED (R17: role in (L); R19: arithmetic) — v1, 2026-11-08, following statement-lock review R00 finding 8.
   4| Only the "additions A = S₀ + l" bullet (PROOF.md:363-367) changes; the deletion/swap bullet is unchanged.
   5| 
   6| **Issue.** PROOF.md:365 bounds νx_l(1+2x_l) by (Z_l²/2)(1+o(1)) citing (E3), but (E3) only gives RSS_{S₀} ≥ nσ²/2,
   7| which yields νx_l ≤ Z_l²(1+o(1)), i.e. a term ≈ 2 log p instead of log p, and then F(S₀+l) − F(S₀) ≤ log p − ½ log n + ...,
   8| which does not → −∞ when p ≫ √n. The multiplicative "1+o(1)" also must be made additive after multiplication by log p.
   9| 
  10| **Corrected step.** Work on Ω_n ∩ 𝒵_n (PROOF.md:351, 357), 𝒵_n := {max_{l∉S₀} Z_l² ≤ 2 log p + 2 log log n}, with Lemma E
  11| applied to 𝔉_n = {A : |A| ≤ s₀+2} (J = s₀+2, D = A(s₀+2)). Since μ ∈ span X_{S₀}, Λ_{S₀} = 0 and RSS_{S₀} = ‖Π^⊥_{S₀}ε‖²;
  12| by (E5) (PROOF.md:172, proof at 198-199), |RSS_{S₀} − nσ²| ≤ C₂n^{2/3}, so for n ≥ n₀,
  13|   RSS_{S₀} ≥ nσ²(1 − C₂n^{−1/3}/σ²) =: nσ²(1 − ε_n),  ε_n = O(n^{−1/3}).
  14| With x_l := σ²Z_l²/RSS_{S₀}: x_l ≤ (2 log p + 2 log log n)/(n(1−ε_n)) ≤ 3A log n/n ≤ ¼ for n ≥ n₀ (p ≤ n^A). Using
  15| −log(1−x) ≤ x + x² for x ≤ ½ (in fact ≤ x(1+2x) for x ≤ ¼ suffices) and ν = n/2 + 0.01:
  16|   −ν log(1 − x_l) ≤ ν x_l (1 + x_l) ≤ (n/2 + 0.01) · Z_l²/(n(1−ε_n)) · (1 + 3A log n/n)
  17|                  ≤ (Z_l²/2)(1 + 2ε_n)(1 + 3A log n/n)(1 + 0.02/n)      (ε_n ≤ ½)
  18|                  ≤ (Z_l²/2) + (Z_l²/2)·κ_n,   κ_n := O(n^{−1/3} + (log n)/n).

  22|   F(S₀+l) − F(S₀) ≤ log((s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀)) − ½ log(n+1) + log p + log log n + 2κ_E + o(1)
  23|                  ≤ log(s₀+1) + log(p/(2p−1−s₀)) − ½ log n + log log n + 2κ_E + o(1)
  24|                  = −½ log n + log log n + O(1) → −∞,
  25| uniformly in l ∉ S₀ (p/(2p−1−s₀) ≤ 1 for p ≥ s₀ + 1). Combined with the unchanged deletion/swap bullet, on Ω_n ∩ 𝒵_n no
  26| feasible flip or swap of S₀ attains a score ≥ F(S₀) for n ≥ n₀: (L).

  32|    m ≥ 1 + s₀ log₂(2p) + ((s₀+2)/2) log₂ n. With p ≤ n^A: m♯_n ≤ k_n := max{s₀, ⌈1 + s₀ + (As₀ + (s₀+2)/2) log₂ n⌉} = O(log n).

params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  31| ## R.2 Score evaluations (each is one call of `Scorer::score`, or a cache hit)
  32| Let κ(n, k) be the cost of one score of a size-k model: Gram sub-block O(k²) (or O(nk²) on the refactor route), two
  33| Cholesky O(k³), solves O(k²), the Q fallback O(nk), the QR route O((n+k)k²) (`cpp/v3_score.h:162-238`); so
  34| κ(n,k) ≤ C_s (n + k)k² + C_s ≤ C_s(n³ + 1) for k ≤ K ≤ n/2. Per request there is also a deterministic overhead
  35| ω(n,p): the score cache uses linear probing over ≤ 2^{⌈log₂(1000p)⌉} ≤ 2000p slots with key comparisons of ≤ K + 1
  36| words (`cpp/v3_score.h:264-289`; fixed Zobrist hashes, no hashing assumption), the occasional full-table clear O(p)
  37| (:284), the start component `Start::comp` with a sort O(K log K + J) (`cpp/v3_start.h:52-64`), and the store offers
  38| (three ordered sets of ≤ 40p+1 entries, comparisons of ≤ K ints: O(K log p), `cpp/v3_ledger.h:33-53`); so
  39| ω(n,p) ≤ C_o [p(K + 1) + J + K log(Kp)] ≤ C_o′ p(n + 2). Number of score requests:
  40| - tables: Σ_b 2^{|C_b|} ≤ J·2^B ≤ 2¹⁶ p;
  41| - one island with N particles and T stages: N (initial draws) + N(T + L + 4)·2m (each label scores ≤ 2 models: Gibbs
  42|   both configurations, a swap proposal and the current state, an independence proposal);
  43| - one local search: ≤ (ℓ + 1)(p + p²/4) + 1;
  44| - one V construction: ≤ |V| ≤ 40p + 1 rescorings (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:671-690`; stores of size 20p, 20p, plus ∅);
  45| - calibration tier e: pilot (N = H_e, T ≤ T_e) + local search + ≤ ℓ × [4 islands (H_e, T ≤ T_e) + local search]
  46|   + ≤ ℓ + 1 V constructions;
  47| - final run: inherited models (≤ (40p+1) + 20p + 20p + 1) + R′ islands (N_e, T ≤ T_e) + final search (+ c₄ search when
  48|   R′ > 4) + LS0.
  49| Hence the total number of score requests is at most
  50|   Σ̄(n,p) := 2¹⁶p + 2[(1 + 4ℓ)(4H₀)(1 + (T̄ + ℓ + 8)·2m) + (ℓ + 1)²(p + p²/4 + 1) + (ℓ + 1)(40p + 1)]
  51|             + (80p + 2) + R′·N̄(1 + (T̄ + ℓ + 8)·2m) + 3(ℓ + 1)(p + p²/4 + 1)
  52|            = O((n + p)·p·ℓ·T₀) = O((n + p)·p·log³(n + p))   (T₀ = max(1000, ℓ²)).
  53| On the exact branch the count is E + 200 (timing) ≤ (5H₀ + 4N₀)p + 200.

  56| Resampling: O(N) guide table + ≤ O(N²) worst-case lookups per stage; `distinct()`: ≤ O(N²W) per call (hash buckets,

  58| ≤ (T_e + 1)·62·3·|V| operations for the ρ_V evaluations, plus target processing — the sort of the k ≤ T_e pilot
  59| targets and the rescan of the target list at every trial (`cpp/v3_calib.h:70, :74-75`): O(k log k + (T_e + 1)k) =
  60| O(T̄²) per construction, ≤ 2(ℓ + 1) constructions (R05 #2); Fisher–Yates order O(m) per particle-round; π₀ draws (independence step and initial
  61| draws) O(J·B + K log(K+1)) each (incl. the final sort of the emitted indices, `cpp/v3_start.h:174`; charged within ω, R2 Codex #1); RB accumulation O(1) per Gibbs step and O(p) per measured round; V construction O(|V|(K + J)).
  62| Setup: standardisation O(np), Gram O(np²), correlations/distances O(p²), complete linkage ≤ O(p³) (`cpp/v3_blocks.h:
  63| 12, 54-61`), neighbour graph O(p² log p) (`cpp/v3_blocks.h:151-170`), tables (above), start DP and convolution
  64| O(J(K + 1)(B + 1) + J2^B). Start-mode ties (LS0 centre, spec): fast path ≤ 10⁶(J + K log K) operations (R.1), and the
  65| TDP fallback ≤ C p·J(2^B + (K + 1)²) ≤ C p²(2¹⁶ + n²). Exact-branch timing (`v3_fit.R:10-14`): a context on

  68| U₂₀₀ ≤ C[n m_t² + 200(κ̄ + ω̄ + k_t log k_t)].

  70| ## Lemma R (within CONFIG, STATEMENT §1). There are absolute (implementation-dependent, not instantiated) constants
  71| C_W, C_M such that for every valid input (R.4) with n ≥ 3,
  72| every seed and every realisation of the uniforms, the total number of elementary operations of 𝔐 is at most
  73|   W̄(n,p) := C_W [ Σ̄(n,p)·(n³ + p(n + 2)) + (N̄²W + N̄H₀)(T̄ + ℓ + 8)(R′ + 8ℓ + 8) + T̄·p·ℓ + np² + p³
  74|                + p²(2¹⁶ + n²) + 10⁶(p + n log n) + U₂₀₀ + (ℓ + 1)T̄²·(40p + 2)
  75|                + (R′ + 8ℓ + 2)·4N̄·2pB + Cert(n,p) ]
  76|           = O( (n+p)·p·(n³ + pn)·log³(n+p) + (n+p)²·p·log³(n+p) + p²n² + p³ + Cert(n,p) ),
  77| and the number of words held at any time is at most
  78|   M̄(n,p) := 2·C_M [ np + p² + 2¹⁶p + J(K+1)(B+1) + N̄(W + K) + R′·(500p(W + K) + (80p + 1)(K + 4)) + (40p+1)(K + 3)
  79|                + (R′ + 8ℓ + 2)(T̄ + ℓ + 8 + 6p) + K(ℓ + 3)² + 2(ℓ + 1)·min(40p + 1, 10⁴)(K + 3)
  80|                + (R′ + 8ℓ + 2)(T̄ + 1) + 2(ℓ + 1)(T̄ + 1) + (n + K)K·w + 10⁶(K + 1) + n·max(64, k_t) + m_t² + 2pB·(R′ + 8ℓ + 2) + Cert_M(n,p) ]
  81|           = O((n + p)² + Cert_M(n,p)).
  82| *Proof.* Every loop is capped (R.1); the work is the sum over R.2–R.3 of (count) × (cost per item, including ω per
  83| score request), each a polynomial in (n,p) independent of the data, seed and uniforms. The words held at any time are
  84| bounded by the sum of the following, each with its term in M̄: X and the stored Gram (np + p²); correlation and
  85| distance matrices (p²); dendrogram arrays (O(p)); block tables and size profiles (2¹⁶p, J(K+1)(B+1)); the score
  86| cache (500p entries of ≤ W + K words, `v3_calib.R:138`, `v3_run.R:89`) and the three stores (≤ 80p + 1 models of
  87| ≤ K + 4 words), per worker when R′ > 4 (factor R′, also covering the merge state); V (≤ 40p + 1 models with 3 doubles);
  88| the population and its resampled copy (N̄(W + K)); the island archives kept in R (pilot ≤ 2, diagnostics ≤ 8ℓ, final
  89| R′ islands; each with O(1) words per stage and per terminal round, the RB rounds 4p, the PIP and RB accumulators 2p:
  90| (R′ + 8ℓ + 2)(T̄ + ℓ + 8 + 6p); `v3_calib.R:49-56, :85-99, :125`); local-search archives (≤ 2(ℓ + 1) + 3 searches,
  91| each ≤ ℓ + 1 scanned models of ≤ K ints: K(ℓ + 3)²); the V snapshots (≤ 2(ℓ + 1) constructions, each ≤ min(40p + 1,
  92| 10⁴) models with 2 doubles, `v3_calib.R:17-21`); the guard's checkpoint records (one per bridge stage, per search and
  93| per build, O(1) words each); the stored grids; the scorer workspaces (O((n + K)K) for the QR route); the
  94| tie-enumeration store (≤ 10⁶ models of ≤ K + 1 words) and the TDP tables (≤ J(K + 1) + 2¹⁶p, already counted); the
  95| exact-branch timing context (n·max(64, k_t) + m_t²); and the R-level copies and the serialised fit (at most one more
  96| copy of all of the above: the factor 2). Recursion stacks (exact enumeration, depth ≤ K, `cpp/v3_core.cpp:505-524`;
  97| start-mode enumeration and TDP, depth ≤ J) are O(p) words, covered by MACH's stack clause. Each term is O((n + p)²); the least obvious are 2(ℓ + 1)·10⁴(K + 3) =
  98| O(n log(n + p)) and (R′ + 8ℓ + 2)(T̄ + 6p) = O(log³(n + p) + p log(n + p)). ∎

   1| # L2 — Lemma S: input, degenerate and numerical paths are empty (a.s.) on the classes
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED (by this seat); R02: S.1, S.2 and D2 survive; S.3 list extended per R02 #5. Paths refer to INVENTORY.md; code = `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/`.
   4| 
   5| ## S.1 Inputs (A1–A7)
   6| Setting: model G (fixed or random design X with p ≥ 1 columns, y = α1 + Xβ + ε, ε ~ N(0, σ²I), σ² > 0), n ≥ 3, the
   7| seed a declared integer in [1, 2³¹ − 1], the allocation a declared list of two finite positive numbers.
   8| - A1 (`v3_fit.R:63-64`), A2 (`v3_fit.R:66-69`): excluded by the declared seed and allocation (class (d)).
   9| - A3 (`v3_preprocess.R:97-107`): X is a numeric matrix with finite entries (fixed design: by the class definition D0;
  10|   LH-iid: Gaussian rows are finite a.s.), y = α1 + Xβ + ε is finite a.s., n ≥ 3 and p ≥ 1. So P(A3) = 0.
  11| - A4 (`v3_preprocess.R:111-114`): a column is dropped only if all its entries are exactly equal. Exact-Gram LH and the
  12|   GEN fixed designs are standardised with ‖x_j‖² = n − 1 > 0 and centred, hence nonconstant; for random designs with a
  13|   nonsingular Gaussian row law each column is nonconstant a.s. (n ≥ 2). So no column is dropped (p unchanged) and
  14|   P(A4) = 0.
  15| - A5 (`v3_preprocess.R:115`): y constant means ε ∈ {c1 − α1 − Xβ : c ∈ ℝ}, a line in ℝⁿ, which has Lebesgue measure 0
  16|   for n ≥ 2; so P(A5) = 0.
  17| - A6 (`degenerate_n`, spec e3): requires n = 1; excluded by n ≥ 3. A7 (`unsupported_size`, spec e7): excluded by
  18|   IDEAL-W.
  19| 
  20| ## S.2 Numerical failures (C1–C5) are impossible under EX-A
  21| The only source of `NumericalFailure` is `Scorer::score` (`cpp/v3_score.h:226-238`), thrown only if all three routes
  22| fail. Route 1 (`try_chol`, `cpp/v3_score.h:175-188`) on a model S with 1 ≤ k = |S| ≤ K forms H = (n+1)G_S + I_k and
  23| A = G_S + I_k with G_S = X_SᵀX_S ⪰ 0, so H, A ⪰ I_k are positive definite. In exact arithmetic the Cholesky recursion
  24| `chol_inplace` (`cpp/v3_score.h:76-90`) produces pivots d_j = (L_jj)² > 0 for a positive definite matrix (they are
  25| ratios of leading principal minors), so its failure test `!(d > 0) || !isfinite(d)` (:80) never fires. In
  26| `finish_from_factors` (:204-224) the log-determinants are finite, and
  27|   Q = yᵀy − n zᵀH⁻¹z ≥ yᵀy − (n/(n+1)) yᵀy = yᵀy/(n+1) > 0,
  28| because X_S((n+1)X_SᵀX_S + I)⁻¹X_Sᵀ ⪯ (n+1)⁻¹I (singular values σ²/((n+1)σ² + 1) ≤ 1/(n+1)) and yᵀy = n − 1 > 0 after
  29| standardisation (S.1). If the code recomputes Q by `q_nonneg` (when Q < 10⁻⁸yᵀy, possible only for n + 1 > 10⁸), the
  30| recomputed value equals Q exactly: with β = nH⁻¹z, ‖y − X_Sβ‖² + (‖X_Sβ‖² + ‖β‖²)/n = yᵀy − 2βᵀz + n⁻¹βᵀHβ =
  31| yᵀy − n zᵀH⁻¹z. Hence 2b₀ + Q > 0, log m(S) is finite (:222-223), `try_chol` returns true, and `score` returns at
  32| :233. For k = 0 the score is log m(∅) directly (:232). The k > K throw (:230) is an internal invariant: every caller
  33| passes models of size ≤ K (additions at |S| = K are excluded: Gibbs `o_j = 0`, local search `continue`,

   9| V finite, nonempty set of models (the candidate set built by `cpp_cal_V`, `v3_core.cpp:671-690`), A(S) = log γ₀(S)
  10| (`lg0`), d(S) = log γ₁(S) − log γ₀(S). For t ∈ ℝ: ℓ_S(t) = A(S) + t d(S), F(t) = log Σ_{S∈V} e^{ℓ_S(t)} (`F_V`,
  11| v3_calib.h:49-53), q_t(S) = e^{ℓ_S(t) − F(t)}. The code's restricted ESS is
  12| ρ(u, v) = exp{2F(v) − F(u) − F(2v − u)} (`rho_V`, v3_calib.h:55-58). Write Δ(u, v) := F(u) − 2F(v) + F(2v − u), so
  13| ρ = e^{−Δ}. c₀ := log(10/9), so ρ ≥ 0.90 ⟺ Δ ≤ c₀.
  14| 
  15| ## Lemma 3.1 (exact identity). For every M ∈ V and all real u, v:
  16|   ρ(u, v) = q_u(M) · q_{2v−u}(M) / q_v(M)².
  17| *Proof.* F(t) = ℓ_M(t) − log q_t(M). ℓ_M is affine, so ℓ_M(u) − 2ℓ_M(v) + ℓ_M(2v−u) = 0 and
  18| Δ(u,v) = −log q_u(M) + 2 log q_v(M) − log q_{2v−u}(M). ∎
  19| *Consequences.* (i) ρ(u,v) ≥ q_u(M)·q_{2v−u}(M) for every M ∈ V (since q_v(M) ≤ 1). (ii) If some M has
  20| q_u(M) ≥ √0.9 and q_{2v−u}(M) ≥ √0.9, the step (u, v) passes.
  21| 
  22| ## Lemma 3.2 (convexity facts). F is convex and C^∞ with F′(t) = E_{q_t}d, F″(t) = Var_{q_t}(d). For u ≤ v,
  23|   Δ(u, v) = ∫_u^{2v−u} (v − u − |t − v|) F″(t) dt,  hence 0 ≤ Δ(u, v) ≤ (v − u)² · sup_{t∈[u, 2v−u]} Var_{q_t}(d),
  24| and v ↦ ρ(u, v) is non-increasing on [u, ∞).
  25| *Proof.* The second difference of a C² function with the Peano kernel K(t) = (h − |t − v|)₊, h = v − u, ∫K = h².
  26| Monotonicity: ∂_v Δ(u,v) = −2F′(v) + 2F′(2v − u) ≥ 0 because F′ is non-decreasing and 2v − u ≥ v. ∎
  27| *Corollary 3.2′ (dominance intervals).* For c ∈ (½, 1) and M ∈ V the set {t : q_t(M) ≥ c} is a (possibly empty)

  29| 
  30| ## Lemma 3.3 (pilot schedule). At every tier e the pilot's temperatures 0 = φ₀ < φ₁ < … < φ_k = 1 satisfy
  31| k ≤ T_e, and every non-final increment is ≥ 1/T_e. The tier's pilot schedule `pil$schedule` = (φ₀, …, φ_k) is the
  32| target list of every construction at that tier.
  33| *Proof.* Island loop (adaptive branch), v3_engine.h:303-341: the loop exits when φ_prev == 1.0 (:310); otherwise
  34| `pilot_next_phi` (v3_calib.h:30-46) returns either 1.0 (if the step to 1 passes), or the bisection value lo with
  35| lo − φ ≥ 1/T_e (unforced; lo < 1 since every tested mid is < hi ≤ 1), or the forced value f = min(1, φ + 1/T_e),
  36| replaced by 1 when f ≥ 1 − 10⁻¹² (so f ≥ φ + 1/T_e or f = 1). Hence each step is a strict increase, every non-final
  37| step increases φ by ≥ 1/T_e, and the last step lands exactly at 1 (the only values ≥ 1 − 10⁻¹² produced are 1.0, or
  38| an unforced lo < 1, which is not final). If k steps occur, (k − 1)/T_e ≤ φ_{k−1} < 1, so k ≤ T_e; termination
  39| follows. `cpp_cal_pilot` returns sched = (0, φ₁, …, φ_k) (v3_core.cpp:604); `v3_cal_tier` passes `pil$schedule`
  40| to every `build` of that tier (v3_calib.R:44, :68, :79, :111). ∎
  41| 
  42| ## Lemma 3.4 (what the construction does). `build_grid(lg0, d, targets, T_e)` (v3_calib.h:68-98) with the pilot
  43| schedule as targets:
  44| (a) every appended point is either the current target b (the smallest pilot temperature > u) or, if ρ(u,b) < 0.90, the
  45|     bisection value lo ∈ (u, b) (60 halvings with lo = u, hi = b); a point ≥ 1 − 10⁻¹² is snapped to 1;
  46| (b) consequently: an unsnapped step never skips its current target; every pilot temperature strictly below the first
  47|     raw candidate that is snapped to 1 is reached; that candidate is replaced by 1 and later targets are skipped
  48|     (R03 #5). Hence #intervals = N_p′ + N_b^app, where N_b^app counts appended bisection steps (L5) and N_p′ ≤ k ≤ T_e
  49|     counts the steps that end on a pilot temperature or on the snapped value 1;
  50| (c) failure reasons under EX-A: `no_target_above_u` never occurs (1 is a target and u < 1 inside the loop);
  51|     `validation_failed` never occurs for an unsnapped point (ρ(u,v) ≥ 0.90 was tested at that exact v) and for a
  52|     snapped point v = 1 it fails iff ρ(u, 1) < 0.90; `non_progress` occurs iff no tested mid passes. If no mid passes,
  53|     every update is hi = mid, so the 60th test is exactly the smallest dyadic point u + (b − u)2⁻⁶⁰; if some mid passes,
  54|     it is ≥ that point, which therefore passes too (monotonicity, Lemma 3.2). So `non_progress` ⟺
  55|     ρ(u, u + (b − u)2⁻⁶⁰) < 0.90; and once a mid passed, the second progress check (:90) cannot fail (lo > u) (R03 #4).

  58| smallest pilot temperature > u and unsnapped appended points satisfy v ≤ b, so the next u is ≤ b and b remains the
  59| next target until it is appended or a snap to 1 ends the construction. ∎
  60| 
  61| ## Proposition 3.5 (success criterion; grid ⊆ pilot ∪ {1}). Let (φ_i) be the tier's pilot schedule and V the candidate set.
  62| (a) If ρ(u, v) ≥ 0.90 for every pair 0 ≤ u < v ≤ 1 with u ∈ {φ_i} ∪ {snap points} — in particular if
  63|     sup_{t∈[0,2]} Var_{q_t}(d) < c₀, or if some M ∈ V has q_t(M) ≥ √0.9 for t = 0 and t = 2 (hence, by Cor. 3.2′, for
  64|     all t ∈ [0, 2]) — then the construction succeeds; it never bisects, its points are the pilot temperatures up to
  65|     the first one in [1 − 10⁻¹², 1], which is replaced by 1 (later targets are skipped), so its interval count is
  66|     ≤ k ≤ T_e. (It is NOT always exactly the pilot schedule: R01 #2.)
  67| (b) In general the construction succeeds iff no `non_progress`, no failed validation at a snapped point, and
  68|     N_p′ + N_b^app ≤ T_e (appended intervals).
  69| *Proof.* (a) At u = φ_{i−1} the target is b = φ_i and ρ(u, b) ≥ 0.90, so v = b, or v = 1 if b ≥ 1 − 10⁻¹² (then

  71| after a snap u = 1 and the loop ends. So N_b = 0, every interval ends at a distinct pilot temperature or at 1, and the

  74| 2v − u ∈ [0, 2]; Lemma 3.1(i) gives ρ ≥ 0.9. (b) is Lemma 3.4(c). ∎

  76| ## Remark 3.6 (why (a) is rarely enough; measured). Numerics N1 (`numerics/psi_enum.py`, outputs `N1_psi_F.txt`,

  81| construction with a one-jump pilot (targets {1}) succeeds with only 8–15 intervals (F) and 10 (M), and with a 10-step

   1| # L5 — How many points does the construction insert? Two-model transition lemma (deterministic)
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED (by this seat); R03 (Codex xhigh): Lemmas 5.0, 5.1, 5.2, 5.2′ VERIFIED / VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS,
   4| Corollary 5.3 ERROR as first written → corrected below (v2). Notation of L3 (ℓ_S, F, q_t, ρ, Δ). EX-A.
   5| A *trial* of the construction is one pass of the loop at a point u; it is *bisection-limited* if ρ(u, b) < 0.90 at its
   6| current target b (L3 Lemma 3.4(a)). N_b^try counts bisection-limited trials; N_b^app ≤ N_b^try counts those that
   7| append an interval. The interval identity of L3 Lemma 3.4(b) uses N_b^app. (R03 #3.) A bisection-limited trial that
   8| appends never appends a snapped point: if lo were snapped to 1 then ρ(u, 1) ≤ ρ(u, b) < 0.90 (monotonicity) and
   9| validation fails, so such a trial ends the construction (event (γ)).
  10| 
  11| ## Lemma 5.0 (bisection step length). If a trial from u is bisection-limited and some mid passes, the raw passing point
  12| v_raw := lo and the last failing tested point w = u + h (= hi) satisfy v_raw − u ≥ h/2, ρ(u, w) < 0.90, and
  13| ρ(u, v_raw) ≥ 0.90 (before any snap; R03 #5).
  14| *Proof.* With lo = u, hi = b and 60 halvings (v3_calib.h:83-85), at the end hi − lo = (b − u)2⁻⁶⁰; hi has failed
  15| (either hi = b, which failed, or hi was set at a failing mid) and lo = v passed. Progress means some mid passed, so
  16| lo − u = jδ with δ = (b − u)2⁻⁶⁰ and an integer j ≥ 1, so h = hi − u = (j + 1)δ ≤ 2jδ = 2(lo − u). ∎
  17| 
  18| ## Lemma 5.1 (two-model closed form). For M₁, M₂ with d(M₂) − d(M₁) = D > 0, let x(t) := ℓ_{M₂}(t) − ℓ_{M₁}(t) = x₀ + tD
  19| and, for the two-point family on {M₁, M₂}, ρ⁽²⁾(u, v) = 1 − a(c − 1)²/((1 + a)(1 + ac²)) with a = e^{x(u)}, c = e^{(v−u)D}.
  20| Moreover, for all a > 0 and c ≥ 1: (i) 1 − ρ⁽²⁾ ≤ tanh²((v − u)D/2); (ii) 1 − ρ⁽²⁾ ≤ 1/(1 + a);
  21| (iii) 1 − ρ⁽²⁾ ≤ ac²/(1 + ac²).
  22| *Proof.* By Lemma 3.1 with M = M₂ on the two-point family, ρ⁽²⁾ = σ(x)σ(x+2s)/σ(x+s)² with σ(z) = e^z/(1+e^z),
  23| s = (v − u)D; simplifying gives (1 + ac)²/((1 + a)(1 + ac²)), and (1 + ac)² − (1 + a)(1 + ac²) = −a(c − 1)².
  24| (i) a/((1 + a)(1 + ac²)) is maximised over a > 0 at a = 1/c with value 1/(1 + c)², and (c − 1)²/(c + 1)² =
  25| tanh²(s/2). (ii) a(c−1)² ≤ ac² ≤ 1 + ac². (iii) (c − 1)² ≤ c² and 1 + a ≥ 1. ∎
  26| 
  27| ## Lemma 5.2 (insertions on a two-model family with an ε-remainder). Let V ∋ M₁, M₂ with D = d(M₂) − d(M₁) > 0 and
  28| suppose r_t := 1 − q_t(M₁) − q_t(M₂) ≤ ε for all t ∈ [0, 2], with ε ∈ [0, 0.02]. Put θ := 0.90/(1 − ε)² (< 0.94),
