params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  18| data, so a data-dependent cap does not affect operational closure [OP] or the stream/uniform accounting.

  20| constants C_R = 3(M + σ²), c_E = σ²/(12(M + σ²)), κ_E = 0.52/c_E + 1), with n₀ depending also on C_J.

  29| ## L0.2 Three consequences (used in L2, L3)

<file path="Theory_work/Wave1C/C-GROW/lemmas/L1_descent.md">
   1| # L1 — Deterministic descent on a superset lattice (claim (C1))
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R03 (Codex Sol high, reviews/R03_L0L1L2_check_sol.md): VERIFIED. Deterministic (fixed data, EX-A). Model: T37R Lemma 2(b) ("PROVED",
   4| `Theory_work/Old_Projects/New_BVS_Headquarters/branch_snapshots/W1-T37R/PROOF.md:103-115`), which proves the same
   5| reduction for supersets with at most d extras; here the lattice is that of an arbitrary deterministic set Q ⊇ S₀ and
   6| the move count is made explicit. Search semantics: GEN/lemmas/L4_search.md (M §6.10 as restated in SoP
   7| `02_method.tex:463-467`; LS0: SoP `02_method.tex:490-499`).
   8| 
   9| ## Setting
  10| 
  11| S₀ ⊆ Q ⊆ [p], |Q| ≤ K (so every T with S₀ ⊆ T ⊆ Q is feasible), 𝓛 := {T : S₀ ⊆ T ⊆ Q}. F(S) = log w(|S|) + log m(S)
  12| on Ω. Neighbours of S (M §6.10): additions S ∪ {l} (l ∉ S; only if |S| < K), deletions S ∖ {i} (i ∈ S), swaps
  13| (S ∖ {i}) ∪ {l} (i ∈ S, l ∉ S). Events (deterministic properties of the data):
  14| 
  15| * **NA(𝓛)**: F(T ∪ {l}) < F(T) for every T ∈ 𝓛 with |T| < K and every l ∉ T.
  16| * **TL(𝓛)**: for every T ∈ 𝓛 and every feasible neighbour A of T with S₀ ⊄ A: F(A) < F(T).
  17|   (Such A are exactly T ∖ {i} and (T ∖ {i}) ∪ {l} with i ∈ S₀, l ∉ T.)
  18| 
  19| ## Lemma L1.1 (one step)
  20| 
  21| On NA(𝓛) ∩ TL(𝓛), for every C ∈ 𝓛:
  22| (a) if C ≠ S₀: every deletion C ∖ {e}, e ∈ C ∖ S₀, satisfies F(C ∖ {e}) > F(C); every other feasible neighbour A of C
  23| satisfies F(A) < max_{e∈C∖S₀} F(C ∖ {e}). Hence the set of maximisers of F over the feasible neighbours of C consists
  24| of deletions of elements of C ∖ S₀ only, and each maximiser strictly improves F(C) and lies in 𝓛.
  25| (b) if C = S₀: every feasible neighbour A of S₀ satisfies F(A) < F(S₀).
  26| 
  27| *Proof.* (a) Let e ∈ C ∖ S₀. Then T := C ∖ {e} ∈ 𝓛 (S₀ ⊆ T ⊆ Q), |T| = |C| − 1 < K and e ∉ T, so NA at (T, e)
  28| gives F(C) = F(T ∪ {e}) < F(T) = F(C ∖ {e}). Now let A be a feasible neighbour of C that is not a deletion of an
  29| element of C ∖ S₀. Cases:
  30| * A = C ∪ {l} (l ∉ C, |C| < K): NA at (C, l) gives F(A) < F(C) < F(C ∖ {e}) for any e ∈ C ∖ S₀ (nonempty).
  31| * A removes a truth (A = C ∖ {i} or (C ∖ {i}) ∪ {l}, i ∈ S₀, l ∉ C): S₀ ⊄ A, so TL gives F(A) < F(C) < F(C ∖ {e}).
  32| * A = (C ∖ {e}) ∪ {l} with e ∈ C ∖ S₀, l ∉ C: T := C ∖ {e} ∈ 𝓛, |T| < K, l ∉ T, so NA at (T, l) gives
  33|   F(A) < F(C ∖ {e}).
  34| These cases exhaust the neighbours (an addition, a deletion of a truth or of an extra, a swap removing a truth or an
  35| extra). Hence every non-deletion neighbour, and every truth deletion, has F strictly below the largest extra
  36| deletion, which itself exceeds F(C).
  37| (b) A neighbour of S₀ is an addition (NA at (S₀, l); |S₀| ≤ |Q| ≤ K, and additions exist only if |S₀| < K), or a
  38| deletion or swap, which removes a truth (S₀ consists of truths): TL at T = S₀. ∎
  39| 
  40| ## Lemma L1.2 (the path and the capped search)
  41| 
  42| On NA(𝓛) ∩ TL(𝓛), for every centre C ∈ 𝓛:
  43| (i) the uncapped greedy path C = S⁰, S¹, … (scan-maximiser, lexicographic ties, move only on strict improvement)
  44| satisfies S^{t+1} = S^t ∖ {e_t} with e_t ∈ S^t ∖ S₀, F(S⁰) < F(S¹) < …, and reaches S₀ after exactly
  45| τ(C) = |C ∖ S₀| moves; it stops at S₀ (no strict improvement there);
  46| (ii) the capped production search from C (cap ℓ moves, then one further scan) performs the same scans and moves up to
  47| its cap; it scores S₀ whenever ℓ ≥ |C ∖ S₀| − 1 (if C = S₀, S₀ is the emitted centre, scored by OP-LS0 — LS0 scores its own centre — as in GEN L5.2; R10 S5); if ℓ ≥ |C ∖ S₀| its endpoint
  48| is S₀, reached with a completed scan finding no strict improvement, without `local_limit`.
  49| 
  50| *Proof.* (i) Induction on t with L1.1(a): if S^t ∈ 𝓛 ∖ {S₀}, the scan maximisers are deletions of extras, the tie
  51| rule picks one of them, S^{t+1} ∈ 𝓛 and |S^{t+1} ∖ S₀| = |S^t ∖ S₀| − 1. After |C ∖ S₀| moves the state is S₀; by
  52| L1.1(b) the scan at S₀ finds no strict improvement.
  53| (ii) The capped search coincides with the uncapped path while the move count is below ℓ (GEN L4.1(iii), whose proof
  54| uses only the search semantics). S₀ = S^τ is a scanned neighbour of S^{τ−1}; the scan at S^{τ−1} happens iff
  55| τ − 1 ≤ ℓ (inside the loop if τ − 1 < ℓ, as the one further scan if τ − 1 = ℓ). If ℓ ≥ τ, the τ-th move is made and
  56| the next scan (inside the loop or the final one) finds no strict improvement by L1.1(b). ∎
  57| 
  58| **Remarks.** (1) No margin between moves and no bound on |Q| enters this lemma; the move count is linear in the
  59| number of extras (GEN's bound was 2^{v̄} − 1). (2) The lemma is the growing-lattice form of T37R Lemma 2(b); NA there
  60| is required only for |P′| ≤ d. (3) Ties between equal-F extra deletions are broken lexicographically; which extra
  61| goes first is irrelevant for the count.
</file>

 169| ## 2. Removing the selection of conditioning sets

 171| For all l outside Q define the deterministic neighborhood

 173|     H_l={j: dist(j,{l} union S0)<=R_n},

 180|     h_{U,l}=n (RSS_U-RSS_{U+l})/RSS_U
 181|            =n Corr_sample(W_l,Y | W_U)^2.                       (6.3)
 182| 
 183| These expressions use Y before its final response scaling; the correlation
 184| is invariant to that scaling and all column scalings. On the events used
 185| here the residual variances are positive.

 187| **Lemma L6.3. PROVED (by this seat, unchecked).** On A_cov, uniformly over
 188| l outside Q and ALL U not containing l with |U|<=15,
 189| 
 190|     |h_{U,l}-h_{U intersect H_l,l}| <= ϖ_n,
 191|     ϖ_n=C (log n)^{3/2}/sqrt(n) -> 0,
 192|     h_{U,l} <= C log n.                                        (6.4)
 193| 
 194| *Proof.* Put U0=U intersect H_l, V=U minus U0. In the population,
 195| conditional covariance of W_l with any W_v, v in V, given W_U0 is at most
 196| r^{|l-v|}<=r^{R_n}<=n^{-2}. Likewise conditional covariance of Y with W_v
 197| is at most C sum_{j in S0 minus U0}r^{|j-v|}<=C n^{-2}, using P4 and the
 198| bounded coefficients theta_j/t_j. Noise has zero population covariance.
 199| The population residual correlation of W_l and Y given U0 is at most
 200| C r^{d_n}<=C n^{-1/2}: P4 applies for every truth not in U0, and residual
 201| variances have fixed positive lower bounds.
 202| 
 203| Let a,b be the sample vectors of partial correlations of W_l and Y,
 204| respectively, with W_V given U0, and R their sample conditional correlation
 205| matrix. Lemma L6.2 gives ||a||+||b||<=C ħ_n, ||R^{-1}||<=C, uniformly.
 206| The inverse bound follows also directly from Schur complements of the
 207| bounded-size joint Gram. The exact recursive correlation formula is
 208| 
 209|     z_U=(z_0-a'R^{-1}b)/sqrt((1-a'R^{-1}a)(1-b'R^{-1}b)),

 211| where z_0=Corr_sample(W_l,Y|U0). Thus |z_U-z_0|<=C ħ_n^2, and

 223| **Lemma L6.4. PROVED (by this seat, unchecked).** There are constants C,c>0

 233|                        h_{U,l}>=t},

 245| *Proof.* All index sets in this paragraph are deterministic. Let
 246| D=U0 union S0 and regress the raw population coordinate W_l on W_D:

 248|     W_l=W_U0 b + m_raw + e,
 249|     m_raw=sum_{j in S0 minus U0} alpha_j
 250|                 (W_j-W_U0 b_j).

 252| Here b is the population regression of W_l on U0, b_j that of W_j
 253| on U0, and alpha is the regression on the truth residuals. P4 gives
 254| each residual covariance with l absolute value <=r^{d_n}; the conditional
 255| truth covariance has eigenvalues >=c_-, by the Schur complement lower
 256| bound of Sigma. Hence ||alpha||<=C r^{d_n}. The coefficients b_j are

 260|     m=(I-P_U0) C m_raw has ||m||<=C sqrt(n) r^{d_n}<=C.          (6.8)

 262| The innovation e is independent of W_D, has independent N(0,tau^2)
 263| entries, and c_-<=tau^2<=1. Conditional on W_D and eps, the residual
 264| r_Y=(I-P_U0)Y is fixed: standardizing the TRUE columns uses only W_D.
 265| In the subspace V=1-perp intersect span(CW_U0)-perp, of dimension
 266| d=N-|U0|, the vector g=(I-P_U0)Ce is isotropic Gaussian with variance
 267| tau^2. Except on an event of conditional probability exp(-c n),
 268| ||g||>=c sqrt(n). On that event and the column norm event in (6.8),

 270|     sqrt(h_{U0,l})
 271|       <= (1+C/sqrt(n)) sqrt(n) |(g/||g||)' (r_Y/||r_Y||)| + C. (6.9)

 273| This follows from ||g+m||>=||g||-||m|| and Cauchy–Schwarz for m.
 274| Zero residual Y has probability zero; alternatively define its statistic
 275| as zero, which cannot enlarge the upper tail.

 278| G. Its direction is uniform on the sphere and
 279| sqrt(n)|(g/||g||)'v|=sqrt(n)|G'v|/||G||. The chi-square mgf bound of

 282|     P(||G||<sqrt(d)(1-n^{-1/4})) <= C exp(-c sqrt(n)).

 391| ## 5. NA with approximate local innovations
 392| 
 393| **Lemma L6.6. PROVED (by this seat, unchecked).** P(NA(L))->1.
 394| 
 395| *Proof.* For each deterministic T in L and l notin T, let a,b be its
 396| nearest indices on either side of l (either can be absent). Population
 397| Markov regression gives
 398| 
 399|     W_l=c_a W_a+c_b W_b+e_{l,a,b},
 400| 
 401| where e_{l,a,b} is independent of the entire W_T, has iid Gaussian
 402| entries with variance tau_{l,a,b}^2 in [c_-,1]. Consequently, with
 403| g_{l,a,b}=C e_{l,a,b},
 404| 
 405|     (I-P_T)CW_l=(I-P_T)g_{l,a,b}.                             (6.13)
 406| 
 407| This is exact. The coefficients are population coefficients, not sample
 408| regression coefficients. Column standardization does not affect the
 409| normalized direction in (6.13).
 410| 
 411| There are at most p(q+1)^2 innovations. Gaussian chi-square concentration
 412| and a union bound give min ||g||>=c sqrt(n) with probability tending
 413| to one. For each (T,l), conditional on W_T,
 414| 
 415|     ||P_T g_{l,a,b}||^2/tau_{l,a,b}^2 ~ chi^2_{|T|}.
 416| 
 417| There are at most p 2^{q-s0}=n^{O(1)} pairs and |T|<=q<=C log n.
 418| The mgf bound
 419| P(chi^2_d>v)<=2^{d/2}exp(-v/4) and a sufficiently large v=C'log n
 420| therefore imply, uniformly, ||P_Tg||<=C sqrt(log n) with probability
 421| tending to one. Also ||P_T eps||<=||P_Q eps||<=C sigma sqrt(log n)
 422| simultaneously, by conditional chi-square concentration given X.
 423| 
 424| Define Z^0_{l,a,b}=g_{l,a,b}'eps/(sigma ||g_{l,a,b}||). Given the RAW
 425| matrix W each is a standard normal, because g is a W-measurable linear
 426| combination of raw columns and eps is independent of W. (The raw scales
 427| need not be measurable in standardized X; no such claim is needed.)
 428| A conditional union bound given W, then integration, gives
 429| 
 430|     max (Z^0)^2 <= 2log(2p(q+1)^2)+2log log n                    (6.14)
 431| 
 432| with failure probability at most 1/log n. No independence between
 433| the different Z^0 variables is needed.
 434| 
 435| Let h=(I-P_T)g. Subtracting the two normalized noise inner products,
 436| 
 437|     |Z_{T,l}-Z^0_{l,a,b}|
 438|       <= |Z^0| (||g||/||h||-1)
 439|           + ||P_Teps|| ||P_Tg||/(sigma ||h||).
 440| 
 441| On the preceding events ||h||^2=||g||^2-||P_Tg||^2>=c n,
 442| ||g||/||h||-1=O(log n/n). Equations (6.14) and p<=n^A give
 443| 
 444|     max_{T,l}|Z_{T,l}-Z^0_{l,a,b}|=O(log n/sqrt(n)),
 445|     max_{T,l} Z_{T,l}^2 <= 2log p+O(log log n)+o(1).            (6.15)
 446| 
 447| The L2.2 threshold is
 448| c_n=log(n+1)+2log p-2log(q+1)-4 kappa_E-2. Its excess over
 449| the right side in (6.15) tends to infinity, since q=O(log n).
 450| L2.2 on A_score proves NA. The exact fixed-design direction family
 451| may be exponentially larger; the proof bounds a uniform error to a
 452| small reference family instead of asserting (G4-dir). QED.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

 148| ## 5. Frontier (characterised; claims only where proved)
 149| * **Unrestricted span vs capped feasibility.** If rank X_{c,𝒞} = N then r = 0 for every μ_c (no residual outside the
 150|   unrestricted candidate span) — but μ_c may still have no feasible (|S| ≤ K) or sparse representation; p_𝒞 ≥ n alone

 152|   representability, outside T03♯.
 153| * **Why T02(i♯) does not port.** The numerator identity E_true[m^c_b(S)/f_true] = 1 survives misspecification (any fixed
 154|   rate b, any positive true density); what fails is the denominator lower bound (Lemma den′), proved for the pure-noise
 155|   residual. For the full contrast experiment, the candidate densities can inflate their scalar variance to ≈ σ² + Δ_n but cannot represent the
 156|   orthogonal mean r, which costs a likelihood/KL loss of order N:
 157|   log[m^c_b(S)/f₀] ≤ −(N/2)log(1 + Δ_n/σ²)(1 + o_P(1)) uniformly in S ⊆ 𝒞 when Δ_n ≥ Δ₀ > 0 and d_n/N → 0 (Lemma O2).
 158|   This is an obstruction to that denominator strategy only, not a failure of posterior consistency. Reduced-experiment
 159|   variants (loss ≍ d_n[log(v/σ²) + σ²/v − 1]/2 in the candidate span) are conjectural.

   1| # L5 — Frontier: what is not covered and why
   2| 
   3| Status (per claim): Lemma O1 — R03 VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS (applied); Lemma O2 — R03 VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS (its
   4| original consequence paragraph was GAP/FALSE and was replaced); §6 Examples E2, E3 — added after R04, R05 VERIFIED;
   5| §§3–5 remarks/conjectures, not claims. Sweep R06 fixes applied. Council pending.
   6| 
   7| ## §1 A nonzero residual outside the unrestricted candidate span requires rank X_𝒞 < N
   8| 
   9| **Lemma O1.** If rank X_{c,𝒞} = N, then every full mean μ_c ∈ ℝ^N lies in the *unrestricted* span col X_{c,𝒞}: any
  10| representation μ_c = X_{c,𝒞}θ + r with X_{c,𝒞}ᵀr = 0 has r = 0. *Proof.* col X_{c,𝒞} = ℝ^N and r ⊥ ℝ^N. ∎
  11| (p_𝒞 ≥ n alone does not imply rank N.) Consequence. For a full-rank candidate design there is no residual outside the
  12| unrestricted span, but μ_c may still have no *feasible* (|S| ≤ K ≈ n/2) or *sparse* representation: there
  13| "the candidate set misses a true variable" means a question of sparse/capped representability (approximate sparsity),
  14| outside T03♯ (exact s₀-sparse truth). EP with r = 0 and a sparse θ^𝒞 is of course possible (then it is the
  15| well-specified case). GR (Theorem MIS) restores a *well-specified* conditional Gaussian candidate regression for any
  16| p_𝒞; it is *sparse* only under the separately assumed projection-sparsity (fixed s₀^𝒞) — Gaussianity alone does not give
  17| it (e.g. independent standard Gaussian candidates and an omitted variable equal to their sum plus independent noise: every
  18| candidate has a nonzero projected coefficient).
  19| 
  20| ## §2 Why T02(i♯) (the size tail) does not port to EP
  21| 
  22| What survives: the numerator identity E_true[m^c_b(S)/f_true] = 1 holds for every fixed rate b and every positive true
  23| density ([P1] lem:num), misspecified or not. What fails is the denominator lower bound (Lemma den′), which was proved for
  24| the true model with a pure-noise residual. Lemma O2 below is an obstruction to *that denominator strategy* only (the candidate densities can inflate their scalar
  25| variance to ≈ σ² + Δ_n but cannot represent the orthogonal mean r); it says
  26| nothing against posterior consistency under EP.
  27| 
  28| T02(i♯) (T03R §2, `PROOF.md:74-99`) bounds π(|S| > m | y) by a ratio whose numerator has E₀[I_{b₋}(E_m)/f₀(y_c)] =
  29| ϖ(E_m) ([P1] `lem:num`; an identity valid under **any** true density f₀) and whose denominator is a lower bound on
  30| m^c_{b₊}(S₀)/f₀(y_c) ≥ (n+1)^{−s₀/2}c_IG σ*² n^{−1/2}e^{−Λ_n} (Lemma den′, `PROOF.md:89-91`), proved for the
  31| true model S₀ and the true variance.
  32| 
  33| **Lemma O2 (the denominator is exponentially small under EP).** Assume EP, G, rank X_{c,𝒞} =: d_n with d_n/N → 0,
  34| and Δ_n ≥ Δ₀ > 0. Then for every rate b′ > 0 and every S ⊆ 𝒞, with f₀ = N_N(μ_c, σ²I),
  35|   log[m^c_{b′}(S)(y_c)/f₀(y_c)] ≤ −(N/2)·log(1 + Δ_n/σ²)·(1 + o_P(1)),
  36| uniformly in S ⊆ 𝒞 and b′ (the o_P(1) term does not depend on S or b′).
  37| *Proof.* m^c_{b′}(S) is a mixture over (β, v) of N_N(X_{c,S}β, vI) densities (ridge slab N(0, nv(G_S + I)⁻¹) on β given v, and IG(a₀ + ½, b′) = IG(0.51, b′) on v in the contrast experiment;
  38| [P1] §"Integral representation", `PROOF_v3.tex:52-56,340-342`; SoP `02_method.tex:127-130`), so it is at most sup_{β, v>0} N_N(y_c; X_{c,S}β, vI) = (2πv̂_S)^{−N/2}e^{−N/2},
  39| v̂_S := ‖(I − P_S)y_c‖²/N. Let V := col X_{c,𝒞}. Since P_V ⪰ P_S and (I − P_V)μ^𝒞 = 0, r ∈ V^⊥:
  40| N v̂_S ≥ ‖(I − P_V)y_c‖² = ‖r + (I − P_V)e‖² = ‖r‖² + 2rᵀe + ‖(I − P_V)e‖².
  41| ‖(I − P_V)e‖²/σ² ~ χ²_{N−d_n}, rᵀe ~ N(0, σ²‖r‖²); so v̂_S ≥ Δ_n + σ²(1 − d_n/N) − O_P(√(1/N)) − O_P(√(Δ_n/N))
  42| = σ²_{𝒞,n}(1 − o_P(1)) uniformly in S. And f₀(y_c) = (2πσ²)^{−N/2}exp(−‖e‖²/(2σ²)) with ‖e‖²/σ² = N + O_P(√N).
  43| Hence log(m/f₀) ≤ −(N/2)log(v̂_S/σ²) + (‖e‖²/σ² − N)/2 ≤ −(N/2)log(σ²_{𝒞,n}/σ²) + o_P(N), and
  44| log(σ²_{𝒞,n}/σ²) = log(1 + Δ_n/σ²) ≥ log(1 + Δ₀/σ²) > 0. ∎
  45| **Consequence for the technique (replaced after R03; the earlier draft's posterior bound and its "vacuous for every
  46| m ≤ K" claim were a GAP and FALSE respectively).** O2 rules out the polynomial lower bound with a tight exponent used by
  47| den′ in the full experiment. For Δ_n bounded away from zero, a method using only the numerator's mean and a single S₀
  48| denominator incurs an exponential denominator loss. At a nonempty logarithmic cutoff m = O(log n), T03R E1(c) gives
  49| log R_m = −o(n), so the prior factor cannot compensate for that loss. This obstructs that particular route to TAIL^𝒞 at
  50| logarithmic cutoffs. It does not establish an upper bound on posterior tail mass, nor a sharp necessary cutoff for
  51| arbitrary m (R03 exhibits a duplicate-column design where the same route does work at m = K − 1). TAIL^𝒞 for growing
  52| p_𝒞 is discharged here by a different route — Lemma T / Corollary F(b) under (TL) — and for bounded p_𝒞 by
  53| Corollary F(a); the window below (TL) remains open.
  54| 
  55| ## §3 Repair routes (conjectures, not attempted to completion)
  56| (a) **Sufficiency reduction.** π_𝒞(· | y) depends on y_c only through (P_V y_c, ‖(I − P_V)y_c‖²). Performing the T02(i♯)
  57| change of measure in the reduced experiment replaces the e^{−cN} loss by e^{−c d_n} (variance mismatch σ² vs σ²_{𝒞,n} in
  58| d_n directions; the 1-dimensional residual statistic costs O(1) after matching means). This would give TAIL^𝒞 when
  59| d_n = O(log n). Not proved.
  60| (b) **Large-Δ direct sums — SUPERSEDED by Lemma T (L4.9), which proves a stronger version of this route (no eigenvalue
  61| condition beyond S₀^𝒞, threshold (TL)).** Original remark: When Δ_n ≥ (1 + ε)σ², the superset exponent (n/2)σ²χ²_j/(2b + Q) is ≤ tχ²_j with
  62| t < ½ uniformly over sizes up to K (because 2b + Q^c_S ≥ ‖r‖² + 2rᵀe), so E e^{tχ²_j} = (1 − 2t)^{−j/2} without
  63| truncation and the superset sum over all sizes ≤ K converges under SE_w(K; g₀); with (C6)(a) this would give TAIL^𝒞.
  64| Not proved (the uniform control of 2b + Q over all S ⊆ 𝒞 of size ≤ K is the step to write).
  65| 
  66| ## §4 Outside GR: non-Gaussian or heteroscedastic omitted residual
  67| SL Theorem 4 covers a fixed-size candidate set under a general random design via the KL projection (SL §2.3). For our
  68| prior and p_𝒞 ≤ n^A nothing is claimed. Numerics N5 (ω = x₀² − 1 and ω = x₀x₁ − 0.3 with Gaussian candidates, whose
  69| linear projections on x_𝒞 vanish) show substantial finite-sample posterior mass on {3, 4} in these runs (median
  70| π = 0.962 / 0.966 at n = 6400; mean PIP of a non-target candidate up to 0.13) — exploratory evidence consistent with a
  71| possible KL-projection extension; no convergence or rate conclusion follows.
  72| 
  73| ## §5 Fixed design without exact projection
  74| If P_𝒞μ is not exactly sparse but is "sparse plus small", the residual signal leaks into extra candidates with
  75| noncentral χ² terms; a GEN-type leakage condition (NL_η / NL_avg, GEN `STATEMENT.md` §2 (H2c)) would be the natural
  76| hypothesis. Not attempted.
  77| 
  78| ## §6 Boundary examples: why GR and EP cannot simply be deleted (from R04; R05 VERIFIED)
  79| 
  80| **Example E2 (Gaussian marginals are not enough for GR).** n even ≥ 4; deterministic centred orthogonal raw candidate
  81| columns x₁, x₂ with ‖x_j‖² = n and x₂ᵢ = ±1 (balanced); Z ~ N(0, 1) independent of ε ~ N_n(0, I); omitted column
  82| x_k := Z x₂; y^r = x₁ + x_k + ε. The omitted contribution ω = Zx₂ has E[ω] = 0, Gaussian marginals with identical
  83| variance 1, but covariance x₂x₂ᵀ (rank one), so GR fails. A "mean-only" projection prescription (E[ω | X_𝒞] = 0) would
  84| target {1}. Conditionally on Z = z ≠ 0, the candidate problem is a G-model (fixed design, σ² = 1) with raw coefficients
  85| (1, z); standardisation rescales them by √(n/N); the T03♯ hypotheses hold (orthogonal design, p_𝒞 = 2, fixed nonzero
  86| coefficients ⇒ BM-∞), so π_𝒞({1, 2} | y) → 1 in probability given Z = z. Since P(Z = 0) = 0, integrating over z
  87| (dominated convergence for the bounded conditional probabilities) gives π_𝒞({1} | y) → 0 in probability under the joint
  88| law. So the covariance/independence content of GR matters: a common random omitted slope defeats the transfer.
  89| (Not an iid-row counterexample to Song–Liang; it violates their iid-row setting.)
  90| 
  91| **Example E3 (dropping EP for a fixed sparse target).** Fixed orthogonal candidates x₁, x₂ (X_𝒞ᵀX_𝒞 = N·I),
  92| μ_c = bx₁ + cx₂ + r with b, c ≠ 0 fixed and r ⊥ span X_𝒞, ‖r‖² ≤ MN. If one names the fixed target {1} (i.e. treats cx₂
  93| as part of a non-orthogonal "remainder" bx₁-residual r′ := cx₂ + r, which violates EP for the target {1}), the posterior
  94| does not concentrate on {1}: EP holds for the target {1, 2} with θ^𝒞 = (b, c), and Corollary F(a) (p_𝒞 = 2; BM-∞ since
  95| b, c are fixed; SE trivially) gives π_𝒞({1, 2} | y) → 1, hence π_𝒞({1} | y) → 0. So the orthogonality in EP is what
  96| identifies the target; it cannot be dropped for a pre-named target.
  97| (Neither example shows that GR or EP is necessary for *every* consistency theorem; they show the present transfer and
  98| proof cannot be generalised by deleting those hypotheses.)

(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step

(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

   6| non-cancellation) are not checkable (θ* unknown) and are not assessed; the only plug-in numbers (riboflavin, diabetes

  68|    |r| > 0.5 are split across the method's blocks (blocks of size ≤ B = 8 cannot hold a pervasive cluster).
  69|    *FRED-QD / FRED-MD*: a common factor (21–27%) plus tight local clusters (interest-rate spreads, manufacturing
  70|    employment aggregates) with exact φ²(3) ≈ 1.9e-5 / 9.1e-5 — "factor + local".
  71|    Reading: posterior level — POST applies to factor designs whose population correlation matrix has a fixed floor;
  72|    reported model — outside the proved local classes. Dense cross-block marginal correlation motivates, but does not
  73|    establish, Lemma VN's conditional visibility hypotheses (marginal correlation can coexist with zero partial
  74|    correlation); only the quantified models V1–V4 carry the proved route obstruction [R07 #8]. FAC-A/B are the
  75|    relevant tickets.

  77| 3. **Smooth-curve / functional, near-collinear.** *tecator*: one component carries 98.6% of the trace, adjacent

  79|    mutually correlated at |r| ≈ 0.9999. Observed: extreme near-collinearity. Not claimed: exclusion from the fixed-floor
  80|    classes — that would require a specified grid-refinement sequence (population process, grid, normalisation) with a
  81|    proved vanishing sparse floor, which is not supplied; a fixed 100-variable correlation matrix (or independent copies
  82|    of it) does have a fixed positive floor [R07 #4]. Reading: if the relevant asymptotic model is a densely refined
  83|    smooth curve, a functional theory would be needed; this ticket does not decide it.

  85| ## What this says about applicability (summary for HQ)
  86| * Of eight standard public designs, three (spam, digits, diabetes-quadratic) show **local** correlation of the kind
  87|   covered by the posterior theorem and by Theorem LOC's class (digits is an image; growing 2-D grids are outside LOC's
  88|   proved scope); four (riboflavin, iclaims, FRED-QD, FRED-MD) are **pervasive factor** designs — posterior theory
  89|   applies to their class; reported-model theory for growing-p versions: FAC-A's class (one factor + bounded blocks, p ≲ n^{1/6}) where it
  90|   applies, otherwise open (iclaims, p = 10: exact branch, ENUM). With p FIXED, all eight designs are eventually on the

   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**. Check record: R02 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol high,

   8| ## Setting

  10| (A ≥ 1 fixed, p ≫ n allowed, p ≥ max(2, s₀); p = 1 means s₀ = 1, Ω = {∅, {1}}, and only R and BM matter — omitted), X = centred, sample-standardised design, R̂ := XᵀX/(n − 1) (the sample
  11| correlation matrix), Y = Xθ* + Cε with fixed S₀, |S₀| = s₀, θ*_j ∈ [θ_lo, θ_hi] in absolute value on S₀, θ* = 0 off S₀,
  12| ε ~ N(0, σ²I) independent of the raw design. (Raw-scale convention, fixed raw slopes with |β_j| ∈ [b_lo, b_hi] and unit population variances [R02-3]: then
  13| θ* = D_xβ is raw-design-measurable; use the raw-design event 𝒢_n ∩ ℋ_n, ℋ_n := {all sample/population sd ratios in
  14| [½, 2]} (P(ℋ_n) → 1 by χ² tails and p ≤ n^A), take θ_lo = b_lo/2, θ_hi = 2b_hi, and run the diagonal argument over
  15| raw-design sequences; otherwise unchanged.) For the standardised-signal convention: conditionally on X, Y is
  16| Gaussian on the centred contrast space with mean Xθ* and noise variance σ², so the posterior's noise kernel depends
  17| only on X and the supremum over standardised designs below is legitimate [R02-4] (model G with β := D_x⁻¹θ*, which is
  18| raw-design-measurable, not X-measurable).
  19| 
  20| Write j₀ := ⌈(2A + 1)s₀⌉ + 1 and
  21|   m̄_n := ⌈[s₀(A log n + log 2) + log 2 + ((s₀ + 2)/2) log n] / log(3/2)⌉,  k̄_n := min(p, s₀ + max(j₀, m̄_n)).
  22| 
  23| **Hypothesis LSF (logarithmic sparse floor).** (i) λ_min(Σ_{n,S}) ≥ φ² for every S with |S| ≤ min(p, s₀ + j₀),
  24| for a fixed φ ∈ (0, 1]; and (ii) λ_min(Σ_{n,S}) ≥ ψ_n for every S with |S| ≤ k̄_n, where
  25| ψ_n √n/(log n)^{3/2} → ∞. (If λ_min(Σ_n) ≥ c > 0 for all n, both hold with φ² = ψ_n = c.)
  26| 
  27| ## Lemma POST
  28| **(a)** Under LSF there are X-measurable events 𝒜_n with P(𝒜_n) → 1 on which every design satisfies the T03♯
  29| hypotheses R (with M := s₀²θ_hi² + 1 and φ₀² := φ²/2), SE_λ(j₀) (φ₀²), SE_w(m♯_n; g₀) (g₀ := 1), s₀ ≤ K, and BM-∞ with
  30| the deterministic envelope θ_lo² nφ₀²/(σ² log n) → ∞ — with these common constants and envelope, for n ≥ n₀.
  31| **(b)** Consequently, under the joint law of (raw design, ε): 1 − π(S₀) = O_P(√(log n/n)), and the conclusions of
  32| SL1 (a)–(e) hold with r_n = √(log n/n) (PIP sure screening and specificity uniformly in j, MPM, ξ_q for fixed q ∈ (0, 1) or
  33| deterministic q_n with r_n = o(min(q_n, 1 − q_n)) only, exact HPM, model size); without beta-min (θ*_j allowed to vary, some → 0) the inclusion clause for J_n(c) holds likewise.
  34| **(c)** (Fixed exact-Gram designs.) If XᵀX = (n − 1)Σ_n exactly (p ≤ n − 1) and LSF(i) holds with ψ_n ≥ 1/(n − 1) in
  35| (ii), the T03♯ hypotheses hold deterministically with φ₀² = φ², g₀ = 1.
  36|

   1| # L2 — Combes–Thomas bound and uniform conditional-covariance decay
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**. Check record: R02 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol high,
   4| `reviews/R02_L1L2_check_sol.md`): VERIFIED (one NIT, applied in §L2.3).
   5| Falsification numerics: `numerics/ct_check.py` → `numerics/ct_check_out.txt`.
   6| 
   7| ## L2.1 Combes–Thomas lemma (finite matrices on integer positions)
   8| 
   9| **Lemma CT.** Let I be a finite index set and x : I → ℤ injective ("positions"); write d_ij := |x_i − x_j|. Let A be
  10| a real symmetric matrix on I with spectrum in [α, β], α > 0, and |A_ij| ≤ K e^{−a d_ij} for all i ≠ j, with K > 0,
  11| a > 0. Put
  12|   u := [α/(4K) + 1/(e^a − 1)]⁻¹,   t* := a − log(1 + u)  (so 0 < t* < a).
  13| Then for all i, j ∈ I:  |(A⁻¹)_ij| ≤ (2/α) e^{−t* d_ij}.
  14| 
  15| *Proof.* (i) *The constant.* For 0 ≤ t < a let S(t) := 2K Σ_{d≥1} e^{−ad}(e^{td} − 1) = 2K[1/(e^{a−t} − 1) − 1/(e^a − 1)],
  16| continuous and strictly increasing on [0, a), S(0) = 0, S(t) → ∞ as t ↑ a. Solving S(t) = α/2 gives
  17| 1/(e^{a−t} − 1) = α/(4K) + 1/(e^a − 1) = 1/u, i.e. t = t*. Since 1/u > 1/(e^a − 1), u < e^a − 1, so t* > 0; and
  18| u > 0 gives t* < a. Hence S(t*) = α/2.
  19| (ii) *Conjugation.* Fix t ∈ {t*, −t*} and D := diag(e^{t x_i}). A_t := DAD⁻¹ has entries A_ij e^{t(x_i − x_j)}.
  20| E := A_t − A has zero diagonal and |E_ij| = |A_ij| |e^{t(x_i − x_j)} − 1| ≤ K e^{−a d_ij}(e^{t* d_ij} − 1), using
  21| |e^{s} − 1| ≤ e^{|s|} − 1 for real s.
  22| (iii) *Schur test.* For every i, since x is injective at most two j satisfy d_ij = d for each d ≥ 1, so
  23| Σ_j |E_ij| ≤ S(t*) = α/2; the same bound holds for column sums (the bound is symmetric in i, j). Hence
  24| ‖E‖₂ ≤ √(‖E‖₁‖E‖_∞) ≤ α/2.
  25| (iv) *Inverse.* A is symmetric with λ_min(A) ≥ α, so ‖A⁻¹‖₂ ≤ 1/α and ‖A⁻¹E‖₂ ≤ ½. Thus A_t = A(I + A⁻¹E) is
  26| invertible and ‖A_t⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂/(1 − ½) ≤ 2/α. Since A_t⁻¹ = DA⁻¹D⁻¹, its (i, j) entry is (A⁻¹)_ij e^{t(x_i − x_j)},
  27| and every entry of a matrix is bounded in absolute value by its spectral norm. Choosing the sign of t so that
  28| t(x_i − x_j) = t* d_ij gives |(A⁻¹)_ij| e^{t* d_ij} ≤ 2/α. ∎
  29| 
  30| Remarks. (1) β is not used: only the lower spectral bound and the off-diagonal decay matter. (2) The bound is
  31| uniform in |I| and in the particular positions (only injectivity into ℤ is used). (3) Diagonal entries satisfy the
  32| sharper |(A⁻¹)_ii| ≤ 1/α.
  33| 
  34| ## L2.2 Uniform conditional decay for the class LOC
  35| 
  36| **Definition (class LOC(c, C, K, a)).** A unit-diagonal p × p covariance matrix Σ with spectrum in [c, C]
  37| (0 < c ≤ 1 ≤ C < ∞) for which there is a bijection π : [p] → [p] such that **either** (LOC-Σ) |Σ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a|π(j) − π(k)|}
  38| for j ≠ k, **or** (LOC-Θ) the precision Θ := Σ⁻¹ satisfies |Θ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a|π(j) − π(k)|} for j ≠ k. Write
  39| d(j, k) := |π(j) − π(k)|. For a sequence Σ_n the constants (c, C, K, a) are fixed; π = π_n may vary with n.
  40| 
  41| **Lemma CD (conditional decay).** Let Σ ∈ LOC(c, C, K, a) and W ~ N(0, Σ). Define
  42|   under (LOC-Σ): t₁ := t*(α = c, K, a), K₁ := 2/c;   under (LOC-Θ): t₁ := a, K₁ := K;
  43|   t₂ := t*(α = 1/C, K₁, t₁),  K₂ := 2C.
  44| Then for every U ⊆ [p] and all distinct j, k ∉ U:
  45|   (a) |Cov(W_j, W_k | W_U)| ≤ K₂ e^{−t₂ d(j,k)};
  46|   (b) c ≤ Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ 1, and every conditional covariance matrix Cov(W_V | W_U) (V ⊆ [p] ∖ U) has spectrum in
  47|       [c, C];
  48|   (c) under (LOC-Θ), Σ itself satisfies (LOC-Σ) with constants (2C, t*(1/C, K, a)); under (LOC-Σ), Θ satisfies
  49|       (LOC-Θ) with (2/c, t*(c, K, a)).
  50| The constants (K₂, t₂) depend only on (c, C, K, a), not on p, U, j, k or π.
  51| 
  52| *Proof.* Θ has spectrum in [1/C, 1/c]. Under (LOC-Σ), Lemma CT applied to Σ (positions π, α = c) gives
  53| |Θ_jk| ≤ (2/c)e^{−t₁ d(j,k)} for all j, k; this is (c) second half. Under (LOC-Θ) the bound |Θ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a d} holds
  54| by assumption for j ≠ k, and Lemma CT applied to Θ (α = 1/C) gives (c) first half. In both cases |Θ_jk| ≤ K₁e^{−t₁ d(j,k)}
  55| for j ≠ k. Let V := [p] ∖ U. For Gaussian W, Cov(W_V | W_U) = (Θ_VV)⁻¹ (block inversion). Θ_VV is a principal
  56| submatrix of Θ, so its spectrum lies in [1/C, 1/c] (Rayleigh quotients); its off-diagonal entries obey the same bound
  57| with positions π|_V (still injective). Lemma CT with α = 1/C gives (a). For (b): the spectrum of (Θ_VV)⁻¹ lies in
  58| [c, C]; in particular Var(W_j | W_U) = ((Θ_VV)⁻¹)_jj ≥ c, and Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ Var(W_j) = 1. For sub-vectors
  59| V′ ⊆ V, Cov(W_{V′} | W_U) is a principal submatrix of Cov(W_V | W_U), so its spectrum lies in [c, C] too. ∎
  60| 
  61| ## L2.3 Sufficient conditions (used in L4_families)
  62| 
  63| (i) **Banded Σ** (|Σ_jk| = 0 for d(j,k) > b) with spectrum in [c, C]: (LOC-Σ) holds with K := e^{ab} for any a > 0
  64| (take a = 1, K = e^{b}), because |Σ_jk| ≤ 1 ≤ e^{b − d} for d ≤ b. (ii) **Banded Θ** (Gaussian Markov random field
  65| on a line with range b, e.g. causal AR(b)) with spectrum of Σ in [c, C]: (LOC-Θ) with a = 1, K := e^{b}/c
  66| (|Θ_jk| ≤ ‖Θ‖ ≤ 1/c). (iii) **Block-diagonal** Σ with blocks of size ≤ g, ordered consecutively by π: banded with
  67| b = g − 1. (iv) **Stationary Toeplitz** Σ_jk = γ(|j − k|)/γ(0) with |γ(h)/γ(0)| ≤ K′ρ^h (ρ < 1) and spectrum in [c, C]:
  68| (LOC-Σ) with a = log(1/ρ), K = K′ (normalisation aligned with L4 (c), C1-Opus-8). For AR(1) with parameter 0 < |ρ| < 1 (ρ = 0 is Σ = I: LOC with any fixed K, a > 0; sequences need fixed |ρ| bounded
  69| away from 1 — no unit-root limits) [R02-5]: Σ_jk = ρ^{|j−k|}, spectrum in
  70| [(1 − |ρ|)/(1 + |ρ|), (1 + |ρ|)/(1 − |ρ|)] (GROW L5 (P1)), K = 1, a = log(1/|ρ|).

   9| **What this is and is not.** VN is a statement about the start mode γ₀ (the product-of-block-tables start law) and
  10| therefore about the *proof routes* of GEN (bounded centre S̃₀ = S*) and GROW/LOC (sandwich S₀ ⊆ S̃₀ ⊆ Q with
  11| |Q| = O(log n)). It says nothing about whether LS0 or the full method reaches S₀ from a large start mode.

  13| ## L5.0 Setting and statement
  14| Random design as STATEMENT §1 (raw rows iid N(m, Σ_n), Σ_n unit-diagonal, p ≤ n^A, fixed s₀, |θ*_j| ∈ [θ_lo, θ_hi],
  15| Y = Xθ* + Cε, ε independent of the design), and
  16| * (F16) λ_min(Σ_{n,S}) ≥ c > 0 for every S with |S| ≤ 16 + s₀ (fixed c).
  17| Population response (a single population row): Y° := Σ_{k∈S₀}θ*_kW_k + σξ, ξ ~ N(0, 1) independent of W
  18| (STATEMENT writes V for Y°). For a deterministic null set
  19| 𝒩_n ⊆ [p] ∖ S₀ define the **visible-null floor**
  20| * VNF(κ_n): Corr(W_l, Y° | W_U)² ≥ κ_n for every l ∈ 𝒩_n and every U ⊆ [p] ∖ (S₀ ∪ {l}) with |U| ≤ 15,
  21| with nκ_n/log n → ∞.
  22| 
  23| **Lemma VN.** Under (F16) and VNF(κ_n), for any X-measurable partition with blocks of size ≤ 16, with probability
  24| → 1 (joint law) every maximiser S̃ of γ₀ on Ω satisfies
  25|   |S̃| = K  or  S̃ ⊇ 𝒩_n ∖ ⋃{C_b : C_b ∩ S₀ ≠ ∅};
  26| in particular |S̃ ∖ S₀| ≥ min(K − s₀, |𝒩_n| − 15s₀).
  27| 
  28| **Corollary VN-routes.** (i) If |𝒩_n| → ∞, then for every fixed v̄: P(|S̃₀| ≤ v̄) → 0. Hence there are no X-measurable
  29| S*_n with |S*_n| ≤ v̄ such that GEN's (H2) holds with fixed constants on design events of probability → 1: otherwise
  30| GEN (C1) along every deterministic sequence in those events plus the diagonal argument (GEN L5.3) would give
  31| P(S̃₀ = S*_n) → 1. The GEN route ((C3), (C3-fav), (C4)) is unavailable. (ii) If min(K, |𝒩_n|)/log n → ∞, then
  32| for every C_Q and every deterministic Q_n with |Q_n| ≤ C_Q log n: P(S̃₀ ⊆ Q_n) → 0. Hence GROW's (G1) + (G3) cannot hold
  33| with fixed constants on design events of probability → 1 (GROW (C3) would give P(S̃ ⊆ Q) → 1 by the same diagonal
  34| argument), and no sandwich with an O(log n) relevance set — the mechanism of GROW and of Theorem LOC — exists.

  36| ## L5.1 Proof
  37| *Regularity.* Every set of the form {l} ∪ U ∪ S₀ with |U| ≤ 15 has size ≤ 16 + s₀. The argument of [L6] L6.2
  38| (GROW `lemmas/L6_random_AR1.md`; entrywise event for the raw centred columns and the noise column, ħ_n = C_A√(log n/n);
  39| bounded-dimension perturbation of conditional covariances with conditional variances ≥ c by (F16) and residual
  40| variance of Y° ≥ σ²; coefficients θ*_k/t_k within O(ħ_n) of θ*_k) uses only Gaussianity, unit variances and these
  41| floors; it gives an event A_cov, P(A_cov) → 1, on which, uniformly over l ∈ [p] and U ⊆ [p] ∖ (S₀ ∪ {l}), |U| ≤ 15,
  42| the sample partial correlation ρ̂_{U,l} of x_l and Y given X_U satisfies |ρ̂_{U,l} − Corr(W_l, Y° | W_U)| ≤ C ħ_n.
  43| On A_cov and VNF, h_{U,l} := n ρ̂²_{U,l} ≥ n(√κ_n − Cħ_n)² ≥ nκ_n/2 for n ≥ n₀ (ħ_n = o(√κ_n) because
  44| nκ_n/log n → ∞). Also the L0 events for the family of all subsets of [p] of size ≤ 16 hold w.p. → 1 ([L6] §1,
  45| "A_score"; Gram floors from (F16) and the entrywise event; energy ‖μ‖² ≤ s₀²θ_hi²n).
  46| *Block-table increment.* By GROW L0.2(c) (block-table form) and RSS_{U∪{l}}/RSS_U = 1 − h_{U,l}/n:
  47|   log r_b(U ∪ {l}) − log r_b(U) = −½ log(n + 1) − ν log(1 − h_{U,l}/n) + (R_{U∪l} − R_U)
  48|                                 ≥ −½ log(n + 1) + h_{U,l}/2 − 2κ_E,
  49| using −log(1 − x) ≥ x and ν ≥ n/2.

   1| # L6 — Lemma ENUM: the exact-enumeration override (v2, after council round 2)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; added after council round 1 (C1 Sol issue 1); restated in v2 with the coded
   4| inequality as the general condition (C2 Sol issue 1, C2 Opus issue 1). Checked by the round-2 council seats (C2 Sol:
   5| "the new ENUM proof is correct"; C2 Opus: "correct and matches the production code"); council r3: both seats re-derived ENUM, all gates PASS (C3_council_*.md).
   6| 
   7| **Code facts.** After preprocessing (retained columns; for iid Gaussian columns no column is constant or duplicated,
   8| almost surely, so p is the design's p a.s.), the production core decides the branch by the counting inequality
   9|   (EXB)  Σ_{k≤K} C(p, k) ≤ (5H₀ + 4N₀)p,  N₀ = max(2500, n, p),  H₀ = ⌈512N₀/2500⌉,  K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋)
  10| (`Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_preprocess.R:18-27`, counted by `cpp_exact_count`). On the exact branch it enumerates Ω,
  11| scores every model and reports the maximiser of the all-scored set for the strict order (F, −|S|, lex), with provenance
  12| `phase = exact, mechanism = enumeration`, and returns before LS0 (`Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_fit.R:120-125`). Status
  13| `exact` is part of the output event 𝒪 (FIN `s1_setting.tex:24`); a `resource_limit` stop on the exact branch is "no output"
  14| (U_n) and does not affect the lemma, which is stated jointly with 𝒪 [C3-Opus-7].
  15| 
  16| **Lemma ENUM.** (i) **General override.** For any design sequence for which (EXB) holds for all large n (a condition
  17| on (n, p_n) only), under EX-A: if 1 − π(S₀) < ½ then Ŝ⁺ = S₀ whenever the enumeration returns with output. Hence,
  18| whenever POST's conclusion 1 − π(S₀) = o_P(1) holds under the joint law, P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) → 0 and
  19| liminf P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ = S₀}) = 1 − limsup P(U_n). (ii) **Sufficient conditions for (EXB).** (EXB) holds whenever
  20| 2^{p_n} ≤ 4n·p_n, i.e. p_n − log₂ p_n ≤ log₂ n + 2; in particular for every fixed p, for p_n ≤ c log n with c < 1/log 2,
  21| and for 2^{p_n} ≤ n (e.g. p_n = 2⌊log n/(2 log 2)⌋, C2 Sol's example).
  22| 
  23| *Proof.* (ii) Σ_{k≤K}C(p,k) ≤ 2^p and (5H₀ + 4N₀)p ≥ 4N₀p ≥ 4np. For fixed p, 2^p ≤ 4np for n ≥ 2^p/4; for
  24| p_n ≤ c log n, 2^{p_n} ≤ n^{c log 2} ≤ n eventually. (i) If 1 − π(S₀) < ½, S₀ is the unique maximiser of π, i.e.
  25| F(S₀) > F(S) for every S ∈ Ω ∖ {S₀} (SL0(iv)); every model is scored, so the maximum of the all-scored set under
  26| (F, −|S|, lex) is S₀. Thus 𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {1 − π(S₀) ≥ ½} on the exact branch, and P(1 − π(S₀) ≥ ½) → 0. The liminf
  27| identity is the algebra of FIN §5.1 (M5(0) with D_n = 0). ∎
  28| 
  29| **Effect on the map.** Every family row's reported-model status is "covered" for sequences on which (EXB) holds
  30| eventually (given POST's hypotheses); the "unproved" and "route-obstructed" labels refer only to sequences on which
  31| (EXB) fails infinitely often (for which necessarily 2^{p_n} > 4np_n, i.e. p_n ≥ log₂ n roughly, along those n).
  32| LS0 and enumeration are different mechanisms: "LOC-B does not apply" ≠ "reported model unproved".

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W2-APP Part 2 — real designs: design-only diagnostics and classification
   2| 
   3| **Nature of this part.** Descriptive. A single finite data set cannot *verify* an asymptotic hypothesis (which is a
   4| statement about a sequence of designs); what can be done is to measure the design-only quantities the hypotheses refer
   5| to and say which theorem class each design **resembles**. Signal-dependent conditions (beta-min, PTV, visibility,
   6| non-cancellation) are not checkable (θ* unknown) and are not assessed; the only plug-in numbers (riboflavin, diabetes
   7| OMP supports in `data_diag/SUMMARY.md`) are labelled there as plug-in, not verification.
   8| 
   9| **Sources.** The project has no real data set (SoP `06_open_and_plan.tex:279`, ENG19 "Real data ... OPEN"). Public
  10| designs, provenance with md5 in `data_diag/SUMMARY.md` §1 and `data_diag/data/PROVENANCE.txt`: riboflavin (hdi 0.1-10,
  11| CRAN Archive tarball), tecator/Fat spectra (fds 1.8), iclaims (bsts 0.9.10), FRED-QD and FRED-MD (BVAR 1.0.5 data with
  12| BVAR's transformation codes re-implemented), diabetes quadratic model of Efron et al. 2004 (scikit-learn 1.4.2), spam
  13| (kernlab 0.9-33), digits (scikit-learn 1.4.2). Scripts `data_diag/diag_*.R`, `diag_lib.R`, `prep_*.{R,py}`; outputs
  14| `data_diag/out_<name>.*`; master table `data_diag/summary_table.csv`. The method's partition was computed with the
  15| production C++ (`v3_blocks`, byte-identical copy of `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/`, SHA-256 verified,
  16| `data_diag/core_copy/SOURCE_SHA256.txt`). Helper: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (own provider); numbers spot-read by the lead.
  17| 
  18| **Labels.** φ²(k) := min_{|S|=k} λ_min(R_S) (sample correlation). EXACT (k = 2; k = 3 by full/pruned enumeration;
  19| iclaims all k); UB = witness set from greedy/random-restart search (upper bound on φ²(k) — evidence of badness);
  20| LB = rigorous lower bound (Gershgorin, or λ_min(R) when p < n by interlacing).
  21| 
  22| ## Master numbers (from `data_diag/summary_table.csv`)
  23| 
  24| | design | n | p | top-1 share | med. partners abs(r)>.5 (raw → after top factor(s)) | φ² exact k=2 / k=3 | φ² UB k=7 | LB (λ_min R, p<n) | method blocks: #, median/max leakage |
  25| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  26| | riboflavin | 71 | 4088 | 0.36 | 982.5 → 89 | 0.0094 / n.a. | 0.0026 | uninformative | 683; 0.82 / 0.975 |
  27| | tecator | 215 | 100 | 0.99 | 99 → 75 | 4.0e-6 / 4.1e-9 | 6.8e-11 | 1.7e-11 | 13; 1.00 / 1.00 |
  28| | iclaims | 456 | 10 | 0.83 | 9 → 0 | 0.10 / 0.096 | 0.066 (exact) | 0.064 | 4; 0.86 / 0.87 |
  29| | FRED-QD | 257 | 170 | 0.27 | 7 → 3 | 0.0040 / 1.9e-5 | 1.7e-5 | 2.3e-6 | 17; 0.60 / 0.98 |
  30| | FRED-MD | 775 | 99 | 0.21 | 4 → 2 | 0.015 / 9.1e-5 | 7.0e-5 | 4.2e-5 | 13; 0.46 / 0.88 |
  31| | diabetes (quad.) | 442 | 64 | 0.17 | 2 → 1 | 0.041 / 0.012 | 8.1e-5 | 3.6e-7 | 11; 0.56 / 0.84 |
  32| | spam | 4601 | 57 | 0.12 | 0 → 0 | 0.0039 / 0.0039 | 0.0039 | 0.0039 | 10; 0.16 / 0.57 |
  33| | digits | 1797 | 61 | 0.12 | 2 → 0 | 0.062 / 0.059 | 0.055 | 0.050 | 11; 0.49 / 0.66 |

  35| ## Classification (design-only; "resembles" = the class whose design hypotheses the measured pattern matches; v2 after sweep R07)
  36| 
  37| A single finite design is not a sequence: membership of any asymptotic class (fixed floor, LOC constants, VN floors)
  38| is neither confirmed nor refuted by it; every statement below is descriptive [R07 #4, #7, #8]. "Resembles" refers to
  39| the correlation pattern only: the theorems assume iid Gaussian rows, which none of these designs has (spam: heavy-tailed
  40| counts; digits: integer pixels; diabetes-quadratic: polynomial terms; FRED: serially dependent rows) [C2-Opus-3].
  41| Lower bounds labelled "rigorous" are rigorous up to floating-point error.
  42| 
  43| 1. **Local — resemble the LOC / bounded-block classes (L4 (a), (d), (e)); conditioning ranges from moderate (spam,
  44|    digits) to near-collinear clusters (diabetes)** [C1-Opus-5].
  45|    *spam*: no partners above 0.3 for the median variable; one near-duplicate pair (|r| = 0.996) explains the small
  46|    scale of the sparse eigenvalues: for k ≥ 2, interlacing brackets φ²(k) in [0.003855, 0.003934] (exact φ²(2) =
  47|    0.003934, φ²(3) = 0.003901; k = 9 witness 0.003869; λ_min(R) = 0.003855) [R07 #10]. Pattern: nearly independent
  48|    columns plus one cluster of ≈ 11–12 correlated variables (90% quantile of partners above 0.3 is 10, max 11;
  49|    out_spam_partners.csv) and isolated pairs = bounded blocks [C1-Opus-7]. *digits*: pixel-neighbourhood correlation, flat spectrum, observed
  50|    sparse eigenvalues ≈ 0.05. The variables are pixels of a two-dimensional image; Theorem LOC is proved for
  51|    one-dimensional neighbourhood growth, so an extension to growing two-dimensional grids is not covered by the present
  52|    theorem — membership of a sequence representing this particular design is not established either way [R07 #7].
  53|    *diabetes (quadratic)*: correlation confined to clusters (s1–s5, their products and squares; median 2 partners) —
  54|    local block clusters, with a nearly collinear direction (λ_min(R) = 3.6e-7).
  55|    Reading: these patterns match the classes where POST and, under PTV, Theorem LOC apply. The reported numbers are
  56|    observed sample global/sparse eigenvalues (with their exact/UB/LB roles); they are diagnostics relevant to possible
  57|    theorem constants, not the design's φ₀² (which is a population, anchored quantity depending on the unknown support)
  58|    [R07 #22].
  59| 
  60| 2. **Pervasive factor structure — resemble (g) (equicorrelation / factor): POST class; reported model per FAC.**
  61|    *iclaims* (one factor carries 83% of the trace, every pair ≥ 0.698 [C3-Opus-3]; after removing it, no partner > 0.5; p = 10 is
  62|    fixed, so the exact branch applies — at its actual size (n = 456, p = 10) too — and the reported-model question is
  63|    covered by Lemma ENUM + POST in a fixed-p iid-Gaussian-row model — the actual rows are a weekly time series,
  64|    serially dependent) [C2-Opus-2, C3-Opus-1];
  65|    *riboflavin* (top factor 36%, median 982 partners > 0.5, still 89 after removing the factor; the |r| > 0.9 tail is
  66|    sparse; the largest |r| among 8.4·10⁶ independent pairs at n = 71 would be ≈ 0.6–0.67 (typical value ≈ 0.59; 0.67 is a crude upper reference), an extreme-value context
  67|    statistic only — it does not apportion the bulk of the correlations to noise [R07 #9]); 99.5% of pairs with
  68|    |r| > 0.5 are split across the method's blocks (blocks of size ≤ B = 8 cannot hold a pervasive cluster).
  69|    *FRED-QD / FRED-MD*: a common factor (21–27%) plus tight local clusters (interest-rate spreads, manufacturing
  70|    employment aggregates) with exact φ²(3) ≈ 1.9e-5 / 9.1e-5 — "factor + local".
  71|    Reading: posterior level — POST applies to factor designs whose population correlation matrix has a fixed floor;
  72|    reported model — outside the proved local classes. Dense cross-block marginal correlation motivates, but does not
  73|    establish, Lemma VN's conditional visibility hypotheses (marginal correlation can coexist with zero partial
  74|    correlation); only the quantified models V1–V4 carry the proved route obstruction [R07 #8]. FAC-A/B are the
  75|    relevant tickets.
  76| 
  77| 3. **Smooth-curve / functional, near-collinear.** *tecator*: one component carries 98.6% of the trace, adjacent
  78|    wavelengths correlate at 1 − 4e-6, λ_min(R) = 1.7e-11 (positive), exact φ²(3) = 4.1e-9; the method's blocks are
  79|    mutually correlated at |r| ≈ 0.9999. Observed: extreme near-collinearity. Not claimed: exclusion from the fixed-floor
  80|    classes — that would require a specified grid-refinement sequence (population process, grid, normalisation) with a
  81|    proved vanishing sparse floor, which is not supplied; a fixed 100-variable correlation matrix (or independent copies
  82|    of it) does have a fixed positive floor [R07 #4]. Reading: if the relevant asymptotic model is a densely refined
  83|    smooth curve, a functional theory would be needed; this ticket does not decide it.
  84| 
  85| ## What this says about applicability (summary for HQ)
  86| * Of eight standard public designs, three (spam, digits, diabetes-quadratic) show **local** correlation of the kind
  87|   covered by the posterior theorem and by Theorem LOC's class (digits is an image; growing 2-D grids are outside LOC's
  88|   proved scope); four (riboflavin, iclaims, FRED-QD, FRED-MD) are **pervasive factor** designs — posterior theory
  89|   applies to their class; reported-model theory for growing-p versions: FAC-A's class (one factor + bounded blocks, p ≲ n^{1/6}) where it
  90|   applies, otherwise open (iclaims, p = 10: exact branch, ENUM). With p FIXED, all eight designs are eventually on the
  91|   exact branch (ENUM + POST in an iid-Gaussian-row model with a positive population floor), incl. tecator's fixed-design
  92|   reading; the classification matters for growing-p models [C3-Opus-1]; one (tecator) is an extremely **near-collinear functional**
  93|   design, whose appropriate asymptotic model is not decided here.
  94| * Several real designs contain small **near-collinear clusters** (exact φ²(3) between 4e-9 and 1e-2); these are observed
  95|   sample quantities, recorded as data about where the designs sit, not a statement about the theorems' validity.
  96| * The method's own partition (B ≤ 16) captures local clusters (spam: median leakage 0.16) but cannot capture pervasive
  97|   correlation (riboflavin/FRED/tecator: most strong pairs split across blocks). LOC needs no partition condition; the
  98|   VN obstruction is proved only for the quantified models V1–V4 — the block splitting here is descriptive [C1-Opus-4].

   1| # L2 — Combes–Thomas bound and uniform conditional-covariance decay
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**. Check record: R02 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol high,
   4| `reviews/R02_L1L2_check_sol.md`): VERIFIED (one NIT, applied in §L2.3).
   5| Falsification numerics: `numerics/ct_check.py` → `numerics/ct_check_out.txt`.
   6| 
   7| ## L2.1 Combes–Thomas lemma (finite matrices on integer positions)
   8| 
   9| **Lemma CT.** Let I be a finite index set and x : I → ℤ injective ("positions"); write d_ij := |x_i − x_j|. Let A be
  10| a real symmetric matrix on I with spectrum in [α, β], α > 0, and |A_ij| ≤ K e^{−a d_ij} for all i ≠ j, with K > 0,
  11| a > 0. Put
  12|   u := [α/(4K) + 1/(e^a − 1)]⁻¹,   t* := a − log(1 + u)  (so 0 < t* < a).
  13| Then for all i, j ∈ I:  |(A⁻¹)_ij| ≤ (2/α) e^{−t* d_ij}.
  14| 
  15| *Proof.* (i) *The constant.* For 0 ≤ t < a let S(t) := 2K Σ_{d≥1} e^{−ad}(e^{td} − 1) = 2K[1/(e^{a−t} − 1) − 1/(e^a − 1)],
  16| continuous and strictly increasing on [0, a), S(0) = 0, S(t) → ∞ as t ↑ a. Solving S(t) = α/2 gives
  17| 1/(e^{a−t} − 1) = α/(4K) + 1/(e^a − 1) = 1/u, i.e. t = t*. Since 1/u > 1/(e^a − 1), u < e^a − 1, so t* > 0; and
  18| u > 0 gives t* < a. Hence S(t*) = α/2.
  19| (ii) *Conjugation.* Fix t ∈ {t*, −t*} and D := diag(e^{t x_i}). A_t := DAD⁻¹ has entries A_ij e^{t(x_i − x_j)}.
  20| E := A_t − A has zero diagonal and |E_ij| = |A_ij| |e^{t(x_i − x_j)} − 1| ≤ K e^{−a d_ij}(e^{t* d_ij} − 1), using
  21| |e^{s} − 1| ≤ e^{|s|} − 1 for real s.
  22| (iii) *Schur test.* For every i, since x is injective at most two j satisfy d_ij = d for each d ≥ 1, so
  23| Σ_j |E_ij| ≤ S(t*) = α/2; the same bound holds for column sums (the bound is symmetric in i, j). Hence
  24| ‖E‖₂ ≤ √(‖E‖₁‖E‖_∞) ≤ α/2.
  25| (iv) *Inverse.* A is symmetric with λ_min(A) ≥ α, so ‖A⁻¹‖₂ ≤ 1/α and ‖A⁻¹E‖₂ ≤ ½. Thus A_t = A(I + A⁻¹E) is
  26| invertible and ‖A_t⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂/(1 − ½) ≤ 2/α. Since A_t⁻¹ = DA⁻¹D⁻¹, its (i, j) entry is (A⁻¹)_ij e^{t(x_i − x_j)},
  27| and every entry of a matrix is bounded in absolute value by its spectral norm. Choosing the sign of t so that
  28| t(x_i − x_j) = t* d_ij gives |(A⁻¹)_ij| e^{t* d_ij} ≤ 2/α. ∎
  29| 
  30| Remarks. (1) β is not used: only the lower spectral bound and the off-diagonal decay matter. (2) The bound is
  31| uniform in |I| and in the particular positions (only injectivity into ℤ is used). (3) Diagonal entries satisfy the
  32| sharper |(A⁻¹)_ii| ≤ 1/α.
  33| 
  34| ## L2.2 Uniform conditional decay for the class LOC
  35| 
  36| **Definition (class LOC(c, C, K, a)).** A unit-diagonal p × p covariance matrix Σ with spectrum in [c, C]
  37| (0 < c ≤ 1 ≤ C < ∞) for which there is a bijection π : [p] → [p] such that **either** (LOC-Σ) |Σ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a|π(j) − π(k)|}
  38| for j ≠ k, **or** (LOC-Θ) the precision Θ := Σ⁻¹ satisfies |Θ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a|π(j) − π(k)|} for j ≠ k. Write
  39| d(j, k) := |π(j) − π(k)|. For a sequence Σ_n the constants (c, C, K, a) are fixed; π = π_n may vary with n.
  40| 
  41| **Lemma CD (conditional decay).** Let Σ ∈ LOC(c, C, K, a) and W ~ N(0, Σ). Define
  42|   under (LOC-Σ): t₁ := t*(α = c, K, a), K₁ := 2/c;   under (LOC-Θ): t₁ := a, K₁ := K;
  43|   t₂ := t*(α = 1/C, K₁, t₁),  K₂ := 2C.
  44| Then for every U ⊆ [p] and all distinct j, k ∉ U:
  45|   (a) |Cov(W_j, W_k | W_U)| ≤ K₂ e^{−t₂ d(j,k)};
  46|   (b) c ≤ Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ 1, and every conditional covariance matrix Cov(W_V | W_U) (V ⊆ [p] ∖ U) has spectrum in
  47|       [c, C];
  48|   (c) under (LOC-Θ), Σ itself satisfies (LOC-Σ) with constants (2C, t*(1/C, K, a)); under (LOC-Σ), Θ satisfies
  49|       (LOC-Θ) with (2/c, t*(c, K, a)).
  50| The constants (K₂, t₂) depend only on (c, C, K, a), not on p, U, j, k or π.
  51| 
  52| *Proof.* Θ has spectrum in [1/C, 1/c]. Under (LOC-Σ), Lemma CT applied to Σ (positions π, α = c) gives
  53| |Θ_jk| ≤ (2/c)e^{−t₁ d(j,k)} for all j, k; this is (c) second half. Under (LOC-Θ) the bound |Θ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a d} holds
  54| by assumption for j ≠ k, and Lemma CT applied to Θ (α = 1/C) gives (c) first half. In both cases |Θ_jk| ≤ K₁e^{−t₁ d(j,k)}
  55| for j ≠ k. Let V := [p] ∖ U. For Gaussian W, Cov(W_V | W_U) = (Θ_VV)⁻¹ (block inversion). Θ_VV is a principal
  56| submatrix of Θ, so its spectrum lies in [1/C, 1/c] (Rayleigh quotients); its off-diagonal entries obey the same bound
  57| with positions π|_V (still injective). Lemma CT with α = 1/C gives (a). For (b): the spectrum of (Θ_VV)⁻¹ lies in
  58| [c, C]; in particular Var(W_j | W_U) = ((Θ_VV)⁻¹)_jj ≥ c, and Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ Var(W_j) = 1. For sub-vectors
  59| V′ ⊆ V, Cov(W_{V′} | W_U) is a principal submatrix of Cov(W_V | W_U), so its spectrum lies in [c, C] too. ∎
  60| 
  61| ## L2.3 Sufficient conditions (used in L4_families)
  62| 
  63| (i) **Banded Σ** (|Σ_jk| = 0 for d(j,k) > b) with spectrum in [c, C]: (LOC-Σ) holds with K := e^{ab} for any a > 0
  64| (take a = 1, K = e^{b}), because |Σ_jk| ≤ 1 ≤ e^{b − d} for d ≤ b. (ii) **Banded Θ** (Gaussian Markov random field
  65| on a line with range b, e.g. causal AR(b)) with spectrum of Σ in [c, C]: (LOC-Θ) with a = 1, K := e^{b}/c
  66| (|Θ_jk| ≤ ‖Θ‖ ≤ 1/c). (iii) **Block-diagonal** Σ with blocks of size ≤ g, ordered consecutively by π: banded with
  67| b = g − 1. (iv) **Stationary Toeplitz** Σ_jk = γ(|j − k|)/γ(0) with |γ(h)/γ(0)| ≤ K′ρ^h (ρ < 1) and spectrum in [c, C]:
  68| (LOC-Σ) with a = log(1/ρ), K = K′ (normalisation aligned with L4 (c), C1-Opus-8). For AR(1) with parameter 0 < |ρ| < 1 (ρ = 0 is Σ = I: LOC with any fixed K, a > 0; sequences need fixed |ρ| bounded
  69| away from 1 — no unit-root limits) [R02-5]: Σ_jk = ρ^{|j−k|}, spectrum in
  70| [(1 − |ρ|)/(1 + |ρ|), (1 + |ρ|)/(1 − |ρ|)] (GROW L5 (P1)), K = 1, a = log(1/|ρ|).

   8| almost surely, so p is the design's p a.s.), the production core decides the branch by the counting inequality
   9|   (EXB)  Σ_{k≤K} C(p, k) ≤ (5H₀ + 4N₀)p,  N₀ = max(2500, n, p),  H₀ = ⌈512N₀/2500⌉,  K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋)
  10| (`Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_preprocess.R:18-27`, counted by `cpp_exact_count`). On the exact branch it enumerates Ω,
  11| scores every model and reports the maximiser of the all-scored set for the strict order (F, −|S|, lex), with provenance
  12| `phase = exact, mechanism = enumeration`, and returns before LS0 (`Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_fit.R:120-125`). Status
  13| `exact` is part of the output event 𝒪 (FIN `s1_setting.tex:24`); a `resource_limit` stop on the exact branch is "no output"
  14| (U_n) and does not affect the lemma, which is stated jointly with 𝒪 [C3-Opus-7].
  15| 
  16| **Lemma ENUM.** (i) **General override.** For any design sequence for which (EXB) holds for all large n (a condition
  17| on (n, p_n) only), under EX-A: if 1 − π(S₀) < ½ then Ŝ⁺ = S₀ whenever the enumeration returns with output. Hence,
  18| whenever POST's conclusion 1 − π(S₀) = o_P(1) holds under the joint law, P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) → 0 and
  19| liminf P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ = S₀}) = 1 − limsup P(U_n). (ii) **Sufficient conditions for (EXB).** (EXB) holds whenever
  20| 2^{p_n} ≤ 4n·p_n, i.e. p_n − log₂ p_n ≤ log₂ n + 2; in particular for every fixed p, for p_n ≤ c log n with c < 1/log 2,
  21| and for 2^{p_n} ≤ n (e.g. p_n = 2⌊log n/(2 log 2)⌋, C2 Sol's example).
  22| 
  23| *Proof.* (ii) Σ_{k≤K}C(p,k) ≤ 2^p and (5H₀ + 4N₀)p ≥ 4N₀p ≥ 4np. For fixed p, 2^p ≤ 4np for n ≥ 2^p/4; for
  24| p_n ≤ c log n, 2^{p_n} ≤ n^{c log 2} ≤ n eventually. (i) If 1 − π(S₀) < ½, S₀ is the unique maximiser of π, i.e.
  25| F(S₀) > F(S) for every S ∈ Ω ∖ {S₀} (SL0(iv)); every model is scored, so the maximum of the all-scored set under
  26| (F, −|S|, lex) is S₀. Thus 𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {1 − π(S₀) ≥ ½} on the exact branch, and P(1 − π(S₀) ≥ ½) → 0. The liminf
  27| identity is the algebra of FIN §5.1 (M5(0) with D_n = 0). ∎

asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).

   1| # L1 — Key lemma U: a uniform, factor-aware bound on the add statistic over ALL subsets
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; key-lemma check R02 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh,
   4| reviews/R02_L1_check_sol.md): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS (5 MINOR), all applied — v1.1, 2026-11-09. Falsification
   5| numerics: numerics/fu_check.py → FU_out.txt, fu5_check.py → FU5_out.txt; R02's own exhaustive check (in R02).
   6| 
   7| Notation: STATEMENT.md §1–§2. For a symmetric positive semidefinite p × p matrix M, T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T with M_TT ≻ 0
   8| and v_M > 0 (R02 item 3; in particular for every positive definite M) put
   9| c_M := M_TT⁻¹M_{Tl} (c_M := 0 if T = ∅), v_M := M_ll − M_{lT}c_M (Schur complement), and the vector
  10| a_M ∈ ℝ^p with (a_M)_l = 1/√v_M, (a_M)_T = −c_M/√v_M, zero elsewhere. For x ∈ ℝ^p,
  11|   Z^M_{T,l}(x) := a_Mᵀx = (x_l − M_{lT}M_TT⁻¹x_T)/√v_M,
  12| the standardised innovation of x_l given x_T when x ~ N(0, M).
  13| 
  14| ## L1.0 The add statistic is a Gram-only innovation
  15| 
  16| Under model G with standardised X (centred columns), R̂ := XᵀX/(n − 1) and g := Xᵀε/(σ√(n − 1)). For T ⊆ [p] with
  17| R̂_TT ≻ 0 and l ∉ T with (I − P_T)x_l ≠ 0, the add direction u_{T,l} := (I − P_T)x_l/‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ satisfies
  18| 
  19|   Z_{T,l} := u_{T,l}ᵀε/σ = Z^{R̂}_{T,l}(g),   and, conditionally on X, g ~ N(0, R̂).                         (0.1)
  20| 
  21| *Proof.* (I − P_T)x_l = x_l − X_T(X_TᵀX_T)⁻¹X_Tᵀx_l, so (I − P_T)x_lᵀε = σ√(n−1)(g_l − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹g_T) and
  22| ‖(I − P_T)x_l‖² = (n−1)(R̂_ll − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹R̂_{Tl}) = (n−1)v_{R̂}. Since the columns of X are centred, Xᵀε = XᵀCε and
  23| Cov(Xᵀε | X) = σ²XᵀX. ∎
  24| 
  25| So everything below is a statement about a Gaussian vector and its covariance. We avoid a direct union bound over the
  26| innovation normals indexed by (T, l): we union over the local innovation pairs (l, U) and over subsets of factor groups
  27| with thresholds depending on the number of groups (when all groups are singletons the latter are 2^p − 1 subsets, whose
  28| count is absorbed by the size-dependent threshold); the factor variables W_T (up to 2^p of them) are controlled
  29| simultaneously by the deterministic bound U(b), not by counting (R02 item 4).
  30| 
  31| ## L1.1 Exact decomposition along the residual factor direction (one global factor + block-local part)
  32| 
  33| **Lemma U(a).** Let Σ = λλᵀ + Ψ with Ψ ≻ 0 block-diagonal with respect to a partition 𝒢 of [p] (λ arbitrary). On a
  34| probability space carrying independent ξ₀ ~ N(0, 1) and ζ ~ N(0, Ψ), put γ := λξ₀ + ζ (so γ ~ N(0, Σ)). For
  35| T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T, U := T ∩ g(l), define
  36| 
  37|   ψ_{l|U} := Ψ_ll − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹Ψ_{Ul},   Ξ_{l,U} := (ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U)/√ψ_{l|U},
  38|   λ̃_{l|U} := λ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U,   s_T := λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹λ_T,   W_T := (ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T)/√(1 + s_T)
  39| 
  40| (empty-set conventions, R02 item 3: only sums/products over empty index sets vanish; explicitly c_∅ = 0, s_∅ = 0,
  41| W_∅ = ξ₀, ψ_{l|∅} = Ψ_ll, λ̃_{l|∅} = λ_l, Ξ_{l,∅} = ζ_l/√Ψ_ll; Ψ_TT⁻¹ is block-diagonal with blocks Ψ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹,
  42| T_g := T ∩ g). Then
  43| Ξ_{l,U} ~ N(0, 1), W_T ~ N(0, 1), Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ W_T (independent), and
  44| 
  45|   Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = [√ψ_{l|U} Ξ_{l,U} + (λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T)) W_T] / √(ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T)).          (1.1)
  46| 
  47| *Proof.* Work in L² of the probability space. 𝓗_T := span{γ_j : j ∈ T} ⊆ 𝓚_T := span{ξ₀, ζ_j : j ∈ T}, because
  48| γ_j = λ_jξ₀ + ζ_j. Cov(ξ₀, ζ_T) = diag(1, Ψ_TT) ≻ 0 and Σ_TT ⪰ Ψ_TT ≻ 0, so dim 𝓚_T = |T| + 1 and dim 𝓗_T = |T|;
  49| 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T is one-dimensional. For jointly Gaussian centred variables the conditional expectation equals the L²
  50| projection, so Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = (γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l)/‖γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l‖_{L²}. Decompose
  51| 
  52|   γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l = (γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l) + (P_{𝓚_T}γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l),
  53| 
  54| an orthogonal sum (the first term is ⊥ 𝓚_T ⊇ 𝓗_T, the second lies in 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T).
  55| *First term.* P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = λ_lξ₀ + P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l, and ζ_l is uncorrelated with ξ₀ and with ζ_j for j ∉ g(l) (Ψ block-
  56| diagonal), so P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l = P_{span(ζ_U)}ζ_l = Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U. Hence γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U
  57| = √ψ_{l|U}Ξ_{l,U}, with variance ψ_{l|U} > 0.
  58| *Second term.* Let ω_T := ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T and c := (1 + s_T)⁻¹Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T. Then cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹(s_Tξ₀ +
  59| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T) ∈ 𝓗_T and ξ₀ − cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹ω_T. For j ∈ T, E[ω_Tγ_j] = λ_j − (λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tj}) = λ_j − λ_j = 0,
  60| so ω_T ⊥ 𝓗_T, ω_T ∈ 𝓚_T, and ω_T ≠ 0 (Var ω_T = 1 + s_T ≥ 1). Thus 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T = span(ω_T) and W_T = ω_T/√(1 + s_T)
  61| is its unit vector. The second term is E[γ_lW_T]W_T with
  62|   E[γ_lW_T] = (λ_l − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tl})/√(1 + s_T) = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T),
  63| because Ψ_{Tl} vanishes outside U and (Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T)_U = Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U (block-diagonality).
  64| *Assembly.* The two terms are orthogonal, so the innovation variance is ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T), which gives
  65| (1.1). Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ 𝓚_T ∋ W_T and both are Gaussian, hence independent. ∎
  66| 
  67| **Interpretation (route A).** The innovation of x_l given x_T has an idiosyncratic part, which depends on T only
  68| through T ∩ g(l) (at most p·2^{γ̄−1} distinct standard normals over all (T, l)), and one factor part along the
  69| residual factor variable W_T (one normal per T, shared by all l). This is the "Pythagorean split along the residual
  70| factor direction"; the direction count is controlled by the groups and by k = 1, not by the size of the lattice.
  71| 
  72| ## L1.2 Deterministic bound
  73| 
  74| **Lemma U(b).** In the setting of U(a), let c_min := min{λ_VᵀΨ_VV⁻¹λ_V : ∅ ≠ V ⊆ g ∈ 𝒢} and assume c_min > 0. Put
  75| κ'_{l,U} := |λ̃_{l|U}|/√ψ_{l|U}, κ' := max κ'_{l,U}, κ := κ'/√c_min (= κ(Σ) of STATEMENT §2), and for groups g,
  76| Q_g := ζ_gᵀΨ_gg⁻¹ζ_g. Notation (R02 item 1): κ = κ(λ, Ψ, 𝒢) is representation-dependent; κ'_* := max_{l,U}κ'_{l,U}
  77| = κ√c_min (written κ' below) and κ'_bd := κ̄√c_min ≥ κ'_* whenever κ ≤ κ̄. Note c_min = min_j λ_j²/Ψ_jj (variational
  78| monotonicity with λ in place of ζ) and, in the correlation class, c_min ≤ (1 − ψ₀)/ψ₀, so κ'_bd ≤ κ̄/√ψ₀. For T ≠ ∅
  79| let 𝒢(T) := {g : T ∩ g ≠ ∅}, h_T := |𝒢(T)|. Then for every T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T:
  80| 
  81|   |Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ |Ξ_{l,U}| + κ'|ξ₀|/(1 + s_T) + κ√( Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} Q_g / h_T )   (the whole last summand is defined
  82|   as 0 if T = ∅).                                                                                              (1.2)
  83| 
  84| *Proof.* Write (1.1) as (αΞ + βW)/√(α² + β²), α = √ψ_{l|U} > 0, β = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T). Since √(α² + β²) ≥ α,
  85| |Z| ≤ |Ξ| + (|β|/α)|W| = |Ξ| + κ'_{l,U}|ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T|/(1 + s_T). By block-diagonality,
  86| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T = Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹ζ_{T_g}; by Cauchy–Schwarz in the inner product ⟨x, y⟩ = xᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹y,
  87| each summand is at most √(s_{T_g}) √(q_{T_g}) in absolute value, with s_{T_g} := λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹λ_{T_g},

   1| # L8 — Part III frontier: the path route for exact-Gram compound symmetry (tools proved; target open)
   2| 
   3| Status: Lemma CS-1D and Lemma GAP: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** (tools; not used by Parts I–II). Conjecture
   4| PATH-CS: **OPEN** (evidence only). Numerics: numerics/cs1d.py (selftest), D2_summary.md, D3_summary.md.

   6| ## Lemma CS-1D (exact one-dimensional reduction)
   7| 
   8| Exact Gram XᵀX = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I + a11ᵀ], a ∈ (0, 1), response scaled to yᵀy = n − 1, z := Xᵀy. Put
   9| A := (n + 1)(n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B := (n + 1)(n − 1)a, A′ := (n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B′ := (n − 1)a, N_k := k + A/B,
  10| P_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j², L_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j. For every T with |T| = k ≤ K,
  11| 
  12|   F(T) = log w(k) + D_k − ν log(0.02 + (n − 1) − (n/A)Φ(T)),   Φ(T) := P_T − L_T²/N_k,
  13|   D_k := −½[(k − 1) log A + log(A + kB) − (k − 1) log A′ − log(A′ + kB′)]  (D_0 := 0), up to the constant log c_n.
  14| 
  15| *Proof.* For |T| = k, G_T = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I_k + a11ᵀ] does not depend on which T; H_T = AI + B11ᵀ,
  16| G_T + I = A′I + B′11ᵀ; det(αI + β11ᵀ) = α^{k−1}(α + kβ) and (αI + β11ᵀ)⁻¹ = α⁻¹(I − β(α + kβ)⁻¹11ᵀ); hence
  17| z_TᵀH_T⁻¹z_T = A⁻¹(P_T − B(A + kB)⁻¹L_T²) = A⁻¹Φ(T) since B/(A + kB) = 1/N_k. Insert into the score of FINAL s1. ∎
  18| (numerics/cs1d.py selftest: agreement with the exact scorer to 5.6e-9 at n = 10⁶; identical LS0 endpoints and move
  19| counts in the selftest — paths themselves were not compared; R06 item 12.)
  20| 
  21| **Move identities (exact).** With c_T := L_T/N_k and N := N_k:
  22|   deletion of e ∈ T:  Φ(T) − Φ(T ∖ e) = (N/(N − 1))(z_e − c_T)²;
  23|   addition of l ∉ T:  Φ(T ∪ l) − Φ(T) = (N/(N + 1))(z_l − c_T)²;
  24|   swap e → l:         Φ(T ∖ e ∪ l) − Φ(T) = u² − v² − (u − v)²/N,  u := z_l − c_T, v := z_e − c_T.
  25| (Elementary algebra from Φ = P − L²/N.) Since F is increasing in Φ at fixed size, the best deletion from T removes the
  26| element of T closest to c_T, the best addition adds the outside element farthest from c_T, and every comparison between
  27| moves reduces to these one-dimensional quantities. For T ⊇ S₀ the signal parts cancel: the null z-values are

  30| τ times (Σ_{j∈T}h_j − γ_n)/N with a common γ_n = O_P(1) (L1 U(a) with singleton groups).

  32| ## Lemma GAP (deterministic invariant of a deletion path)
  33| 
  34| Suppose LS0 starts at [p] and its first t moves are deletions of nulls, each the element of the current set closest to
  35| its centre c_T. Let D_t be the deleted set. Then (i) D_t is a contiguous run in the order of the null z-values, and
  36| (ii) c_{T_t} lies in the closed interval between the largest kept null below D_t and the smallest kept null above D_t
  37| (with ±∞ if none).
  38| *Proof.* Induction. t = 1: e₁ is the null closest to c_{[p]}; the nearest kept nulls on either side of z_{e₁} are at
  39| least as far from c as z_{e₁}. Step: let e be the kept element closest to c := c_T, say z_e ≥ c (the other case is
  40| symmetric). Then c_{T∖e} = c + (c − z_e)/(N − 1) moves away from z_e by (z_e − c)/(N − 1) < z_e − c ≤ c − ℓ′ (ℓ′ the
  41| nearest kept below; by minimality of e), because N − 1 > 1 (N ≥ s₀ + 1 + A/B > 2 while a null is kept). So the new centre
  42| stays strictly between ℓ′ and the next kept element above z_e; D ∪ {e} is still contiguous. ∎

  44| ## Conjecture PATH-CS and where a proof stops

  46| **Conjecture PATH-CS.** Exact-Gram CS, fixed a, s₀, θ*, σ², (GC-CS), and the visibility condition making S̃₀ = [p]

asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often

that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any

    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

  66|   ψ_{l|U} := Ψ_ll − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹Ψ_{Ul},  λ̃_{l|U} := λ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U,
  67|   c_min := min{λ_VᵀΨ_VV⁻¹λ_V : ∅ ≠ V ⊆ g ∈ 𝒢} (> 0),  κ := max_{l,U} |λ̃_{l|U}|/√(ψ_{l|U}c_min),

   1| # L1 — Key lemma U: a uniform, factor-aware bound on the add statistic over ALL subsets
   2|
