   4| reviews/R02_L1_check_sol.md): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS (5 MINOR), all applied — v1.1, 2026-11-09. Falsification
   5| numerics: numerics/fu_check.py → FU_out.txt, fu5_check.py → FU5_out.txt; R02's own exhaustive check (in R02).
   6| 
   7| Notation: STATEMENT.md §1–§2. For a symmetric positive semidefinite p × p matrix M, T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T with M_TT ≻ 0
   8| and v_M > 0 (R02 item 3; in particular for every positive definite M) put
   9| c_M := M_TT⁻¹M_{Tl} (c_M := 0 if T = ∅), v_M := M_ll − M_{lT}c_M (Schur complement), and the vector
  10| a_M ∈ ℝ^p with (a_M)_l = 1/√v_M, (a_M)_T = −c_M/√v_M, zero elsewhere. For x ∈ ℝ^p,
  11|   Z^M_{T,l}(x) := a_Mᵀx = (x_l − M_{lT}M_TT⁻¹x_T)/√v_M,
  12| the standardised innovation of x_l given x_T when x ~ N(0, M).
  13| 
  14| ## L1.0 The add statistic is a Gram-only innovation
  15| 
  16| Under model G with standardised X (centred columns), R̂ := XᵀX/(n − 1) and g := Xᵀε/(σ√(n − 1)). For T ⊆ [p] with
  17| R̂_TT ≻ 0 and l ∉ T with (I − P_T)x_l ≠ 0, the add direction u_{T,l} := (I − P_T)x_l/‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ satisfies
  18| 
  19|   Z_{T,l} := u_{T,l}ᵀε/σ = Z^{R̂}_{T,l}(g),   and, conditionally on X, g ~ N(0, R̂).                         (0.1)
  20| 
  21| *Proof.* (I − P_T)x_l = x_l − X_T(X_TᵀX_T)⁻¹X_Tᵀx_l, so (I − P_T)x_lᵀε = σ√(n−1)(g_l − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹g_T) and
  22| ‖(I − P_T)x_l‖² = (n−1)(R̂_ll − R̂_{lT}R̂_TT⁻¹R̂_{Tl}) = (n−1)v_{R̂}. Since the columns of X are centred, Xᵀε = XᵀCε and
  23| Cov(Xᵀε | X) = σ²XᵀX. ∎
  24| 
  25| So everything below is a statement about a Gaussian vector and its covariance. We avoid a direct union bound over the
  26| innovation normals indexed by (T, l): we union over the local innovation pairs (l, U) and over subsets of factor groups
  27| with thresholds depending on the number of groups (when all groups are singletons the latter are 2^p − 1 subsets, whose
  28| count is absorbed by the size-dependent threshold); the factor variables W_T (up to 2^p of them) are controlled
  29| simultaneously by the deterministic bound U(b), not by counting (R02 item 4).
  30| 
  31| ## L1.1 Exact decomposition along the residual factor direction (one global factor + block-local part)
  32| 
  33| **Lemma U(a).** Let Σ = λλᵀ + Ψ with Ψ ≻ 0 block-diagonal with respect to a partition 𝒢 of [p] (λ arbitrary). On a
  34| probability space carrying independent ξ₀ ~ N(0, 1) and ζ ~ N(0, Ψ), put γ := λξ₀ + ζ (so γ ~ N(0, Σ)). For
  35| T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T, U := T ∩ g(l), define
  36| 
  37|   ψ_{l|U} := Ψ_ll − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹Ψ_{Ul},   Ξ_{l,U} := (ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U)/√ψ_{l|U},
  38|   λ̃_{l|U} := λ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U,   s_T := λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹λ_T,   W_T := (ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T)/√(1 + s_T)
  39| 
  40| (empty-set conventions, R02 item 3: only sums/products over empty index sets vanish; explicitly c_∅ = 0, s_∅ = 0,
  41| W_∅ = ξ₀, ψ_{l|∅} = Ψ_ll, λ̃_{l|∅} = λ_l, Ξ_{l,∅} = ζ_l/√Ψ_ll; Ψ_TT⁻¹ is block-diagonal with blocks Ψ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹,
  42| T_g := T ∩ g). Then
  43| Ξ_{l,U} ~ N(0, 1), W_T ~ N(0, 1), Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ W_T (independent), and
  44| 
  45|   Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = [√ψ_{l|U} Ξ_{l,U} + (λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T)) W_T] / √(ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T)).          (1.1)
  46| 
  47| *Proof.* Work in L² of the probability space. 𝓗_T := span{γ_j : j ∈ T} ⊆ 𝓚_T := span{ξ₀, ζ_j : j ∈ T}, because
  48| γ_j = λ_jξ₀ + ζ_j. Cov(ξ₀, ζ_T) = diag(1, Ψ_TT) ≻ 0 and Σ_TT ⪰ Ψ_TT ≻ 0, so dim 𝓚_T = |T| + 1 and dim 𝓗_T = |T|;
  49| 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T is one-dimensional. For jointly Gaussian centred variables the conditional expectation equals the L²
  50| projection, so Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ) = (γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l)/‖γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l‖_{L²}. Decompose
  51| 
  52|   γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l = (γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l) + (P_{𝓚_T}γ_l − P_{𝓗_T}γ_l),
  53| 
  54| an orthogonal sum (the first term is ⊥ 𝓚_T ⊇ 𝓗_T, the second lies in 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T).
  55| *First term.* P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = λ_lξ₀ + P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l, and ζ_l is uncorrelated with ξ₀ and with ζ_j for j ∉ g(l) (Ψ block-
  56| diagonal), so P_{𝓚_T}ζ_l = P_{span(ζ_U)}ζ_l = Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U. Hence γ_l − P_{𝓚_T}γ_l = ζ_l − Ψ_{lU}Ψ_UU⁻¹ζ_U
  57| = √ψ_{l|U}Ξ_{l,U}, with variance ψ_{l|U} > 0.
  58| *Second term.* Let ω_T := ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T and c := (1 + s_T)⁻¹Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T. Then cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹(s_Tξ₀ +
  59| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T) ∈ 𝓗_T and ξ₀ − cᵀγ_T = (1 + s_T)⁻¹ω_T. For j ∈ T, E[ω_Tγ_j] = λ_j − (λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tj}) = λ_j − λ_j = 0,
  60| so ω_T ⊥ 𝓗_T, ω_T ∈ 𝓚_T, and ω_T ≠ 0 (Var ω_T = 1 + s_T ≥ 1). Thus 𝓚_T ⊖ 𝓗_T = span(ω_T) and W_T = ω_T/√(1 + s_T)
  61| is its unit vector. The second term is E[γ_lW_T]W_T with
  62|   E[γ_lW_T] = (λ_l − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹Ψ_{Tl})/√(1 + s_T) = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T),
  63| because Ψ_{Tl} vanishes outside U and (Ψ_TT⁻¹λ_T)_U = Ψ_UU⁻¹λ_U (block-diagonality).
  64| *Assembly.* The two terms are orthogonal, so the innovation variance is ψ_{l|U} + λ̃²_{l|U}/(1 + s_T), which gives
  65| (1.1). Ξ_{l,U} ⊥ 𝓚_T ∋ W_T and both are Gaussian, hence independent. ∎
  66| 
  67| **Interpretation (route A).** The innovation of x_l given x_T has an idiosyncratic part, which depends on T only
  68| through T ∩ g(l) (at most p·2^{γ̄−1} distinct standard normals over all (T, l)), and one factor part along the
  69| residual factor variable W_T (one normal per T, shared by all l). This is the "Pythagorean split along the residual
  70| factor direction"; the direction count is controlled by the groups and by k = 1, not by the size of the lattice.
  71| 
  72| ## L1.2 Deterministic bound
  73| 
  74| **Lemma U(b).** In the setting of U(a), let c_min := min{λ_VᵀΨ_VV⁻¹λ_V : ∅ ≠ V ⊆ g ∈ 𝒢} and assume c_min > 0. Put
  75| κ'_{l,U} := |λ̃_{l|U}|/√ψ_{l|U}, κ' := max κ'_{l,U}, κ := κ'/√c_min (= κ(Σ) of STATEMENT §2), and for groups g,
  76| Q_g := ζ_gᵀΨ_gg⁻¹ζ_g. Notation (R02 item 1): κ = κ(λ, Ψ, 𝒢) is representation-dependent; κ'_* := max_{l,U}κ'_{l,U}
  77| = κ√c_min (written κ' below) and κ'_bd := κ̄√c_min ≥ κ'_* whenever κ ≤ κ̄. Note c_min = min_j λ_j²/Ψ_jj (variational
  78| monotonicity with λ in place of ζ) and, in the correlation class, c_min ≤ (1 − ψ₀)/ψ₀, so κ'_bd ≤ κ̄/√ψ₀. For T ≠ ∅
  79| let 𝒢(T) := {g : T ∩ g ≠ ∅}, h_T := |𝒢(T)|. Then for every T ⊆ [p], l ∉ T:
  80| 
  81|   |Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ |Ξ_{l,U}| + κ'|ξ₀|/(1 + s_T) + κ√( Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} Q_g / h_T )   (the whole last summand is defined
  82|   as 0 if T = ∅).                                                                                              (1.2)
  83| 
  84| *Proof.* Write (1.1) as (αΞ + βW)/√(α² + β²), α = √ψ_{l|U} > 0, β = λ̃_{l|U}/√(1 + s_T). Since √(α² + β²) ≥ α,
  85| |Z| ≤ |Ξ| + (|β|/α)|W| = |Ξ| + κ'_{l,U}|ξ₀ − λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T|/(1 + s_T). By block-diagonality,
  86| λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T = Σ_{g∈𝒢(T)} λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹ζ_{T_g}; by Cauchy–Schwarz in the inner product ⟨x, y⟩ = xᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹y,
  87| each summand is at most √(s_{T_g}) √(q_{T_g}) in absolute value, with s_{T_g} := λ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹λ_{T_g},
  88| q_{T_g} := ζ_{T_g}ᵀΨ_{T_gT_g}⁻¹ζ_{T_g}. Monotonicity: for V ⊆ g, q_V = max_{c∈ℝ^V}(2cᵀζ_V − cᵀΨ_VVc) ≤
  89| max_{c∈ℝ^g}(2cᵀζ_g − cᵀΨ_gg c) = Q_g (extend c by zeros). Cauchy–Schwarz over g and s_T = Σ_g s_{T_g}:
  90| |λ_TᵀΨ_TT⁻¹ζ_T| ≤ √s_T · √(Σ_{𝒢(T)} Q_g). Each nonempty T_g has s_{T_g} ≥ c_min, so s_T ≥ c_min h_T and
  91| √s_T/(1 + s_T) ≤ 1/√s_T ≤ 1/√(c_min h_T). Combine, and use κ'_{l,U}/√c_min ≤ κ. ∎
  92| 
  93| ## L1.3 Probability bounds
  94| 
  95| **Lemma U(c).** In the setting of U(b), let every group have size ≤ γ̄, let G := |𝒢| ≤ p, and fix n ≥ 16 (so
  96| log log n > 0). There is an event E_U(n) with P(E_U(n)ᶜ) ≤ 3/log n on which, for every T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T,
  97| 
  98|   |Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ √(2 log(p 2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n) + κ'√(2 log log n) + κ √(a_{h_T})            (1.3)
  99| 
 100| (the whole size-dependent summand is defined as 0 for T = ∅, without evaluating its logarithm), where for 1 ≤ h ≤ G,
 101| with r_h := (2 log(h + 1) + log log n)/h,
 102|   a_h := 2 log(eG/h) + 2r_h + γ̄ + 2√(γ̄ (log(eG/h) + r_h)).
 103| In particular, since G ≤ p and h_T ≥ |T|/γ̄, for T ≠ ∅
 104| 
 105|   √(a_{h_T}) ≤ √(2 log(e γ̄ p/|T|)) + ϱ_n,  ϱ_n := √(2(2 log 2 + log log n) + γ̄ + 2√(γ̄(log(e γ̄ p) + 2 log 2 + log log n))),
 106| 
 107| and ϱ_n = O((log p)^{1/4} + (log log n)^{1/2}); explicitly, with ℓ := log log n ≥ 1 and b := 2 log 2 + ℓ,
 108| ϱ_n ≤ √(2b) + √γ̄ + √2 γ̄^{1/4}[log(eγ̄p) + b]^{1/4} ≤ C(γ̄)[(log p)^{1/4} + ℓ^{1/2}] (n ≥ 16; γ̄ fixed is material).
 109| 
 110| *Proof.* (i) For each (l, U), U ⊆ g(l) ∖ {l}, Ξ_{l,U} ~ N(0, 1); there are at most p2^{γ̄−1} such pairs. With
 111| t² := 2 log(p2^{γ̄−1}) + 2 log log n ≥ 2/π and P(|N(0,1)| > t) ≤ √(2/π)e^{−t²/2}/t ≤ e^{−t²/2}, the union bound gives
 112| P(max|Ξ_{l,U}| > t) ≤ 1/log n; and t ≤ √(2 log(p2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n).
 113| (ii) P(|ξ₀| > √(2 log log n)) ≤ 1/log n (same tail bound; 2 log log n ≥ 2/π for n ≥ 16).
 114| (iii) The (Q_g)_g are independent (ζ_g independent across groups, Ψ block-diagonal) with Q_g ~ χ²_{|g|}. For a set 𝒥
 115| of h groups, Σ_𝒥 Q_g ~ χ²_D with D ≤ hγ̄. Laurent–Massart (2000, Lemma 1; as cited in PXN lemmas/CR_corr_tails.md):
 116| P(χ²_D ≥ D + 2√(Dx) + 2x) ≤ e^{−x}; the threshold is increasing in D, so it may be replaced by hγ̄ + 2√(hγ̄x) + 2x.
 117| Take x_h := log C(G, h) + 2 log(h + 1) + log log n and union over 𝒥 and h: the failure probability is at most
 118| Σ_{h≥1}(h + 1)^{−2}/log n ≤ 1/log n. On the complement, using log C(G,h) ≤ h log(eG/h),
 119| (1/h)Σ_𝒥 Q_g ≤ γ̄ + 2√(γ̄ x_h/h) + 2x_h/h ≤ a_h.
 120| Let E_U(n) be the intersection of the three events; then (1.2) gives (1.3). For the second display:
 121| √(a + b) ≤ √a + √b with a = 2 log(eG/h), and log(eG/h_T) ≤ log(e γ̄ p/|T|), r_h ≤ 2 log 2 + log log n. ∎
 122| 
 123| ## L1.4 Perturbation: approximate factor Gram (fixed designs) and iid rows
 124| 
 125| **Lemma U(d).** Let Σ ⪰ ψ₀I be a correlation matrix, R a correlation matrix with ‖R − Σ‖_op ≤ δ ≤ ψ₀/4, x ~ N(0, R),
 126| and γ := Σ^{1/2}R^{−1/2}x (so γ ~ N(0, Σ)). Then, for every T ⊆ [p] and l ∉ T,
 127| 
 128|   |Z^R_{T,l}(x) − Z^Σ_{T,l}(γ)| ≤ L_ψ δ ‖x‖,   L_ψ := C₂ + 2C₃/ψ₀,                                               (1.4)
 129| 
 130| with m := 3ψ₀/4, B := m^{−1/2}, C₂ := (1 + B)(3 + B²)/(2m^{3/2}), C₃ := (1 + B)/√m (R02 item 2),
 131| 
 132| and P(‖x‖² > 5(p + 1)u) ≤ e^{−u} for u ≥ 1.
 133| 
 134| *Proof.* λ_min(R) ≥ 3ψ₀/4. For M ∈ {R, Σ}: v_M ≥ λ_min(M) (Schur complement); c_MᵀM_TTc_M ≤ M_ll = 1, so
 135| ‖c_M‖² ≤ 1/λ_min(M) ≤ 4/(3ψ₀). (i) c_R − c_Σ = R_TT⁻¹[(R − Σ)_{Tl} − (R − Σ)_TTc_Σ], so ‖c_R − c_Σ‖ ≤
 136| (4/(3ψ₀))δ(1 + ‖c_Σ‖). (ii) v_M = min_c (e_l − ι_Tc)ᵀM(e_l − ι_Tc) (minimiser c_M), so
 137| v_R ≤ v_Σ + δ(1 + ‖c_Σ‖²) and v_Σ ≤ v_R + δ(1 + ‖c_R‖²): |v_R − v_Σ| ≤ δ(1 + 4/(3ψ₀)). (iii) Hence
 138| ‖a_R − a_Σ‖ ≤ ‖c_R − c_Σ‖/√v_R + (1 + ‖c_Σ‖)·|v_R − v_Σ|/(√(v_Rv_Σ)(√v_R + √v_Σ)) ≤ C₂(ψ₀)δ, and
 139| ‖a_Σ‖ ≤ (1 + ‖c_Σ‖)/√v_Σ ≤ C₃(ψ₀). (iv) ‖x − γ‖ = ‖(R^{1/2} − Σ^{1/2})R^{−1/2}x‖ ≤ ‖R − Σ‖/(√λ_min(R) + √λ_min(Σ)) ·
 140| ‖x‖/√λ_min(R) ≤ (2δ/ψ₀)‖x‖ (for PD A, B: ‖A^{1/2} − B^{1/2}‖ ≤ ‖A − B‖/(√λ_min(A) + √λ_min(B))). (v)
 141| |a_Rᵀx − a_Σᵀγ| ≤ ‖a_R − a_Σ‖‖x‖ + ‖a_Σ‖‖x − γ‖ ≤ (C₂ + 2C₃/ψ₀)δ‖x‖ =: L_ψδ‖x‖. The norm bound: ‖x‖² = wᵀRw with
 142| w ~ N(0, I); Laurent–Massart's weighted form gives P(wᵀRw ≥ tr R + 2√(tr(R²)u) + 2‖R‖u) ≤ e^{−u}; tr R = p,
 143| ‖R‖ ≤ tr R = p, tr R² ≤ ‖R‖ tr R ≤ p², so the threshold is ≤ p + 2p√u + 2pu ≤ 5(p + 1)u for u ≥ 1. ∎

 145| Note that ‖Σ‖_op (≈ p λ̄² for a pervasive factor) does not enter L_ψ: only the unit diagonal and λ_min are used.

 147| ## L1.5 Consequence used downstream

 149| **Corollary U.** Let X satisfy (AG) (STATEMENT §3) with Σ_n ∈ 𝔉(γ̄, ψ₀, κ̄), and let g = Xᵀε/(σ√(n−1)). Let E_n =

 153|   |Z_{T,l}| ≤ √(2 log(p 2^{γ̄}) + 2 log log n) + κ'√(2 log log n) + κ̄ (√(2 log(e γ̄ p/|T|)) + ϱ_n)·1{T ≠ ∅}
 154|             + L_ψ δ_n √(5(p + 1) log log n).

 156| *Proof.* (0.1), U(d) with R = R̂, x = g (u = log log n ≥ 1 for n ≥ 16), and U(c) applied to the coupled vector. Fix
 157| X with δ_n ≤ ψ₀/4 and put γ := Σ_n^{1/2}R̂^{−1/2}g. On an enlarged space carrying an independent V ~ N(0, 1), with
 158| b := Σ_n⁻¹λ, set ξ₀ := bᵀγ + √(1 − λᵀΣ_n⁻¹λ)V and ζ := γ − λξ₀ (1 − λᵀΣ_n⁻¹λ > 0 since Ψ ≻ 0). Given X these are

   1| # L2 — Sandwich for Q = [p]: every start-mode maximiser contains S₀
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** — v1.1, 2026-11-09; lemma check R03 (Sol high): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS
   4| (1 MINOR, applied). This re-proves the Q = [p] branch of C-GROW
   5| lemmas/L3_sandwich.md L3.3(a) under reduced hypotheses (R01 item 5); C-GROW's L3 is "PROVED-CHECKED" inside
   6| Theorem GROW but its hypothesis (G1) includes |Q| ≤ C_Q log n, which fails here, so it is not cited verbatim.
   7| 
   8| Hypotheses: model G; ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn; p ≤ n^A (any fixed A; (P) gives this); the method's actual blocks C_b with
   9| |C_b| ≤ 16, a deterministic function of X; (G3a) λ_min(R̂_T) ≥ φ₀² for nonempty T ⊆ C_b (implied by (AG) with
  10| φ₀² = 3ψ₀/4 once δ_n ≤ ψ₀/4); (TV) for a deterministic M_n → ∞: δ²_{U,j} ≥ M_n log n for all j ∈ S₀,
  11| U ⊆ C_{b(j)} ∖ {j}; and K = p (true for n ≥ n₀ under (P), since p = o(n)).
  12| 
  13| **Lemma L2.** P(Sand_n) → 1, where Sand_n := {S₀ ⊆ S̃ for every maximiser S̃ of γ₀ on Ω}.
  14| 
  15| ## Events (as GROW L3.0, block family only)
  16| 
  17| * 𝓔^blk: the events 𝒟₁ ∩ 𝒟₂ ∩ 𝒟₃ of [GEN-L1] (`Theory_work/Wave1/W1-GEN/lemmas/L1_lemmaE.md`; GEN R02
  18|   VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS) for the deterministic family 𝔉_blk := {U : U ⊆ C_b for some b}, which has |U| ≤ 16 and
  19|   |𝔉_blk| ≤ 2^{16}p ≤ 2^{16}n^A, and the vector set {r_U, r_U − r_{U′} : U, U′ ∈ 𝔉_blk} (polynomially many). [GEN-L1]
  20|   needs exactly: fixed maximal set size (16), polynomial family size, Gram floor (G3a) on its nonempty members, and
  21|   ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn. Then P(𝓔^blk) → 1, and on 𝓔^blk, for n ≥ n₀, C-GROW L0.2(c) (score differences for block tables) and
  22|   [GEN-L1] L1.4(b) (nested sets) hold on 𝔉_blk. (C-GROW L0 is only needed with its J fixed = 16 here, i.e. it is
  23|   [GEN-L1] itself.)
  24| * 𝓩 := {Z²_{U,j} ≤ z²_n for all b, U ⊆ C_b, j ∈ C_b ∖ U}, z²_n := 2 log(2^{21}p) + 2 log log n; P(𝓩ᶜ) ≤ 1/log n
  25|   (at most 2^{20}p standard normals; GROW L3.0).
  26| 
  27| ## Proof
  28| 
  29| Work on 𝓔^blk ∩ 𝓩, n ≥ n₀. Let S̃ be any maximiser of γ₀ on Ω, k̃ := |S̃|, Ũ_b := S̃ ∩ C_b. If k̃ = K = p then
  30| S̃ = [p] ⊇ S₀. Otherwise k̃ < K, and for j ∈ S₀ ∖ S̃ with j ∈ C_b the set S̃ ∪ {j} lies in Ω. Since only block b's
  31| factor and the prior change,
  32|   log γ₀(S̃ ∪ {j}) − log γ₀(S̃) = log[(k̃ + 1)/(2p − 1 − k̃)] + log r_b(Ũ_b ∪ {j}) − log r_b(Ũ_b)
  33|      ≥ −log(2p) − ½ log(n + 1) − 2κ_E + (RSS_{Ũ_b} − RSS_{Ũ_b∪{j}})/(2C_R)
  34| (L0.2(c) and [GEN-L1] L1.4(b) for the nested block sets Ũ_b ⊆ Ũ_b ∪ {j}; constants C_R = 3(M + σ²), κ_E of
  35| [GEN-L1]; k̃ + 1 ≥ 1 and 2p − 1 − k̃ ≤ 2p). Here, as in [GEN-L1] and GROW L0/L3, RSS_A := ‖(I − P_A)Y‖² for the
  36| unscaled centred response Y = Cy^r = μ + Cε. [GEN-L1] L1.3 gives log m(A) = c′_n − ½|A| log(n + 1) − ν log RSS_A + R_A
  37| with |R_A| ≤ κ_E uniformly on the block family; the change from scaled RSS^y_A to RSS_A contributes only to the common
  38| c′_n, and both the ridge correction and the 0.02 term are included in R_A (R03 item 2; the shipped score itself is not
  39| claimed scale invariant). By (TV) and 𝓩, with u := u_{Ũ_b,j} ⊥ 1,
  40| RSS_{Ũ_b} − RSS_{Ũ_b∪{j}} = (uᵀY)² = (δ_{Ũ_b,j} + σZ_{Ũ_b,j})² ≥ δ²/2 − σ²Z² ≥ ½M_n log n − σ²z²_n. Since z²_n ≤ 2(A + 1) log n for
  41| n ≥ n₀ and M_n → ∞, the right side of the display is positive for n ≥ n₀ (−log(2p) ≥ −(A + 1) log n), contradicting
  42| maximality. Hence S₀ ⊆ S̃. The argument is per maximiser and the events do not depend on the maximiser, so it holds
  43| for every maximiser simultaneously. P(𝓔^blk ∩ 𝓩) → 1. ∎
  44| 
  45| **Remarks.** (1) No size ladder (GROW L3.2) and no NEG are needed: with Q = [p] the upper inclusion S̃ ⊆ Q is trivial
  46| and the only feasibility issue (adding a missing truth) is handled by "k̃ < K or S̃ = [p]". (2) The normalisation
  47| (response scaled to yᵀy = n − 1 inside the score) is handled by [GEN-L1] L1.3 as stated in the proof: the scaling
  48| enters only the common constant c′_n, and the ridge correction and the 0.02 term are part of R_A, |R_A| ≤ κ_E. (3) Under (P), K = p for n ≥ n₀; the lemma itself only needs

   6| ## Lemma CS-1D (exact one-dimensional reduction)
   7| 
   8| Exact Gram XᵀX = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I + a11ᵀ], a ∈ (0, 1), response scaled to yᵀy = n − 1, z := Xᵀy. Put
   9| A := (n + 1)(n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B := (n + 1)(n − 1)a, A′ := (n − 1)(1 − a) + 1, B′ := (n − 1)a, N_k := k + A/B,
  10| P_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j², L_T := Σ_{j∈T}z_j. For every T with |T| = k ≤ K,
  11| 
  12|   F(T) = log w(k) + D_k − ν log(0.02 + (n − 1) − (n/A)Φ(T)),   Φ(T) := P_T − L_T²/N_k,
  13|   D_k := −½[(k − 1) log A + log(A + kB) − (k − 1) log A′ − log(A′ + kB′)]  (D_0 := 0), up to the constant log c_n.
  14| 
  15| *Proof.* For |T| = k, G_T = (n − 1)[(1 − a)I_k + a11ᵀ] does not depend on which T; H_T = AI + B11ᵀ,
  16| G_T + I = A′I + B′11ᵀ; det(αI + β11ᵀ) = α^{k−1}(α + kβ) and (αI + β11ᵀ)⁻¹ = α⁻¹(I − β(α + kβ)⁻¹11ᵀ); hence
  17| z_TᵀH_T⁻¹z_T = A⁻¹(P_T − B(A + kB)⁻¹L_T²) = A⁻¹Φ(T) since B/(A + kB) = 1/N_k. Insert into the score of FINAL s1. ∎
  18| (numerics/cs1d.py selftest: agreement with the exact scorer to 5.6e-9 at n = 10⁶; identical LS0 endpoints and move
  19| counts in the selftest — paths themselves were not compared; R06 item 12.)
  20| 
  21| **Move identities (exact).** With c_T := L_T/N_k and N := N_k:
  22|   deletion of e ∈ T:  Φ(T) − Φ(T ∖ e) = (N/(N − 1))(z_e − c_T)²;
  23|   addition of l ∉ T:  Φ(T ∪ l) − Φ(T) = (N/(N + 1))(z_l − c_T)²;
  24|   swap e → l:         Φ(T ∖ e ∪ l) − Φ(T) = u² − v² − (u − v)²/N,  u := z_l − c_T, v := z_e − c_T.
  25| (Elementary algebra from Φ = P − L²/N.) Since F is increasing in Φ at fixed size, the best deletion from T removes the
  26| element of T closest to c_T, the best addition adds the outside element farthest from c_T, and every comparison between
  27| moves reduces to these one-dimensional quantities. For T ⊇ S₀ the signal parts cancel: the null z-values are
  28| z_j = ẑ + τh_j (common ẑ, τ = σ√((n−1)(1−a))/s_Y, h_j iid N(0,1) up to a common shift), truths are displaced by
  29| (n − 1)(1 − a)θ*_j/s_Y, i.e. by order n (order √n in units of τ), and c_T − ẑ is
  30| τ times (Σ_{j∈T}h_j − γ_n)/N with a common γ_n = O_P(1) (L1 U(a) with singleton groups).
  31| 
  32| ## Lemma GAP (deterministic invariant of a deletion path)
  33| 
  34| Suppose LS0 starts at [p] and its first t moves are deletions of nulls, each the element of the current set closest to
  35| its centre c_T. Let D_t be the deleted set. Then (i) D_t is a contiguous run in the order of the null z-values, and
  36| (ii) c_{T_t} lies in the closed interval between the largest kept null below D_t and the smallest kept null above D_t
  37| (with ±∞ if none).
  38| *Proof.* Induction. t = 1: e₁ is the null closest to c_{[p]}; the nearest kept nulls on either side of z_{e₁} are at
  39| least as far from c as z_{e₁}. Step: let e be the kept element closest to c := c_T, say z_e ≥ c (the other case is
  40| symmetric). Then c_{T∖e} = c + (c − z_e)/(N − 1) moves away from z_e by (z_e − c)/(N − 1) < z_e − c ≤ c − ℓ′ (ℓ′ the
  41| nearest kept below; by minimality of e), because N − 1 > 1 (N ≥ s₀ + 1 + A/B > 2 while a null is kept). So the new centre
  42| stays strictly between ℓ′ and the next kept element above z_e; D ∪ {e} is still contiguous. ∎
  43| 
  44| ## Conjecture PATH-CS and where a proof stops
  45| 
  46| **Conjecture PATH-CS.** Exact-Gram CS, fixed a, s₀, θ*, σ², (GC-CS), and the visibility condition making S̃₀ = [p]
  47| (every null has a nonzero conditional factor signal in its block): for every sequence p_n ≤ K (any polynomial growth),
  48| P(LS0 from S̃₀ is a pure deletion path ending at S₀) → 1; in particular D_n → 0.
  49| **Evidence.** D2: exact-Gram simulator, p ∈ {100, 200, 400}, n ∈ {10⁵, 10⁶, 10⁷}: pure deletion paths in every
  50| CS3/CS5/S5/F2 run; F2r p = 200, n = 10⁷: 4/5 pure (one swap); MR1 reached S₀ in every run (D2_summary.md); D3: exact 1-D LS0 from [p], a ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9}, s₀ ∈ {1, 4}, p ∈ {200, 1000},
  51| n ∈ {10⁴, 10⁶, 10⁹} (log p/log n up to 0.75), 720 runs: 720 pure deletion paths, 718 ending at S₀ (D3_summary.md).
  52| **What a proof would need (HEURISTIC outline, not a proved reduction; R06 items 8–10).** With h_k := log w(k) + D_k,
  53| V := 0.02 + n − 1 − (n/A)Φ(T), b := n/A, d := Nδ²/(N − 1) (δ the distance from c_T to the nearest kept null),
  54| a₊ := N max_{l∉T}(z_l − c_T)²/(N + 1) and s₊ := max over swaps of Φ(T ∖ e ∪ l) − Φ(T), the exact gains are
  55| Δ_d = h_{k−1} − h_k − ν log(1 + bd/V), Δ_a = h_{k+1} − h_k − ν log(1 − ba₊/V), Δ_s = −ν log(1 − bs₊/V); the best null
  56| deletion is the chosen move precisely when Δ_d > 0 exceeds Δ_a, Δ_s and the truth-removing gains (tie rule aside). By
  57| Lemma GAP the deleted values lie in the gap containing c_T, so bounding a₊ and s₊ reduces to the balance of the gap
  58| around c_T. While kept nulls remain on both sides, an induction suggests |d₊ − d₋| ≤ (d₊ + d₋)/N + s* (s* a spacing of
  59| consecutive null values), which would make s₊ ≤ (d₊ + d₋)s* — a sketch, not checked. The open case is a late stage in
  60| which all remaining kept nulls lie on one side (m ≥ 2 of them): c_T is pulled towards them and the swap identity gives an
  61| S-gain ≈ 4M²(m − 1)/N (M² ≈ 2 log p) against a deletion gain ≈ log n + M²(1 − r²N/(N − 1)), r := (s₀ + A/B)/N; for large
  62| log p/log n and m ≥ m*(a, s₀) this bound does not exclude a swap. An independent-sign heuristic suggests a scale 2^{−m}
  63| for such endings at fixed m; the probability of these adaptively selected endings is unproved. D3 recorded no swap at
  64| all. Excluding such swaps would establish PATH-CS (pure deletion); controlling a bounded or cap-compatible number of
  65| late swaps would establish only the weaker LS0-discovery conclusion (enough for D_n → 0 via [OP]).
  66| 
  67| ## p > K and k ≥ 2 (not claimed)
  68| * **p > K.** If every variable is visible, S̃₀ has size exactly K; the outside set is then not a gap around the centre,
  69|   and the swap identity predicts improving swaps that bring in outside elements far from c_T, with gain of order
  70|   ρ·2 log p (ρ = n/(n − K) ≈ 2) against a deletion gain ≈ log n. A heuristic count of such swaps is (p − K)·n^{−1/4+o(1)},
  71|   which would exceed the MR1 slack ℓ_n + s₀. Not tested (exact Gram needs p ≤ n − 1 and the regime requires the
  72|   asymptotic start mode); heuristic only.
  73| * **k ≥ 2 global factors.** L1 does not prove a multiple-global-factor theorem. One possible sufficient condition for a
  74|   direct matrix extension of the Cauchy–Schwarz step is a lower bound on λ_min of the T-restricted loading Gram
  75|   proportional to the number of groups hit (with a representation-dependent scale and a treatment of effective rank;
  76|   rank-deficient aligned loadings may reduce to the scalar case). Any obstruction for k ≥ 2 is conjectural.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W2-FAC-PK — METHOD_REQUIREMENTS (HQ decides on adoption)
   2| 
   3| Scope of the evidence: exact-Gram compound symmetry, K < p ≤ n − 1 (STATEMENT v3.1 — LOCKED, including the flagged
   4| cap-evaluation restriction for delivery). Statuses: REPORT.md §3.
   5| 
   6| ## The problem with the merged cap (MR1 (C-GROW), ℓ_n + |S̃₀|)
   7| Theorem NEG (L2; hypotheses (CS), (θ) with θ̄ ≠ 0, liminf p/K > 16/15, (PB)): the start mode is size-saturated
   8| (|S̃₀| = K) and the first ⌊n^β⌋ moves of the LS0 path are size-preserving swaps (any fixed β < ½), so LS0 with any
   9| nonnegative integer cap a ≤ |S̃₀| − s₀ − 2 + ⌊n^β⌋ never scores S₀ (w.p. → 1). The LS0 route to reported-model
  10| consistency is therefore unavailable for MR1 on this class, and no O(log n) or polylog allowance can repair it.
  11| This is a statement about the LS0 route, not about the full fit (the full-method question is open; STATEMENT (P6)).
  12| 
  13| ## Proved sufficient change (MR-PK)
  14| Theorem PATH (L3; hypotheses (CS), (θ), K + 16s₀ + 1 ≤ p ≤ n − 1, blocks ≤ 16): for every fixed δ > 0 the uncapped LS0
  15| path ends at S₀ (a strict local maximum) after at most (1 + δ)|S̃₀| moves, w.p. → 1. Hence **any LS0 cap rule
  16| a ≥ max(ℓ_n, ⌈(1 + δ)|S̃₀|⌉) for a fixed δ > 0** makes LS0 end certified at S₀ (Theorem FAC-PK, (P4)). Candidate rules:
  17| 
  18| | rule | δ | proved on this class | worst-case LS0 scans | note |
  19| |---|---|---|---|---|
  20| | ℓ_n + 2|S̃₀| | 1 | yes (any p in range) | ℓ_n + 2K + 1 | largest of the linear-in-mode allowances; dominates the other rows when |S̃₀| = K (observed m*/K ≤ 1.26 in N3) [R07-3] |
  21| | ℓ_n + ⌈(1 + δ)|S̃₀|⌉, e.g. δ = ¼ (0 < δ ≤ 1) | δ | yes (asymptotic) | ℓ_n + ⌈(1 + δ)K⌉ + 1 | cheaper; N3 has finite-n runs with m*/K up to 1.26 (n = 2000, p = n − 1) |
  22| | max(ℓ_n + |S̃₀|, p) | ≥ 1/16 under (PK) | yes when p ≥ (1 + 1/16)K | max(ℓ_n + K, p) + 1 | equals MR1 when p ≤ ℓ_n + |S̃₀|; tied to p, unbounded relative to K for p ≫ n designs |
  23| 
  24| **"Minimal".** Proved: allowances over |S̃₀| of order ≤ n^β (β < ½) fail; allowances ≥ δ|S̃₀| (any fixed δ > 0) suffice.
  25| No optimality is claimed in between. Heuristically the needed allowance is the swap count W ≈ p·n^{−1/(4M_W)} = o(K)
  26| (N1/N3), but no bound on W is proved. **Recommendation:** ℓ_n + 2|S̃₀| for robustness at moderate n; HQ may prefer a
  27| smaller δ for cost.
  28| 
  29| **Transfer (R05-4).** Lemma CAP (FINAL s7) is monotone in the cap for caps ≥ ℓ_n. All three rules in the table satisfy
  30| a ≥ ℓ_n + |S̃₀| (= MR1), so LS0's scored set contains MR1's. What transfers under the original hypotheses: positive
  31| discovery statements (LS0 scores S₀), certified-endpoint statements on the events where the smaller-cap search ends
  32| certified, and the joint-with-output HPM statements derived from them (FINAL s7 "What survives"). What does not transfer
  33| verbatim: worst-case resource statements (re-charged below), negative discovery statements (they transfer only
  34| downward), flags/metadata, and cap-dependent no-output events. A rule below MR1 must still satisfy a ≥ ℓ_n (e.g.
  35| max(ℓ_n, ⌈(1 + δ)|S̃₀|⌉)) to inherit even the legacy-cap results.
  36| 
  37| ## Implementation (option plumbing; not done by this ticket) [R07-1]
  38| The cap rule is evaluated after the start mode by O(1) arithmetic (needed for the delivery argument, L4 (β)). Today the
  39| R→C++ interface collapses every non-legacy value to MR1, so a new rule needs plumbing, not a two-line edit:
  40| * `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_run.R:101` — keep and validate distinct values (e.g. `"ell_n"`, `"ell_n_plus_mode"`,
  41|   `"ell_n_plus_2mode"`, or a δ-parameterised rule with a fixed validated δ and the ceiling ⌈(1 + δ)|S̃₀|⌉) instead of mapping
  42|   everything except `"ell_n"` to `"ell_n_plus_mode"`.
  43| * `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/cpp/v3_core.cpp:394,404` — carry an enum/string instead of the Boolean `ls0_cap_plus_mode`;
  44|   `v3_core.cpp:473` — compute the selected cap after `start_mode` (range check kept); `v3_core.cpp:479` — matching label.
  45| * `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/v3_fit.R:44` (and the call sites `v3_fit.R:114–115, 145`) — pass the selected rule's worst-case
  46|   scan count (e.g. `b$ell + 2*K + 1`) into the initial and escalation preflights; keep the existing bounds for the old
  47|   options; archive formula unchanged in form; label at `v3_fit.R:62`.
  48| Keep the range check (`v3_core.cpp:474`) unreachable on admissible inputs: compute the cap in 64-bit; ℓ_n + 2K ≤ INT_MAX
  49| holds under MACH / the allocation premise (R11 optional 2). When plumbing, compute the preflight's worst-case scan count from the same base cap LS0 uses (today the preflight uses
  50| `b$ell`, LS0 uses `ro$ls0_ell`) [R09-opt1]. Alternatively, if HQ adopts MR-PK as a global replacement of MR1, state that explicitly and drop the extra option.
  51| 
  52| ## Cost (upper bounds on LS0's worst-case terms only; not a statement about total fit time)
  53| For a rule with worst case a_max ≤ ℓ_n + 2K: LS0 score requests ≤ 1 + (a_max + 1)q(p), q(p) = p + p²/4; preflight
  54| time charge 2(a_max + 1)q(p)ŝ_K (vs 2(ℓ_n + K + 1)q(p)ŝ_K); archive (2s + 4)(12K + 256) + 96s + 4(8W + 4K + 96) + 4096 bytes
  55| with s = a_max + 1. Delivery envelopes (Proposition F, A1/A2 form): LS0 terms with K replaced by 2K:
  56| W_G′ := W̄ + C·2K·q(p)[n³ + p(n + 2)], M_G′ := M̄ + C·2K(2K + 1), P̄_LS0′ := (ℓ_n + 2K + 1)q(p)(τU_K + τ₀)/100. Each LS0
  57| worst-case charge is at most (a_max + 1)/(ℓ_n + K + 1) ≤ 2 times its MR1 charge (equality only for scan-proportional
  58| terms); conservative envelope increments and total fit time are not claimed to scale by this factor. For rules with a ≥ ℓ_n + |S̃₀| (all three in the table)
  59| realised LS0 work is identical wherever the MR1 search already ends certified (Lemma CAP(a)); not for smaller rules.
  60| 
  61| **Operational finding (for HQ; numerics/full_method/NF_summary.md).** Already under MR1, the merged preflight's LS0
  62| worst-case time charge is ≈ 5.3·10⁵ s (≈ 146 h) for n = 600, p = 450 (K = 300, 312 scans, 1.59·10⁷ requests,
  63| ŝ_K = 0.0166 s on the local machine). Observed: the 2-hour attempts returned `resource_limit` at preflight; the 1000-hour
  64| attempt timed out after 1200 s of wall clock. Extrapolation (not an observed run): the same recorded charge would also
  65| reject a 24-hour allocation, e.g. the default 8 GB / 24 h [R07-5]. Delivery theorems assume the amended allocation; MR-PK increases this charge by at most a factor two. The
  66| worst-case charge grows like K·p²·ŝ_K, where ŝ_K is measured separately at size K (its dependence on K was not measured
  67| here) [R07-6]. Whether realised LS0 time is close to this charge
  68| was not measured here (no fit completed locally; W2-SIM R2 records timings$ls0). Any tighter valid preflight bound
  69| would be a separate engineering item (finding only).
  70| 
  71| ## Not changed
  72| Prior, SMC kernels, calibration, tables, start-mode rule, final local search (cap ℓ_n).

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  13| ## X1.1 Exact rotation representation
  14| 
  15| Represent the rows as x^r_i = m + √ρ F_i 1 + √(1 − ρ)U_i with F_i ~ N(0, 1), U_i ~ N_p(0, I) iid (this is exactly
  16| N_p(m, Σ)). Centring gives, for every column j, g_j := Cx^r_{·j} = √ρ f + √(1 − ρ)u_j with f := CF, u_j := CU_{·j};
  17| e := Cε. The n-vectors f, u_1, …, u_p, e/σ are iid N(0, C) (standard Gaussian in V), independent.
  18| 
  19| Define e₁ := e/‖e‖, η := fᵀe₁, f_⊥ := f − ηe₁, φ := ‖f_⊥‖, e₂ := f_⊥/φ, and for every j:
  20| ξ_j := u_jᵀe₁, a_j := u_jᵀe₂, u_j^⊥ := u_j − ξ_je₁ − a_je₂ ∈ V₃ := V ∩ {e₁, e₂}^⊥ (dim N).
  21| 
  22| **Lemma X1.1.** ‖e‖, η, φ, ξ = (ξ_j), a = (a_j) are mutually independent, ‖e‖²/σ² ~ χ²_{n−1}, η ~ N(0, 1),
  23| φ² ~ χ²_{n−2}, ξ_j, a_j iid N(0, 1); and W := (u_j^⊥ᵀu_l^⊥)_{j,l≤p} ~ W_p(N, I) is independent of
  24| (‖e‖, η, φ, ξ, a).

  26| *Proof.* e/σ is standard Gaussian in V: ‖e‖ and e₁ are independent, e₁ uniform on the unit sphere of V. Given e₁,
  27| f is standard Gaussian in V, so η = fᵀe₁ ~ N(0, 1) and f_⊥ (standard Gaussian in the (n − 2)-dimensional space
  28| V ∩ e₁^⊥) are conditionally independent; the conditional joint law of (η, φ) is N(0, 1) ⊗ χ_{n−2}, which does not depend
  29| on e₁ (the ambient vector f_⊥ itself is of course not independent of e₁ — R03 X1 item 1); given (e₁, φ), e₂ is uniform on
  30| the unit sphere of V ∩ e₁^⊥. Given

   1| # X3 — Deterministic soft-gap lemma for ϖ-approximate argmin deletions
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)**; lemma check R03 FAILED as written on (iii) (MAJOR) → repaired as R03 proposed;
   4| fresh re-check R03b (Codex Sol high, reviews/R03b_X3_recheck_sol.md): **VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS**, no FATAL/MAJOR, 3 MINOR
   5| applied (reviews/R03_disposition.md). Falsification numerics: numerics/n3x_softgap.py → N3X_out.txt (random
   6| configurations and adversarial ϖ-approximate choices; the full band containment (viii), the initial-phase bounds
   7| (vii) and the crossing-width consequence of (iii) are checked at every step).
   8| 
   9| This lemma is purely deterministic. It replaces FACB L4.1(i) (exact gap invariant) when the deletion rule is only
  10| approximately the argmin.
  11| 
  12| ## Setting
  13| 
  14| 𝒩 a finite index set with distinct reals (ξ_l)_{l∈𝒩}; constants B ∈ ℝ, κ′ > 1, ϖ ≥ 0. Kept sets
  15| K_0 := 𝒩 ⊋ K_1 ⊋ … ⊋ K_I, K_{i+1} = K_i ∖ {j_i}, |K_i| ≥ 1 for i < I (any length I ≥ 0: every claim is a statement
  16| about this given **prefix** and uses no step beyond I; R02 item 1). Centres
  17| x_i := (Σ_{l∈K_i}ξ_l + B)/(|K_i| + κ′), so that (drift identity) x_{i+1} = x_i − (ξ_{j_i} − x_i)/(|K_i| − 1 + κ′).
  18| Nondegeneracy: ξ_l ≠ x_i for all l, i. **Rule (R_ϖ):** for every i < I,
  19|   |ξ_{j_i} − x_i| ≤ d_i + 2ϖ,  d_i := min_{l∈K_i}|ξ_l − x_i|.
  20| Define a_i := max{ξ_l : l ∈ K_i, ξ_l < x_i} (−∞ if none), b_i := min{ξ_l : l ∈ K_i, ξ_l > x_i} (+∞ if none),
  21| L_i := x_i − a_i, R_i := b_i − x_i, ω_i := b_i − a_i, D_i := 𝒩 ∖ K_i.
  22| (In X4: 𝒩 = 𝒩*, B = Σ_{S₀}ξ − ϱ, κ′ = s₀ + κ, so x_i = x_{T_i}.)
  23| 
  24| ## Claims
  25| 
  26| (i) K_i ∩ (a_i, b_i) = ∅ and a_i < x_i < b_i (definitions); if K_i ≠ ∅ at least one side is nonempty (if K_i = ∅,
  27|   e.g. a fully exhausted prefix, a_i = −∞, b_i = +∞ and the hole is the whole line).
  28| (ii) a_i − 2ϖ ≤ ξ_{j_i} ≤ b_i + 2ϖ, and ξ_{j_i} ≤ a_i or ξ_{j_i} ≥ b_i.
  29| (iii) **Crossing.** Call step i a crossing if K_{i+1} has a point strictly between x_{i+1} and x_i. If step i is a
  30|   crossing then both a_i, b_i are finite, d_i = min(L_i, R_i) < 2ϖ/(|K_i| − 2 + κ′) and ω_i ≤ 2d_i + 2ϖ; in particular
  31|   ω_i < 4ϖ if |K_i| ≥ 3, and ω_i < c(κ′)ϖ, c(κ′) := 2 + 4/(κ′ − 1), for every |K_i| ≥ 1 (R03 item 1).
  32| (iv) **Monotonicity.** If step i is not a crossing then a_{i+1} ≤ a_i and b_{i+1} ≥ b_i; in particular ω_{i+1} ≥ ω_i.
  33| (v) If ω_{i₀} ≥ 4ϖ for some i₀ and |K_i| ≥ 3 for i₀ ≤ i < I, then no step i ≥ i₀ is a crossing and [a_i, b_i] ⊆ [a_{i′}, b_{i′}] for i₀ ≤ i ≤ i′ ≤ I.
  34| (vi) In the situation of (v), every l deleted at a step i ∈ [i₀, i′) satisfies a_{i′} − 2ϖ ≤ ξ_l ≤ b_{i′} + 2ϖ.
  35| (vii) **Initial phase (prefix form).** Let Q be the maximal number of points ξ_l in a closed interval of length 9ϖ,
  36|   assume 4Qϖ/(|K_0| − Q − 1 + κ′) ≤ ϖ/10 and |K_i| ≥ 3 for i < I. Put i₀ := min{i ≤ I : ω_i ≥ 4ϖ} (i₀ := ∞ if there is
  37|   none) and M := min(i₀, I). Then M ≤ Q, |x_i − x_0| ≤ ϖ/10 for every i ≤ M, and every point deleted at a step i < M lies
  38|   in [x_0 − 4.1ϖ, x_0 + 4.1ϖ]. (If i₀ > I, the whole prefix is narrow; it then has I ≤ Q steps.)
  39| (viii) **Conclusion.** Under the assumptions of (vii): for every i ≤ I,
  40|   𝒩 ∩ (a_i, b_i) ⊆ D_i ⊆ 𝒩 ∩ (a_i − 4.3ϖ, b_i + 4.3ϖ),
  41|   i.e. D_i is the interval part 𝒩 ∩ (a_i, b_i) plus a subset of the band (a_i − 4.3ϖ, a_i] ∪ [b_i, b_i + 4.3ϖ).
  42| (ix) **Sparse case.** If every two distinct ξ_l differ by more than max(9, c(κ′))ϖ, then for every i ≤ I (any |K_i| ≥ 1),
  43|   no step is a crossing and D_i = 𝒩 ∩ (a_i, b_i) exactly (FACB L4.1(i)).
  44| 
  45| ## Proofs
  46| 
  47| (i) By definition no kept point lies in (a_i, x_i) ∪ (x_i, b_i), and ξ_l ≠ x_i. If K_i ≠ ∅, nondegeneracy places at least
  48| one kept point on one side of x_i; if K_i = ∅, a_i = −∞, b_i = +∞ and the claims hold trivially (R03b item 1).
  49| 
  50| (ii) If ξ_{j_i} > x_i then ξ_{j_i} ≥ b_i (b_i is the smallest kept point above x_i) and, as d_i ≤ R_i,
  51| ξ_{j_i} − x_i ≤ R_i + 2ϖ, i.e. ξ_{j_i} ≤ b_i + 2ϖ. Symmetrically if ξ_{j_i} < x_i.
  52| 
  53| (iii) Suppose ξ_{j_i} > x_i (then x_{i+1} < x_i by the drift identity); write m := |K_i| − 1 + κ′ (> 1) and
  54| h := ξ_{j_i} − x_i = m(x_i − x_{i+1}). A crossing means some kept l ∈ K_{i+1} has x_{i+1} < ξ_l < x_i; then a_i is finite and
  55| a_i ≥ ξ_l > x_{i+1}, so L_i < h/m; and b_i ≤ ξ_{j_i} is finite with R_i ≤ h. By (R_ϖ), h ≤ d_i + 2ϖ.
  56| *Case d_i = L_i:* L_i < (L_i + 2ϖ)/m gives L_i(m − 1) < 2ϖ; and R_i ≤ h ≤ L_i + 2ϖ gives ω_i ≤ 2d_i + 2ϖ.
  57| *Case d_i = R_i < L_i:* R_i < L_i < (R_i + 2ϖ)/m gives R_i(m − 1) < 2ϖ; and L_i < (R_i + 2ϖ)/m < R_i + 2ϖ gives
  58| ω_i < 2d_i + 2ϖ.
  59| In both cases d_i < 2ϖ/(m − 1) = 2ϖ/(|K_i| − 2 + κ′) and ω_i ≤ 2d_i + 2ϖ. If |K_i| ≥ 3 then m − 1 > 2, d_i < ϖ and
  60| ω_i < 4ϖ; in general m − 1 ≥ κ′ − 1, d_i < 2ϖ/(κ′ − 1) and ω_i < c(κ′)ϖ. The case ξ_{j_i} < x_i is the mirror image
  61| (L ↔ R). (The bound is on d_i, not on the side opposite to the deletion: R03's configurations {0.1, −2.1, −10}, B = 12,
  62| κ′ = 2, ϖ = 1, deleting −2.1 (d = R = 0.1, L = 2.1) and its reflection show that a direction-specific bound on L, or a
  63| strict inequality ω < 2d + 2ϖ, would be false.)
  64| 
  65| (iv) Let ξ_{j_i} > x_i (so x_{i+1} < x_i), no crossing. Kept points of K_{i+1} below x_{i+1}: they are the kept points of K_i
  66| below x_i other than those in [x_{i+1}, x_i) — of which there are none (no crossing; ξ_l ≠ x_{i+1}) — so a_{i+1} = a_i.
  67| Kept points above x_{i+1}: those of K_i above x_i, minus j_i, plus none from (x_{i+1}, x_i]; so b_{i+1} ≥ b_i. The case
  68| ξ_{j_i} < x_i is symmetric (b_{i+1} = b_i, a_{i+1} ≤ a_i).
  69| 
  70| (v) Induction on i ≥ i₀: ω_i ≥ 4ϖ ⇒ step i is not a crossing (iii) ⇒ [a_i, b_i] ⊆ [a_{i+1}, b_{i+1}] and ω_{i+1} ≥ ω_i ≥ 4ϖ (iv).
  71| 
  72| (vi) By (ii) at step i, a_i − 2ϖ ≤ ξ_l ≤ b_i + 2ϖ, and [a_i, b_i] ⊆ [a_{i′}, b_{i′}] by (v).
  73| 
  74| (vii) For a narrow step i (ω_i < 4ϖ, i < I): both a_i, b_i are finite, d_i = min(L_i, R_i) ≤ ω_i/2 < 2ϖ and, by (R_ϖ),
  75| |ξ_{j_i} − x_i| < 4ϖ; by the drift identity |x_{i+1} − x_i| < 4ϖ/(|K_i| − 1 + κ′). Suppose M ≥ Q + 1. Then steps
  76| 0, …, Q are all narrow and belong to the prefix (Q < M ≤ I), and |K_i| = |K_0| − i ≥ |K_0| − Q for i ≤ Q. By induction,
  77| for i = 0, …, Q: |x_i − x_0| ≤ i·4ϖ/(|K_0| − Q − 1 + κ′) ≤ 4Qϖ/(|K_0| − Q − 1 + κ′) ≤ ϖ/10 (only the Q increments
  78| x_1 − x_0, …, x_Q − x_{Q−1} are used, R02 item 1). So the Q + 1 deleted points ξ_{j_0}, …, ξ_{j_Q} are distinct and lie in
  79| [x_0 − 4.1ϖ, x_0 + 4.1ϖ], an interval of length 8.2ϖ ≤ 9ϖ — contradicting the definition of Q. Hence M ≤ Q. Repeating
  80| the induction for i = 0, …, M (now M ≤ Q, all steps i < M narrow and in the prefix) gives |x_i − x_0| ≤ ϖ/10 for i ≤ M
  81| and ξ_{j_i} ∈ [x_0 − 4.1ϖ, x_0 + 4.1ϖ] for i < M.
  82| 
  83| (viii) For i ≤ M: D_i ⊆ [x_0 − 4.1ϖ, x_0 + 4.1ϖ] by (vii); and a_i < x_i ≤ x_0 + ϖ/10, b_i > x_i ≥ x_0 − ϖ/10, so
  84| x_0 − 4.1ϖ > a_i − 4.3ϖ and x_0 + 4.1ϖ < b_i + 4.3ϖ. For M < i ≤ I (then i₀ = M ≤ I): points deleted before i₀ lie in
  85| [x_0 − 4.1ϖ, x_0 + 4.1ϖ] ⊆ (a_{i₀} − 4.3ϖ, b_{i₀} + 4.3ϖ) ⊆ (a_i − 4.3ϖ, b_i + 4.3ϖ) by (v); points deleted at steps in
  86| [i₀, i) lie in [a_i − 2ϖ, b_i + 2ϖ] by (vi). The left inclusion is (i).
  87| 
  88| (ix) A crossing at step i requires both sides nonempty (iii), hence ω_i ≥ (minimal spacing) > c(κ′)ϖ, contradicting (iii).
  89| So no step is a crossing, and by (iv) the intervals [a_i, b_i] are nested increasing (no |K| restriction is needed for
  90| (iv)). By (ii) and nesting every deleted point lies in [a_i − 2ϖ, b_i + 2ϖ]; the only point of 𝒩 in [b_i, b_i + 2ϖ] is b_i
  91| itself (spacing > 2ϖ) and it is kept, similarly at a_i; so D_i ⊆ (a_i, b_i); the reverse inclusion is (i). ∎
  92| 
  93| (Zero tolerance, R03b item 2: when ϖ = 0 every finite a_i or b_i is the coordinate of a kept index; distinctness
  94| excludes a deleted point from either finite endpoint, so the closed bound of (vi) gives strict open containment; here
  95| i₀ = M = 0, and for I = 0 the conclusion is immediate from D_0 = ∅.)
  96| 
  97| **Remark.** For steps with |K_i| ≥ 3, (iii)–(v) are the whole mechanism: a kept point can be overtaken by the centre
  98| only when the hole around the centre is narrower than 4ϖ; once the hole is ≥ 4ϖ wide it only grows, as in FACB L4.1,
  99| and each new deletion overshoots the current kept edge by at most 2ϖ. With fewer kept points the threshold is c(κ′)ϖ

 101| wide; (iii) with c(11/10) = 42 is not violated).

   4| R02 VERIFIED). Falsification numerics: `numerics/n4_nar_check.py` Part 1 → `numerics/n4_out.txt` (2-D grids,
   5| exp(−‖Δ‖/φ), φ ∈ {0.8, 1.2, 2}; worst ratio |(A⁻¹)_ij|/bound over Σ and 29 random principal submatrices ≤ 0.32;
   6| observed sup ‖β_A‖₁ ≤ 1.27; the printed "L0" there is a TRUNCATED (m ≤ 4000) lower approximation of the analytic L₀,
   7| and the t* root search uses the truncated series — the numerics are a falsification probe of CT_d and sampled regression
   8| norms only, not a certificate; the analytic proofs below are the certificate [R02-4]). Check record: R02 (Codex
   9| gpt-6.1-sol high, `reviews/R02_L1L3_check_sol.md`): VERIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENTS; amendments 1, 4, 5 applied
  10| (`reviews/R02_disposition.md`).
  11| 
  12| **Notation [R01-3].** In LOC_d(c, C, K, a) and Lemma CT_d the letter K is the decay-envelope constant (K_dec in
  13| STATEMENT); the method's model-size cap is K_n = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋).
  14| 
  15| ## L3.0 Sites and packing
  16| A *site map* is x : I → ℝ^d (I finite) with ‖x_i − x_j‖ ≥ 1 for i ≠ j (Euclidean norm; d ≥ 1 fixed); d_ij := ‖x_i − x_j‖.
  17| **Packing fact.** For every i and R > 0, #{j : d_ij < R} ≤ (2R + 1)^d; hence for every integer m ≥ 1,
  18| #{j : m ≤ d_ij < m + 1} ≤ (2m + 3)^d.
  19| *Proof.* The balls B(x_j, ½) are pairwise disjoint (separation ≥ 1); for d_ij < R they lie in B(x_i, R + ½). Comparing
  20| volumes, the count is ≤ ((R + ½)/½)^d = (2R + 1)^d; for the shell take R = m + 1. ∎
  21| (Integer positions on a line, d = 1, give #{j : d_ij = m} ≤ 2; the packing bound (2m+3) is weaker but sufficient.)
  22| 
  23| ## L3.1 Lemma CT_d
  24| Let A be real symmetric on I with λ_min(A) ≥ α > 0 (no upper spectral bound needed) [R07-14], and |A_ij| ≤ K e^{−a d_ij} for i ≠ j (K, a > 0). For
  25| 0 ≤ t < a put
  26|   S(t) := K Σ_{m≥1} (2m + 3)^d e^{−(a−t)m}(1 − e^{−t(m+1)}).
  27| S is finite, continuous and nondecreasing on [0, a), S(0) = 0, and S(t) → ∞ as t ↑ a. Let
  28| t* = t*(α, K, a, d) := max{t ∈ [0, a) : S(t) ≤ α/2} ∈ (0, a). Then for all i, j ∈ I:  |(A⁻¹)_ij| ≤ (2/α)e^{−t*d_ij}.
  29| 
  30| *Proof.* (i) Each term is continuous, nondecreasing in t and the series converges uniformly on [0, a − ε] (terms
  31| ≤ K(2m + 3)^d e^{−εm}), giving finiteness, continuity, monotonicity and S(0) = 0; as t ↑ a, for any M the partial sum
  32| up to M tends to K Σ_{m≤M}(2m + 3)^d(1 − e^{−a(m+1)}) ≥ K(1 − e^{−2a})Σ_{m≤M}(2m+3)^d, which is unbounded in M; so
  33| S → ∞. Hence {S ≤ α/2} = [0, t*] with 0 < t* < a (continuity at 0 gives t* > 0).
  34| (ii) Fix j and φ(y) := ‖y − x_j‖ (1-Lipschitz). D := diag(e^{t*φ(x_i)}), A_t := DAD⁻¹ (entries A_ik e^{t*(φ(x_i)−φ(x_k))}),
  35| E := A_t − A. E_ii = 0, and for i ≠ k, |E_ik| ≤ |A_ik|(e^{t*|φ(x_i)−φ(x_k)|} − 1) ≤ K e^{−a d_ik}(e^{t*d_ik} − 1)
  36| (|e^s − 1| ≤ e^{|s|} − 1, and |φ(x_i) − φ(x_k)| ≤ d_ik).
  37| (iii) Schur test. For fixed i, group k by the shell m ≤ d_ik < m + 1 (m ≥ 1 since d_ik ≥ 1). On such a shell,
  38| e^{−ad}(e^{t*d} − 1) = e^{−(a−t*)d}(1 − e^{−t*d}) ≤ e^{−(a−t*)m}(1 − e^{−t*(m+1)}). With the packing fact,
  39| Σ_k |E_ik| ≤ S(t*) ≤ α/2; the bound is symmetric in (i, k), so column sums obey it too; ‖E‖₂ ≤ √(‖E‖₁‖E‖_∞) ≤ α/2.
  40| (iv) ‖A⁻¹‖₂ ≤ 1/α, so A_t = A(I + A⁻¹E) is invertible with ‖A_t⁻¹‖₂ ≤ 2/α; A_t⁻¹ = DA⁻¹D⁻¹ has (i, j) entry
  41| (A⁻¹)_ij e^{t*(φ(x_i)−φ(x_j))} = (A⁻¹)_ij e^{t*d_ij} (φ(x_j) = 0), and entries are bounded by the spectral norm. ∎
  42| Remarks. No upper spectral bound is used. The bound is uniform in |I| and in the site map. Any norm on ℝ^d works with (2m+3)^d replaced by
  43| the corresponding packing constant; we fix the Euclidean norm.
  44| 
  45| ## L3.2 Class LOC_d and Lemma CD_d
  46| **Definition.** LOC_d(c, C, K, a): unit-diagonal Σ on [p] with spectrum in [c, C] (0 < c ≤ 1 ≤ C) and a site map
  47| x : [p] → ℝ^d (separation ≥ 1) such that either (LOC_d-Σ) |Σ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a d_jk} (j ≠ k), or (LOC_d-Θ) Θ := Σ⁻¹ obeys
  48| |Θ_jk| ≤ K e^{−a d_jk} (j ≠ k). For sequences the constants are fixed; the site maps may vary with n.
  49| 
  50| **Lemma CD_d.** Let Σ ∈ LOC_d(c, C, K, a), W ~ N(0, Σ). Define
  51|   (LOC_d-Σ): t₁ := t*(c, K, a, d), K₁ := 2/c;   (LOC_d-Θ): t₁ := a, K₁ := K;   t₂ := t*(1/C, K₁, t₁, d), K₂ := 2C.
  52| Then for every U ⊆ [p] and distinct j, k ∉ U:
  53|  (a) |Cov(W_j, W_k | W_U)| ≤ K₂e^{−t₂d_jk};
  54|  (b) c ≤ Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ 1, and for every V ⊆ [p] ∖ U the conditional covariance matrix Cov(W_V | W_U) has
  55|      spectrum in [c, C];
  56|  (c) under (LOC_d-Θ), Σ obeys (LOC_d-Σ) with constants (2C, t*(1/C, K, a, d)); under (LOC_d-Σ), Θ obeys (LOC_d-Θ)
  57|      with (2/c, t*(c, K, a, d)).
  58| *Proof* [R02-1]. As APP L2_CT Lemma CD with Lemma CT replaced by Lemma CT_d. Under either branch, |Θ_jk| ≤ K₁e^{−t₁d_jk}
  59| (j ≠ k): under (LOC_d-Σ) by CT_d applied to Σ (α = c), under (LOC_d-Θ) by assumption; this with CT_d applied to Θ
  60| (α = 1/C) also gives (c). Let H := [p] ∖ U (the FULL unconditioned complement). For Gaussian W, block inversion gives
  61| Cov(W_H | W_U) = (Θ_HH)⁻¹. Θ_HH is a principal submatrix of Θ: spectrum in [1/C, 1/c], off-diagonal entries
  62| ≤ K₁e^{−t₁d}, with the restricted (still separated) site map. CT_d (α = 1/C) gives (a) for j, k ∈ H, and the spectrum of
  63| (Θ_HH)⁻¹ lies in [c, C]. For an arbitrary V ⊆ H, Cov(W_V | W_U) is a principal submatrix of Cov(W_H | W_U) (NOT (Θ_VV)⁻¹,
  64| which would condition on H ∖ V as well), so by interlacing its spectrum lies in [c, C]; in particular Var(W_j | W_U) ≥ c,
  65| and Var(W_j | W_U) ≤ Var(W_j) = 1. ∎
  66| 
  67| ## L3.3 Lemma RB (ℓ¹ bound for population regression coefficients)
  68| Let Σ ∈ LOC_d(c, C, K, a). Let (K_Σ, t_Σ) := (K, a) under (LOC_d-Σ) with t_Σ′ := t*(c, K, a, d), and under (LOC_d-Θ)
  69| (K_Σ, t_Σ) := (2C, t*(1/C, K, a, d)) (CD_d(c)) with t_Σ′ := t*(c, 2C, t_Σ, d). For l ∈ [p] and A ⊆ [p] ∖ {l}, let
  70| β_A(l) := Σ_AA⁻¹Σ_{Al} (coefficients of E[W_l | W_A] = W_Aβ_A(l)). Then
  71|   |β_A(l)_v| ≤ (2/c)e^{−t_Σ′ d_lv}  (v ∈ A),    ‖β_A(l)‖₁ ≤ L₀ := (2/c) Σ_{m≥1}(2m + 3)^d e^{−t_Σ′ m} < ∞.
  72| *Proof.* B := Σ_{A∪{l}} is a principal submatrix: spectrum in [c, C], off-diagonal entries ≤ K_Σe^{−t_Σ d}. Let
  73| Ψ := B⁻¹. Block inversion gives β_A(l)_v = −Ψ_vl/Ψ_ll and Ψ_ll = 1/Var(W_l | W_A) ≥ 1. Lemma CT_d applied to B
  74| (α = c, constants (K_Σ, t_Σ)) gives |Ψ_vl| ≤ (2/c)e^{−t_Σ′d_vl}. Sum over shells with the packing fact
  75| (d_lv ≥ 1). ∎
  76| 
  77| ## L3.4 Lemma TAIL (far conditioning)
  78| Let Σ ∈ LOC_d, l ∈ [p], T ⊆ [p] ∖ {l}, r > 0, T′ := {v ∈ T : d_lv ≤ r}. Then
  79|  (a) Var(E[W_l | W_T] − E[W_l | W_{T′}]) ≤ κ(r) := (K₂²/c) Σ_{m ≥ ⌊r⌋, m≥1} (2m + 3)^d e^{−2t₂m}, and κ(r) → 0 as r → ∞;
  80|  (b) Var(W_l | W_{T′}) = Var(W_l | W_T) + Var(E[W_l | W_T] − E[W_l | W_{T′}]).
  81| *Proof.* (b) e_T := W_l − E[W_l | W_T] is uncorrelated with every linear function of W_T, in particular with
  82| D := E[W_l | W_T] − E[W_l | W_{T′}]; e_{T′} = e_T + D. (a) As in APP L3.6 Step 3: with V := W_{T∖T′} − E[W_{T∖T′} | W_{T′}],
  83| D = Cov(e_{T′}, V)M⁻¹V, M := Cov(W_{T∖T′} | W_{T′}), so Var D = bᵀM⁻¹b ≤ ‖b‖²/c with b_v := Cov(W_l, W_v | W_{T′})
  84| [R02-5: vector renamed]. By CD_d(b) (V = T ∖ T′ ⊆ [p] ∖ T′), λ_min(M) ≥ c; by CD_d(a), |b_v| ≤ K₂e^{−t₂d_lv} with d_lv > r for v ∈ T ∖ T′; group by shells m ≤ d_lv < m + 1
  85| (m ≥ ⌊r⌋, m ≥ 1) and use the packing fact. κ(r) → 0 as the tail of a convergent series. ∎

  92| it cannot join a cycle because that would give a vertex two predecessors.

 354| ## 6. NA-R re-run on a polynomial lattice
 355| 
 356| The constant atom l1 bound in `LOC2/lemmas/L4_LOCd.md:51` is insufficient
 357| here: log q can be of order log n. We prove a vanishing l1 bound instead.
 358| Take r_n=ceil(log log(n+exp(exp(1)))), B_l={v!=l:d(v,l)<=r_n},
 359| T'=T intersect B_l. Frames consist of the single functional
 360| r_{T,l}=W_l-E[W_l|W_T']; there are at most p 2^(2r_n) frames and
 361| log N_n<=log p+o(log n). Atoms are the coordinate functionals W_v, v in Q,
 362| each of variance 1. Put lambda_vector=beta_T(l)-zero_padded(beta_T'(l)).
 363| Then e_{T,l}=r_{T,l}-sum_v lambda_v W_v, an exact deterministic row identity.
 364| 
 365| Here is the stronger tail identity. For w in T minus T', write
 366| E[W_w|W_T']=sum_v gamma_{w,v} W_v. Conditional expectation of
 367| E[W_l|W_T] given W_T' equals E[W_l|W_T']; hence the coefficient difference
 368| on T' is minus sum_{w in T minus T'} beta_T(l)_w gamma_w.
 369| The coefficient difference on T minus T' is beta_T(l)_w. Uniqueness of
 370| coefficients follows from the population floor. By (P3), uniformly,
 371| 
 372|     ||lambda_vector||_1
 373|        <= (1+L0) sum_{w in T minus T'} |beta_T(l)_w|
 374|        <= (1+L0) F(r_n) =: L_n ->0.                       (P16)
 375| 
 376| Also D=E[W_l|W_T]-E[W_l|W_T'] has row variance
 377| <=||lambda_vector||_1^2: all covariance entries have absolute value <=1.
 378| The residual e_{T,l} is orthogonal to D, so
 379| 
 380|     Var(r_{T,l})=Var(e_{T,l})+Var(D)
 381|        <=(1+L_n^2/c)Var(e_{T,l}).                         (P17)
 382| 
 383| Thus (R1), (R2), and even the stronger atom bound with a log log n term hold:
 384| L_n^2(log(q+1)+log log n)=o(log n) and eta_n=L_n^2/c->0.
 385| No conditional-covariance estimate for large sets is needed here.

 388| P_n={(T,l):T in L,l notin T}. Assume it is nonempty; otherwise NA is

 400| probability <=1/log n, and L_n^2 y_n^2=o(log n) by (P16).

 408|     epsilon_n <= H6 sqrt(v_n(q+log n)/n)

 411| since b<1/2. Its normalization multiplier is 1+O(v_n/n)=1+o(1).

 414| 
 415|     c_n=log(n+1)+2log p-2log(q+1)-4 kappa_E-2
 416|        >=2log p+(1-2b)log n-O(1).                         (P19)

 418| The positive fixed slack 1-2b proves max Z^2<=c_n with probability

 425| ## 7. Assembly, cutoff audit, and changed-step ledger
 426| 
 427| On Sand_n the emitted maximizer lies in L. On Sand_n intersect NA intersect
 428| TL, deterministic descent deletes its extras one at a time and the shipped
 429| cap ell_n+|S_tilde_0| exceeds the number of extras. The proof at
 430| `LOC2/lemmas/L5_assembly.md:26` has no polylog-size use once these events
 431| and feasibility hold. It gives D_n bounded by the sum of their failure
 432| probabilities. The global population floor supplies LSF; the posterior
 433| and M5(0) integration at `LOC2/lemmas/L5_assembly.md:30` is unchanged and
 434| gives all the conclusions in Section 0. This is conditional on the named
 435| inputs, with their statuses preserved, and does not claim a new proof of
 436| POST or operational closure.
 437| 
 438| Changed steps, exhaustively relative to the cited LOC2/APP/GROW route:
 439| 
 440| 1. Exponential CD for arbitrary U is replaced, in the sandwich only, by
 441|    finite-dimensional BC (Section 1). Large-set CD is not invoked.
 442| 2. Exponential regression l1/tail is replaced by IR (Section 2).
 443| 3. Q has radius n^b and q=O(n^b); sample floors use q sqrt(log n/n)->0.
 444|    L0' is re-run with log family size O(q+log n), retaining bounded score
 445|    remainders; the sharp excess requires (q+log n)log n/n->0 (Section 3).
 446| 4. Selection-removal radius becomes n^rho; reference count becomes
 447|    O(n^(15rho)); the recursive correlation error is explicitly re-bounded
 448|    in (P8)-(P9), not claimed to retain the source's faster rate.
 449| 5. The fixed-reference spherical tail is unchanged; its count expectation
 450|    and ladder acquire n^lambda, as (P11)-(P12). The maximum threshold's
 451|    coefficient 1/2 in source (6.7) becomes tau, as (P13)-(P14).
 452| 6. Truth inclusion uses the same PTV argument and the rechecked polynomial
 453|    feasibility dichotomy. Junk deletion requires (1-tau)/2>b (P15).
 454| 7. NA uses shrinking l1 atoms (P16), variance ratio (P17), polynomial pair
 455|    chi-square unions, projection error (P18), and slack (P19). The old
 456|    bounded-l1 argument alone does not suffice.
 457| 8. TL uses t_n+h_n^2=O(q+log n)=o(n) and fixed beta-min. Descent, cap,
 458|    posterior transfer and output-error assembly need no further changes.
 459| 
 460| Rate audit: (the amended (P13) lower bound tau>1/2 costs nothing, since b<1/4 for alpha>2 [R06a-3].) BC is valid for any alpha>0. IR requires alpha>2. Polynomial
 461| sample floors and (P18) require b<1/2, true for alpha>1. Toolkit, TL,
 462| feasibility require b<1, also true. Selection removal requires
 463| rho>1/(4alpha). The size ladder only requires 15rho<1/2. The strictly
 464| stronger junk bound requires 15rho+b<1/2. Substituting b=1/(2alpha)
 465| shows feasible rho and tau exist iff alpha>17/2. At equality there is
 466| no fixed slack: this proof does not establish the boundary. For example,
 467| one fully explicit choice for alpha>17/2 is
 468| 
 469|     rho = (1/(4alpha) + (1/2-1/(2alpha))/15)/2,
 470|     lambda = 15rho,
 471|     tau = (2lambda + 1-1/alpha)/2.
 472| 
 473| The preliminary alpha-minus-two conditional exponent is avoidable. Its
 474| other warnings are real: polynomial q changes c_n by 2log q, requires a
 475| vanishing atom l1 norm, and changes both the ladder and maximum union.
 476| All three changes are accounted for above. No assertion of optimality
 477| over alternative sandwich/reference constructions is made.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

 136| ## 6. Why the assumptions are mild and standard (justification, not a claim)
 137| * **(A1)** Gaussian rows with polynomial dimension and a floor on sparse eigenvalues of the population correlation:
 138|   * This is the random-design setting of the Wave-1/1C posterior theory (T03♯ via APP POST).
 139|   * The floor is on sets of size O(log n) only and λ_max may diverge, which is weaker than bounded-spectrum assumptions.
 140|   * Its role parallels the identifiability condition of Song–Liang (Condition 3), descriptively and without an ordering
 141|     of assumption classes (`Theory_work/Wave1C/C-PACK/SONG_LIANG_MAP.md` row 9).
 142| * **(A2)** is an approximate factor model in the sense of Fan–Liao–Mincheva (2013) / Fan–Ke–Wang (2020): a low-rank common
 143|   component plus an idiosyncratic part. The idiosyncratic sparsity is replaced by **additional sufficient structure**:
 144|   exponential decay along an arbitrary geometry of polynomial growth (bandable/spatial/graph classes).
 145|   * Examples covered:
 146|     * stationary AR/ARMA with roots uniformly outside the unit circle;
 147|     * covariance or precision of fixed bandwidth with uniform spectral bounds;
 148|     * block-diagonal with bounded blocks;
 149|     * spatial fields on ℤ^d or on separated sites, with exponential decay;
 150|     * GMRFs whose precision has fixed range or uniformly exponential decay on a polynomial-growth geometry, with uniform
 151|       spectral bounds. Bounded spectrum alone is not enough [R05b-3].
 152|   * For k = 1 the subset-exposure ratio κ is an additional representation-dependent sufficient condition. It excludes zero
 153|     loadings and allows a vanishing common loading scale. It controls every subset and is not equivalent to average
 154|     pervasiveness: neither condition implies the other [R05b-2].
 155|   * For k = 0 the LOC_M spectral bounds and decay, polynomial dimension, and PTV suffice. No prescribed ordering or relation
 156|     to the method's partition is required. The bound λ_max(Σ_n) ≤ C is part of LOC_M [R05a-3].

On NA(𝓛) ∩ TL(𝓛), for every centre C ∈ 𝓛:

its cap; it scores S₀ whenever ℓ ≥ |C ∖ S₀| − 1 (if C = S₀, S₀ is the emitted centre, scored by OP-LS0 — LS0 scores its own centre — as in GEN L5.2; R10 S5); if ℓ ≥ |C ∖ S₀| its endpoint

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # LB — the rate n^{−1/2} cannot be beaten (deterministic lower bound; W3-POST)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** — new in council round C1 → C2 (prompted by C1 seat B, F2). Check record
   4| [C2B-N6]: council C2 seat A (`../reviews/C2_council_astra.md`, gpt-6-astra high) checked every proof step (correct;
   5| reproduced `lb_check` exactly); seat B (`../reviews/C2_council_opus.md`, Opus 5.5 high) checked it line by line
   6| (correct; adversarial minimum ratio 1.00005 at n = 10⁴). Domain counterexample (p = s₀): `../numerics/lb_domain_out.txt`. Notation of
   7| `../STATEMENT.md` §0; [P1], [P3] as there.
   8| 
   9| ## Proposition LB
  10| Let n ≥ 3, any standardised design X with p ≥ 2, any data y (the coded π of STATEMENT §0), and any S₀ ⊆ [p] with
  11| 1 ≤ s₀ < p and s₀ + 1 ≤ K. Put δ := 1 − π(S₀). Then, deterministically,
  12| 
  13|   δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n + 1)).
  14| 
  15| In particular, under any law, 1 − π(S₀) ≥ (1 + √(n+1))⁻¹ for every n with s₀ + 1 ≤ K: no rate o(n^{−1/2}) holds for
  16| the coded target under any design or signal condition. Theorem 1's rate √(log n/n) is therefore sharp up to the factor
  17| √(log n).
  18| 
  19| ## Proof
  20| Fix j ∉ S₀ and S := S₀ ∪ {j} ∈ Ω (|S| = s₀ + 1 ≤ K). With the common factor of m(·) cancelled,
  21| 
  22|   π(S)/π(S₀) = [w(s₀+1)/w(s₀)] · (D_{S₀}/D_S)^{1/2} · ((2b₀ + Q_{S₀})/(2b₀ + Q_S))^{ν}.
  23| 
  24| (i) Prior: w(s₀+1)/w(s₀) = (s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ([P1] `lem:prior`(b)).
  25| (ii) Determinant: D_S/D_{S₀} ≤ n + 1 ([P3] `lem:det`, first part, no eigenvalue condition; also directly: by the Schur
  26| complement, D_S/D_{S₀} = [1 + (n+1)uᵀ(I − P_H)u]/[1 + uᵀ(I − P_A)u] with u = x_j, P_H = (n+1)X_{S₀}H⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ,
  27| P_A = X_{S₀}(G_{S₀}+I)⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ; since I − P_H ⪯ I − P_A (eigenvalues 1/((n+1)λ+1) ≤ 1/(λ+1)), the ratio is ≤ n + 1).
  28| (iii) Fit: Q_S ≤ Q_{S₀} ([P1] `lem:spec`(d): adjoining a column cannot increase Q), so the last factor is ≥ 1.
  29| Hence π(S) ≥ π(S₀) r with r := (s₀+1)/((2p−1−s₀)√(n+1)). Summing over the p − s₀ choices of j (disjoint models, none
  30| equal to S₀): δ ≥ (p − s₀) r (1 − δ). The map p ↦ (p − s₀)/(2p − 1 − s₀) is nondecreasing for s₀ ≥ 1 (derivative
  31| ∝ s₀ − 1 ≥ 0), so at p = s₀ + 1 its value 1/(s₀+1) is its minimum and (p − s₀) r ≥ 1/√(n+1). Thus
  32| δ ≥ (1 − δ)/√(n+1), i.e. δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n+1)). ∎
  33| 
  34| ## Remarks
  35| 1. The bound uses no noise law, no design condition and no signal condition: it is a property of the coded prior and
  36|    ridge score (per-variable Occam factor ≥ (n+1)^{−1/2}, prior multiplicity (p − s₀)·(s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ≥ 1).
  37| 2. Numerics E0 (`../numerics/post_exact_out.txt`, p = 10): median δ√n ≈ 2.1–2.6, consistent with the bound
  38|    δ√(n+1) ≳ 1 and with order n^{−1/2} at fixed p.
  39| 3. Whether the additional √(log n) is attained when p = n^A (sum over p null additions with e^{χ²/2} weights) remains a
  40|    **conjecture** (ASSUMPTION_MAP, sharpness record item 4).

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # LB — the rate n^{−1/2} cannot be beaten (deterministic lower bound; W3-POST)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** — new in council round C1 → C2 (prompted by C1 seat B, F2). Check record
   4| [C2B-N6]: council C2 seat A (`../reviews/C2_council_astra.md`, gpt-6-astra high) checked every proof step (correct;
   5| reproduced `lb_check` exactly); seat B (`../reviews/C2_council_opus.md`, Opus 5.5 high) checked it line by line
   6| (correct; adversarial minimum ratio 1.00005 at n = 10⁴). Domain counterexample (p = s₀): `../numerics/lb_domain_out.txt`. Notation of
   7| `../STATEMENT.md` §0; [P1], [P3] as there.
   8| 
   9| ## Proposition LB
  10| Let n ≥ 3, any standardised design X with p ≥ 2, any data y (the coded π of STATEMENT §0), and any S₀ ⊆ [p] with
  11| 1 ≤ s₀ < p and s₀ + 1 ≤ K. Put δ := 1 − π(S₀). Then, deterministically,
  12| 
  13|   δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n + 1)).
  14| 
  15| In particular, under any law, 1 − π(S₀) ≥ (1 + √(n+1))⁻¹ for every n with s₀ + 1 ≤ K: no rate o(n^{−1/2}) holds for
  16| the coded target under any design or signal condition. Theorem 1's rate √(log n/n) is therefore sharp up to the factor
  17| √(log n).
  18| 
  19| ## Proof
  20| Fix j ∉ S₀ and S := S₀ ∪ {j} ∈ Ω (|S| = s₀ + 1 ≤ K). With the common factor of m(·) cancelled,
  21| 
  22|   π(S)/π(S₀) = [w(s₀+1)/w(s₀)] · (D_{S₀}/D_S)^{1/2} · ((2b₀ + Q_{S₀})/(2b₀ + Q_S))^{ν}.
  23| 
  24| (i) Prior: w(s₀+1)/w(s₀) = (s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ([P1] `lem:prior`(b)).
  25| (ii) Determinant: D_S/D_{S₀} ≤ n + 1 ([P3] `lem:det`, first part, no eigenvalue condition; also directly: by the Schur
  26| complement, D_S/D_{S₀} = [1 + (n+1)uᵀ(I − P_H)u]/[1 + uᵀ(I − P_A)u] with u = x_j, P_H = (n+1)X_{S₀}H⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ,
  27| P_A = X_{S₀}(G_{S₀}+I)⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ; since I − P_H ⪯ I − P_A (eigenvalues 1/((n+1)λ+1) ≤ 1/(λ+1)), the ratio is ≤ n + 1).
  28| (iii) Fit: Q_S ≤ Q_{S₀} ([P1] `lem:spec`(d): adjoining a column cannot increase Q), so the last factor is ≥ 1.
  29| Hence π(S) ≥ π(S₀) r with r := (s₀+1)/((2p−1−s₀)√(n+1)). Summing over the p − s₀ choices of j (disjoint models, none
  30| equal to S₀): δ ≥ (p − s₀) r (1 − δ). The map p ↦ (p − s₀)/(2p − 1 − s₀) is nondecreasing for s₀ ≥ 1 (derivative
  31| ∝ s₀ − 1 ≥ 0), so at p = s₀ + 1 its value 1/(s₀+1) is its minimum and (p − s₀) r ≥ 1/√(n+1). Thus
  32| δ ≥ (1 − δ)/√(n+1), i.e. δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n+1)). ∎
  33| 
  34| ## Remarks
  35| 1. The bound uses no noise law, no design condition and no signal condition: it is a property of the coded prior and
  36|    ridge score (per-variable Occam factor ≥ (n+1)^{−1/2}, prior multiplicity (p − s₀)·(s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ≥ 1).
  37| 2. Numerics E0 (`../numerics/post_exact_out.txt`, p = 10): median δ√n ≈ 2.1–2.6, consistent with the bound
  38|    δ√(n+1) ≳ 1 and with order n^{−1/2} at fixed p.
  39| 3. Whether the additional √(log n) is attained when p = n^A (sum over p null additions with e^{χ²/2} weights) remains a
  40|    **conjecture** (ASSUMPTION_MAP, sharpness record item 4).
</file>

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # LB — the rate n^{−1/2} cannot be beaten (deterministic lower bound; W3-POST)
   2| 
   3| Status: **PROVED (by this seat, unchecked)** — new in council round C1 → C2 (prompted by C1 seat B, F2). Check record
   4| [C2B-N6]: council C2 seat A (`../reviews/C2_council_astra.md`, gpt-6-astra high) checked every proof step (correct;
   5| reproduced `lb_check` exactly); seat B (`../reviews/C2_council_opus.md`, Opus 5.5 high) checked it line by line
   6| (correct; adversarial minimum ratio 1.00005 at n = 10⁴). Domain counterexample (p = s₀): `../numerics/lb_domain_out.txt`. Notation of
   7| `../STATEMENT.md` §0; [P1], [P3] as there.
   8| 
   9| ## Proposition LB
  10| Let n ≥ 3, any standardised design X with p ≥ 2, any data y (the coded π of STATEMENT §0), and any S₀ ⊆ [p] with
  11| 1 ≤ s₀ < p and s₀ + 1 ≤ K. Put δ := 1 − π(S₀). Then, deterministically,
  12| 
  13|   δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n + 1)).
  14| 
  15| In particular, under any law, 1 − π(S₀) ≥ (1 + √(n+1))⁻¹ for every n with s₀ + 1 ≤ K: no rate o(n^{−1/2}) holds for
  16| the coded target under any design or signal condition. Theorem 1's rate √(log n/n) is therefore sharp up to the factor
  17| √(log n).
  18| 
  19| ## Proof
  20| Fix j ∉ S₀ and S := S₀ ∪ {j} ∈ Ω (|S| = s₀ + 1 ≤ K). With the common factor of m(·) cancelled,
  21| 
  22|   π(S)/π(S₀) = [w(s₀+1)/w(s₀)] · (D_{S₀}/D_S)^{1/2} · ((2b₀ + Q_{S₀})/(2b₀ + Q_S))^{ν}.
  23| 
  24| (i) Prior: w(s₀+1)/w(s₀) = (s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ([P1] `lem:prior`(b)).
  25| (ii) Determinant: D_S/D_{S₀} ≤ n + 1 ([P3] `lem:det`, first part, no eigenvalue condition; also directly: by the Schur
  26| complement, D_S/D_{S₀} = [1 + (n+1)uᵀ(I − P_H)u]/[1 + uᵀ(I − P_A)u] with u = x_j, P_H = (n+1)X_{S₀}H⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ,
  27| P_A = X_{S₀}(G_{S₀}+I)⁻¹X_{S₀}ᵀ; since I − P_H ⪯ I − P_A (eigenvalues 1/((n+1)λ+1) ≤ 1/(λ+1)), the ratio is ≤ n + 1).
  28| (iii) Fit: Q_S ≤ Q_{S₀} ([P1] `lem:spec`(d): adjoining a column cannot increase Q), so the last factor is ≥ 1.
  29| Hence π(S) ≥ π(S₀) r with r := (s₀+1)/((2p−1−s₀)√(n+1)). Summing over the p − s₀ choices of j (disjoint models, none
  30| equal to S₀): δ ≥ (p − s₀) r (1 − δ). The map p ↦ (p − s₀)/(2p − 1 − s₀) is nondecreasing for s₀ ≥ 1 (derivative
  31| ∝ s₀ − 1 ≥ 0), so at p = s₀ + 1 its value 1/(s₀+1) is its minimum and (p − s₀) r ≥ 1/√(n+1). Thus
  32| δ ≥ (1 − δ)/√(n+1), i.e. δ ≥ 1/(1 + √(n+1)). ∎
  33| 
  34| ## Remarks
  35| 1. The bound uses no noise law, no design condition and no signal condition: it is a property of the coded prior and
  36|    ridge score (per-variable Occam factor ≥ (n+1)^{−1/2}, prior multiplicity (p − s₀)·(s₀+1)/(2p−1−s₀) ≥ 1).
  37| 2. Numerics E0 (`../numerics/post_exact_out.txt`, p = 10): median δ√n ≈ 2.1–2.6, consistent with the bound
  38|    δ√(n+1) ≳ 1 and with order n^{−1/2} at fixed p.
  39| 3. Whether the additional √(log n) is attained when p = n^A (sum over p null additions with e^{χ²/2} weights) remains a
  40|    **conjecture** (ASSUMPTION_MAP, sharpness record item 4).
</file>

   2|

   7| 
   8| ## Statement (per-n hypotheses [L01-3])
   9| Fix s₀ ≥ 1, A ≥ 1 and constants (σ*², M, φ₀, c) and g₀ (case i) or C_OS (cases ii–iii). There are n₀ and C depending only
  10| on these such that for every n ≥ n₀ and every fixed design X and θ* for which, at that n, s₀ ≤ K, 2 ≤ p ≤ n^A, G, (E),
  11| (F₀) and one of
  12| (i) (F_λ), (F_w; g₀), BM(c), c > c₀;  (ii) (F_λ), (OS; C_OS), BM(c), c > c₀;  (iii) (OS; C_OS), (ID^M; c), c > c₁
  13| hold:  **E δ_n ≤ C r_n.** Under BM-∞ the same holds with n₀ depending also on the envelope. For random designs on
  14| (X, θ*)-measurable events 𝒜_n on which the hypotheses hold: E δ_n ≤ C r_n + P(𝒜_nᶜ) (condition on (X, θ*); ε ⫫ (X, θ*)).
  15| Every step is a bound at a single n using hypotheses at that n only.
  16| 
  17| ## Lemma C1 (deterministic denominator on a high-probability event)
  18| Assume G, (E), (F₀), s₀ ≤ K, n ≥ 16. Let E′ := ‖ε_c‖²/σ*² ~ χ²_N. On {E′ ≤ 2N},
  19|   m^c_{b₊}(S₀)/f₀(y_c) ≥ c_den D_{S₀}^{−1/2} n^{−1/2},  c_den := σ*²·c′_IG·exp{−3 − ρ̄/σ*²},
  20| where ρ̄ := M + M/(2φ₀²) and c′_IG := min_{v∈[σ*²/2, 2σ*²]} IG(v; 0.51, b₊) > 0 (depends on (σ*², M) only).
  21| *Proof.* By (F₀), (E) and [L1a′] (its "changed step" with T = S₀, θ = θ*; ‖θ*‖² ≤ 1.5M/φ₀² by [L1a′] Remark 1):
  22| Q^c_{S₀} ≤ σ*²E′ + ρ with deterministic 0 ≤ ρ ≤ ρ̄. As in [P1] `lem:den` ("Integral representation"),
  23|   m^c_{b₊}(S₀)/f₀(y_c) = D_{S₀}^{−1/2}∫_0^∞ exp{−(N/2)log(v/σ*²) + E′/2 − Q^c_{S₀}/(2v)} IG(v; 0.51, b₊) dv.
  24| With u := v/σ*², the exponent is ≥ F(u) − ρ/(2σ*²u), F(u) := −(N/2)log u + (E′/2)(1 − 1/u). F(1) = 0,
  25| F′(1) = (E′ − N)/2, F″(u) = N/(2u²) − E′/u³. Let I := [1, 1 + n^{−1/2}] if E′ ≥ N and I := [1 − n^{−1/2}, 1] if E′ < N
  26| (I ⊆ [3/4, 5/4] for n ≥ 16; the choice depends on the data, which is allowed in a pointwise lower bound). On I and on
  27| {E′ ≤ 2N}: |F″(u)| ≤ N/(2·(3/4)²) + 2N/(3/4)³ ≤ 6N, and F′(1)(u − 1) ≥ 0, so by Taylor's theorem
  28| F(u) ≥ −3N(u − 1)² ≥ −3N/n ≥ −3. Also ρ/(2σ*²u) ≤ ρ̄/σ*² (u ≥ 3/4 > ½). Restricting the integral to v ∈ σ*²I
  29| (length σ*²n^{−1/2}, inside [σ*²/2, 2σ*²]) gives the claim. ∎
  30| 
  31| ## Lemma C2 (expected size tail)

  33| prove [K-BC-2]; below R_m > 0):
  34|   E π(|S| > m) ≤ (κ²/c_den)·R_m √(D_{S₀}) √n + (8 + 24M/σ*²)/(n − 1) + e^{−N/8}.
