  36| = R_mϖ(S₀) ([P1] `lem:num`, b₋ data-free; W_K cancels). On 𝓑_n ∩ {E′ ≤ 2N}, Lemma C1 gives
  37| π(E_m) ≤ (κ²/c_den)√(D_{S₀})√n·N_m/ϖ(S₀); its expectation is ≤ (κ²/c_den)√(D_{S₀})√n R_m (no independence needed: the
  38| bound is a deterministic multiple of N_m ≥ 0). Off this event use π ≤ 1: P(𝓑_nᶜ) ≤ (8 + 24M/σ*²)/(n−1) ([P1]
  39| `thm:T01iii`), P(E′ > 2N) ≤ e^{−N/8} ([P3] `lem:chi`(a) with x = N/8: N + 2√(Nx) + 2x ≤ 2N). ∎
  40| 
  41| At m = m♯_n: R_m ≤ n^{−(s₀+1)/2}e^{−½ log n} and D_{S₀} ≤ (n+1)^{s₀} ([P1] `lem:spec`(e)), so
  42| E π(|S| > m♯_n) ≤ (κ²/c_den)(1 + 1/n)^{s₀/2} n^{−1/2} + O(1/n).
  43| 
  44| ## Proof of the statement
  45| δ_n ≤ T₀ + T_sup + T_U as in [P3] §main (i), with T₀ := π(|S| > m♯_n), T_sup := π(S ⊋ S₀, |S| ≤ m♯_n), T_U := π(𝒰),
  46| 𝒰 the underfitting S ∈ Ω with |S| ≤ m♯_n. Let 𝒢*_n := 𝒢^sel_n (cases i–ii) or 𝒢^sup_n ∩ 𝒢⁵_n (case iii). Then
  47|   E δ_n ≤ E T₀ + E[(T_sup + T_U)1_{𝒢*_n}] + P((𝒢*_n)ᶜ).
  48| - E T₀ = O(n^{−1/2}) by Lemma C2.
  49| - On 𝒢*_n, T_sup ≤ e^{ρ_n}Υ_n (case i: [P3] `prop:sup`(a) via [T03R] (C5)) or ≤ e^{ρ_n}Υ′_n (cases ii–iii: (C5′)(a));
  50|   so E[T_sup1] ≤ e^{ρ_n}2K_{s₀,0}q_n ≤ C r_n (case i, [T03R] (C5)(b)) or ≤ e^{ρ_n}𝒪_n^{>0} ≤ 2C_OS r_n ((C5′)(b), (OS)).
  51| - On 𝒢*_n, [T03R] (C8) / (C8′): T_U ≤ 2^{s₀}κ̄_n(1 + e^{ρ_n}Υ) + 2^{s₀}e^{2ρ_n}(2p)^{s₀}(n+1)^{s₀/2}Υ^{>j₀} with the
  52|   deterministic κ̄_n = e^{ρ_n}n^{−2} ([T03R] (C10), BM(c), c > c₀) or κ̄_n = n^{−2} (Lemma E1, (ID^M; c), c > c₁). Taking
  53|   expectations: E[T_U1] ≤ C(n^{−2} + (log n)^{(j₀+1)/2}/n) (case i) or ≤ C(n^{−2} + r_n) (ii–iii, (OS)).
  54| - P((𝒢^sel_n)ᶜ) ≤ 5/n, P((𝒢^sup_n)ᶜ) ≤ 4/n ((G3′), A_occam), P((𝒢⁵_n)ᶜ) ≤ 1/n (Lemma E1(a)).
  55| All terms are O(r_n). ∎
  56| 
  57| ## Corollaries and remarks
  58| 1. P(HPM ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E δ_n ([P3] (iii)); P(MPM ≠ S₀) ≤ 2Eδ_n; P(ξ_q ≠ S₀) ≤ Eδ_n/min(q, 1 − q) (if δ_n < min(q, 1 − q) then
  59|    PIP_j > q exactly on S₀); E max_j|PIP_j − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ Eδ_n ([SL]/[P3] (ii)). All O(r_n).
  60| 2. **Sharpness.** With [LB] (1 ≤ s₀ < p, s₀ + 1 ≤ K): E δ_n ≥ (1 + √(n+1))⁻¹. So E δ_n is of order between n^{−1/2} and
  61|    √(log n/n): the brief's target O(n^{−q/2}), q < 1, is exceeded, and q = 1 (up to √log n) is attained. Where the
  62|    √(log n) comes from: only the superset sum (truncated χ² moments, [P3] `lem:chi`(b)); the size tail is O(n^{−1/2}).

params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # Theorem D — draw discovery
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v2, 2026-11-09 (v1 → v2: MAP premise S† = S₀ replaces δ < ½, BT1 §3.1).
   4| Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem D".
   5| 
   6| ## §1 The draws are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D-i)
   7| 
   8| Fix c ∈ A₀ (success set, index r ≤ R′) and run island r's potential record on an iid U[0,1) stream U₁, U₂, … (H-U).
   9| By CC1 the island makes exactly D_r(c) = N_e(1 + T + L + 4) calls of `draw_start` = `draw_pi0` (N_e initial draws; one
  10| independence proposal per particle per round; T + L + 4 rounds per particle). Order them by execution: k = 1, …, D_r.
  11| 
  12| Let τ_k be the number of uniforms already consumed when draw k begins, 𝓕_n := σ(U₁..U_n). Whether draw k begins after
  13| exactly n uniforms is a function of U₁..U_n (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b): the control flow and the number of uniforms each
  14| operation reads are decided by values already read, the data and c), so τ_k is an (𝓕_n)-stopping time, finite since each
  15| operation reads a bounded number of uniforms (`L1_bridge.md:77-88`). By the strong Markov property of iid sequences,
  16| V^{(k)} := (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. Draw k equals Ψ(V^{(k)}) for the measurable
  17| map Ψ realised by `draw_pi0` (it reads 1 + (number of iterations of the remaining-size loop, which includes blocks assigned size 0) + (number of
  18| positive-size blocks) ≤ 1 + 2J uniforms (SW1 #9), a number determined by the values it reads, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`). By START, Ψ(V) ~ π₀ for V iid uniform.
  19| Draws 1..k−1 are 𝓕_{τ_k}-measurable (they end before draw k begins). Hence draw k ~ π₀ independently of draws 1..k−1, for
  20| every k: the D_r draws are iid π₀. Therefore P_c(no draw equals S₀) = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)} exactly.
  21| 
  22| Every draw is evaluated with `emit = true` before its accept decision (CC1), so each draw lies in 𝓜_r:
  23| {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {no draw equals S₀} and P_c(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r) ≤ (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)}.
  24| 
  25| *Freezing.* Augment the statistical record Φ(c, u) by the sequence of the D_r(c) π₀ draws: each draw is computed from
  26| (c, u) by the same control flow as Φ (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-0), (B-d)), so the augmented record Φ̃ is jointly measurable. Put
  27| g(c, u) := 1{no draw of Φ̃(c, u) equals S₀} for c ∈ A₀ and 0 otherwise; g is bounded and jointly measurable, and
  28| 𝓒 ⊥ U_r (SI), so by the T12 freezing lemma
  29| P(no draw of island r equals S₀ | 𝓒) = 1_{E₀}(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(𝓒)} in the localised form. ∎(D-i)
  30| 
  31| ## §2 Several islands (D-ii)
  32| 
  33| Under IND-T, given 𝓒 the four streams are independent (and independent of streams 0–9), so the four indicator events
  34| {no draw of island r equals S₀} are conditionally independent given 𝓒 (apply the freezing lemma to the product
  35| g₁(c, u₁)⋯g₄(c, u₄) with (U₁..U₄) ⊥ 𝓒). Hence P(S₀ ∉ ∪_r𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ Π_r (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r} = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{4D_r}
  36| (D_r does not depend on r). Without IND-T only D-i is used. ∎(D-ii)
  37| 
  38| ## §3 The reported HPM (D-iii, D-iv)
  39| 
  40| *Deterministic step.* Let S† be the hpm_better-maximum of Ω (the exact HPM with the coded tie rule,
  41| `cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`; a strict total order, so S† is unique). By Lemma PC, on {completed}, Ŝ is the hpm_better-maximum
  42| of 𝓜 ⊆ Ω. If S† = S₀ and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then S₀ is ⪰ every element of 𝓜, so Ŝ = S₀. Sufficient condition: δ < ½. Indeed then for
  43| every S ∈ Ω∖S₀, π(S) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) < ½ < π(S₀), so F(S₀) > F(S) (e^F ∝ π on Ω, CC2) and S† = S₀. So
  44| {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}.
  45| 
  46| *Probability.* {completed} ⊆ 𝒜 (no final run otherwise, `v3_fit.R` returns before `v3_final_run` when calibration
  47| fails). Hence
  48| {completed} ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {S† ≠ S₀} ∪ (𝒜 ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r}) for any fixed r ≤ 4,
  49| and by D-i, integrating over 𝓒 and the data (the conditional bound is ≤ 1),
  50| P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}]; with IND-T the
  51| exponent is 4D_r by D-ii.
  52| 
  53| *Production corollary.* Production budgets give N_e = 4^e·N₀ ≥ N₀ = max(2500, n, p) and L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉)
  54| (`v3_preprocess.R:24-25`, tiers `:30`; `v3_run.R:90`), and T ≥ 1 on 𝒜; so D_r ≥ N₀(1 + 1 + L + 4) = N₀(L + 6). ∎(D-iii)
  55| 
  56| *Asymptotics (D-iv).* P(S† ≠ S₀) → 0 (the MAP premise; implied by P-CONC since {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}). (1 − a)^D ≤ e^{−aD}, so E[1_𝒜(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ E[e^{−Q}] with Q := D_rπ₀(S₀) on 𝒜 and Q := ∞ off 𝒜 (LC1 issue 2), i.e. the integrand
  57| 1_𝒜e^{−D_rπ₀(S₀)} is defined as 0 off 𝒜; it is bounded and → 0 in probability by P-OVL, so its expectation → 0 (bounded convergence). In production, D_rπ₀(S₀) ≥
  58| max(n, p)·(L + 6)·π₀(S₀) ≥ max(n, p)·log₂(n+1)·π₀(S₀), so the displayed deterministic condition suffices. ∎
  59| 
  60| ## Remarks
  61| 
  62| - D is a discovery statement: it does not say the particles or the RB PIPs are right (LT♯/C do that). Gibbs flips, swaps,
  63|   local search and LS0 only enlarge 𝓜, so the bound is conservative for the method; it is an equality for the draw
  64|   mechanism alone (`numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §5: 0.3754 vs 0.3728, 0.7876 vs 0.7861, z ≤ 1.07).
  65| - The equality concerns the potential run's D_r draws; a stopped run has fewer draws but reports no HPM as complete.
</file>

   1| # Theorem LT♯ — corrected lower-tail transfer for the coded outputs
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v2, 2026-11-09 (v1 → v2: Step 2′ weighted uniform bound and LT-b′, LT-e′ with a
   4| vanishing threshold, from BT1 §4.1, §5, re-derived). Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem LT♯". Uses Lemma MR
   5| (`MR_identities.md`), Lemma ST (`ST_stay.md`), Lemma PC (`PC_completed.md`), CC3 (`CC_code_check.md`).
   6| 
   7| Throughout: fixed data; island r; everything "given 𝓒 on 𝒜" in the localised form (STATEMENT §0); W := W_r.
   8| For q = 1..4 (measured round q), let
   9| - B_q := 1 − A_{r,q−1} (fraction of particles **not** at S₀ when entering measured round q; A_{r,0} = after the L
  10|   burn-in rounds), B̄ := ¼Σ_{q=1}^{4} B_q;
  11| - Λ_q := (1/N_e)·#{i : particle i enters measured round q at S₀ and is away from S₀ at some time of that round},
  12|   Λ̄ := ¼Σ_q Λ_q.
  13| 
  14| ## Step 1 (pathwise decomposition)
  15| 
  16| Fix j. For a pair (q, i) call it *good* if particle i enters measured round q at S₀ and is at S₀ at every time of the round.
  17| For a good pair, Y^i_{q,j} = S₀ (the state immediately before its Gibbs-j step is S₀), so its recorded value is o_j(S₀) and
  18| |o_j(Y^i_{q,j}) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ κ₀. For any other pair the term is ≤ 1 (o_j ∈ [0, 1]). The bad pairs of round q are those
  19| entering away from S₀ (fraction B_q) or entering at S₀ and leaving (fraction Λ_q). By CC3,
  20| p̂_r(j) − 1{j ∈ S₀} = (4N_e)⁻¹Σ_{q,i}[o_j(Y^i_{q,j}) − 1{j ∈ S₀}], hence for **every** j simultaneously
  21|   |p̂_r(j) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ κ₀ + B̄ + Λ̄.                                                        (1)
  22| The good/bad classification does not depend on j; this is why no union over coordinates (no factor p) appears.
  23| 
  24| ## Step 2 (the two expectations)
  25| 
  26| (a) *Weighted.* By MR-b with h = 1{S ≠ S₀} (data-only, bounded) and s = L + q − 1 (q = 1..4):
  27| E[W·B_q | 𝓒] = 1 − π(S₀) = δ, so E[W·B̄ | 𝓒] = δ. Likewise E[W(1 − A_{r,q}) | 𝓒] = δ for q = 0..4.

   1| # Lemma PC — completed runs carry the potential island records
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma PC". Code paths relative to
   4| `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/`. This is the limited comparison SL1 item 4 asked for, not the full GUARD-W audit.
   5| 
   6| ## Proof
   7| 
   8| Fix the data, a calibration value on 𝒜 and the final streams; assume EX-A.
   9| 
  10| (i) *Islands.* The only early return inside an island is the guard check after each bridge stage
  11| (`cpp/v3_engine.h:335-338`), which sets `res.partial = true`. In `cpp_final_run`, a partial island sets
  12| `status = "resource_limit"` and breaks the island loop (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:451`); later guard checks (final local search
  13| `:459`, LS0 `:480`) and any `NumericalFailure` (`:483`) also leave `status != "completed"`; nothing resets `status` to
  14| "completed". Hence on {completed} no island returned early: each island executed the whole of `run_island_s` (bridge
  15| `:303-339`, burn-in `:343-347`, measured `:351-360`). Under EX-A, the island's statistical record is a function of
  16| (c, island stream) only — the guard, clock, cache and ledger do not feed any transition, weight or evidence increment
  17| (W1-N1 Lemma B step (B-0), `Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md`, valid on main by the CC header). The guard only
  18| decides *whether* to stop, and on {completed} it never stopped. So the record equals the potential (uninterrupted) record
  19| computed from the same stream; the same holds for the set 𝓜_r of models island r evaluated (incl. rejected proposals),
  20| which is a function of (c, island stream) through the augmented record of `D_theorem.md` §1 (C1 Opus #1).
  21| 
  22| (ii) *Reported fields.* On {completed}, `v3_assemble_final` skips the incomplete branch (`v3_run.R:143`) and sets
  23| `log_Z_r`, `log_Z` (`:150-154`), `pip_r`, `pip_primary`, `mpm` (`:159-163`) from the island results, which are the
  24| fields `logZ`, `pip` of (i) (`cpp/v3_engine.h:362-365`); these are the functions of §0 of the island records. `out$hpm` is the ledger's running best (`v3_run.R:142`); it is
  25| **not** a function of the island records alone (the records exclude rejected proposals, tables, inherited models, the final
  26| local search and LS0) — see (iii) (SW1 #1).
  27| 
  28| (iii) *Ledger.* Every model evaluated by island r goes through `eval` with `emit = true` (CC1–CC2), so it is offered to
  29| the HPM at its first evaluation in the run; the ledger lives for the whole final run (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:407`) and is never
  30| reset. So 𝓜 ⊇ ∪_r 𝓜_r (𝓜 also contains tables, inherited models, final-search and LS0 evaluations), 𝓜 ⊆ Ω (CC5), and by CC2
  31| Ŝ = the hpm_better-maximum of 𝓜. ∎
  32| 
  33| Consequence used downstream: for any event G about the potential island records (evidence, PIPs, MPM, particle states), {completed} ∩ G is the same as {completed} ∩
  34| G evaluated on the reported fields; so P(completed ∩ {reported error}) ≤ P(𝒜 ∩ {potential error}).

<file path="Theory_work/Wave3/W3-SAMP/lemmas/ST_stay.md">
   1| # Lemma ST — staying at S₀ under π-invariant kernels
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma ST".
   4| 
   5| Setting: fixed data, φ = 1, the labelled elementary kernels of T12 §1 (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T12_T8_frozen_run_identities/
   6| STATEMENT.md:25-31`): Gibbs G_j (j ∈ [p]), uniform swap U, B copies of the neighbour swap N, independence I. KERNEL: the
   7| coded steps realise these kernels (W1-N1 Lemma B; N9) and each is π-invariant (in fact π-reversible) at φ = 1 (T12
   8| "invariance", `PROOF_v6.tex:54-81`, as re-stated at `W1-N1/lemmas/L2_post_terminal.md:18-20`). S₀ ∈ Ω, π(S₀) > 0,
   9| o₁ = π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀).
  10| 
  11| ## (ST-a) Any π-invariant kernel leaves S₀ with probability at most o₁
  12| 
  13| Let K be a Markov kernel on the finite set Ω with πK = π. Evaluating at S₀:
  14| π(S₀) = Σ_S π(S)K(S, S₀) = π(S₀)K(S₀, S₀) + Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀).
  15| Hence π(S₀)·K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = π(S₀)(1 − K(S₀, S₀)) = Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀) ≤ Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S) = π(Ω∖S₀), i.e.
  16| K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ o₁. ∎
  17| 
  18| ## (ST-b) The Gibbs family
  19| 
  20| T12 §1: at S, G_j moves to S⁺ = S ∪ {j} with probability o_j(S) and to S⁻ = S ∖ {j} otherwise, where o_j(S) =
  21| γ₁(S⁺)/(γ₁(S⁺) + γ₁(S⁻)) if |S⁺| ≤ K and o_j(S) = 0 otherwise. At S = S₀:
  22| - j ∈ S₀: S⁺ = S₀, so G_j leaves S₀ iff it moves to S₀ ∖ {j}, with probability 1 − o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; and
  23|   1 − o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∖j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∖j)) ≤ π(S₀∖j)/π(S₀) (|S₀| ≤ K so S⁺ = S₀ ∈ Ω).
  24| - j ∉ S₀: S⁻ = S₀, so G_j leaves iff it moves to S₀ ∪ {j}, with probability o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; if
  25|   |S₀| = K this is 0; otherwise o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∪j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∪j)) ≤ π(S₀∪j)/π(S₀).
  26| (γ₁ ∝ π on Ω.) So K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) (with π(S₀ ⊕ j) := 0 when S₀ ⊕ j ∉ Ω).
  27| The models S₀ ⊕ j, j ∈ [p], are pairwise distinct and different from S₀, so
  28| Σ_j K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ Σ_j π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀) = o₁. In particular κ₀ := max_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁
  29| (and even Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁). ∎
  30| 
  31| ## (ST-c) One round
  32| 
  33| Hypothesis (stated in ST-c, SW1 #14): the round path law of T12 (R3), realised by the code under EX-A, H-U and KERNEL
  34| (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)).
  35| 
  36| Let a particle enter a round at φ = 1 in state X_{[0]} = S₀; the order σ (a bijection from positions {1..m} to the m labels,
  37| m = p + B + 2) has any law, independent of the entering state; given σ, the within-round path X_{[0]}, …, X_{[m]} is a
  38| Markov chain with kernels K_{σ(1)}, …, K_{σ(m)} (T12 (R3), `STATEMENT.md:44`; W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)). Let
  39| E := {∃k ≤ m : X_{[k]} ≠ S₀}. On E let k* be the first such k; then X_{[k*−1]} = S₀. So
  40| P(E | σ) = Σ_{k=1}^{m} P(X_{[0]} = … = X_{[k−1]} = S₀, X_{[k]} ≠ S₀ | σ) ≤ Σ_{k=1}^{m} K_{σ(k)}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =
  41| Σ_ℓ K_ℓ(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =: λ₀,
  42| the last equality because σ is a bijection, so each label occurs exactly once. Taking expectation over σ, P(E) ≤ λ₀.
  43| Bound λ₀: the p Gibbs labels contribute ≤ o₁ (ST-b); U, I and each of the B copies of N contribute ≤ o₁ each (ST-a, each
  44| is π-invariant at φ = 1). So λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁, and B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) ≤ 16 (CC7) gives λ₀ ≤ 19·o₁. ∎
  45| 
  46| Remarks. (1) No reversibility is needed, only πK = π for each label. (2) The bound is pathwise in the order and holds for
  47| every round at φ = 1, in particular the measured rounds, whatever happened before (the conditional law of the path given
  48| everything before the round is as stated; Lemma B (B-b)). (3) Equality in ST-b is what makes κ₀ the *exact* RB error of a
  49| particle sitting at S₀: its recorded value at G_j is o_j(S₀).
  50| 
  51| ## Numerical falsification
  52| 
  53| `numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §1: exact kernel matrices built from T12 §1 for three targets (incl. cap K = 2 and B = 2):
  54| Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| equals the Gibbs leave-sum to machine precision and is ≤ o₁; every non-Gibbs label leaves with
  55| probability ≤ o₁; λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁; the simulated mean leave fraction E[Λ] is ≤ λ₀. Invariance errors ≤ 1.1e-16.
</file>

   1| # Theorem TR — terminal repair under global overlap (alternative to NC_r)
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Source: BT1 §2 (`reviews/BT1_better_theorem_astra.md`),
   4| re-derived by the lead. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem TR". Uses KERNEL, Lemma ST, T12 (R3), Lemma PC, CC1–CC3.
   5| 
   6| ## Setting
   7| 
   8| Fixed data. w(S) := π(S)/π₀(S); **M := max_{S∈Ω} w(S)** (≥ 1, since Σπ = Σπ₀ = 1); e_0 := 1 and e_L := (1 − 1/M)^L for L ≥ 1 (LC2 issue 4). S₀ ∈ Ω, δ, o₁,
   9| κ₀, λ₀ as in STATEMENT §0/ST; g := min{1, κ₀ + δ + (1 − δ)λ₀} ≤ min{1, 21·o₁}. Given 𝓒 on 𝒜, island r, any frozen
  10| parameters and **any** bridge outcome.
  11| 
  12| ## Statement
  13| 
  14| - (TR-a) For every order σ, the round kernel K_σ := K_{σ(1)}⋯K_{σ(m)} at φ = 1 satisfies K_σ(x, ·) ≥ M⁻¹π(·) for every x;
  15|   hence so does the round kernel K₁ (average over σ), and sup_x ‖K₁^L(x, ·) − π‖_TV ≤ e_L.
  16| - (TR-b) E[‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ | 𝓒] ≤ g + e_L and E[1 − A_{r,q} | 𝓒] ≤ δ + e_{L+q} ≤ δ + e_L (q = 0..4).
  17| - (TR-c) E[‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ | 𝓒] ≤ g + e_L; P(MPM ≠ S₀ | 𝓒) ≤ 2(g + e_L); P(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ δ + e_L.
  18| - (TR-d, asymptotic) Under P-CONC and **P-OVL∞: P(𝒜 ∩ {L/M ≤ c}) → 0 for every c > 0** (Q := L/M on 𝒜, ∞ off 𝒜,
  19|   Q → ∞ in probability; MP1 issue 1): for every ε > 0,
  20|   P(𝒜 ∩ {‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ > ε}) → 0, P(𝒜 ∩ {MPM ≠ S₀}) → 0, P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) → 0 — with no condition on
  21|   Ẑ (NC_r not assumed), the bridge, N_e, or the grid. Production corollary: L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉), so P-OVL∞ means, localised to 𝒜,
  22|   M = o_P(log n) on 𝒜.
  23| 
  24| ## Proof
  25| 
  26| (TR-a) *Independence kernel.* At φ = 1 the I step proposes y ~ π₀ and accepts with probability min{1, w(y)/w(x)}. For
  27| y ≠ x: K_I(x, y) = π₀(y)min{1, w(y)/w(x)} = min{π₀(y), π(y)/w(x)} ≥ min{π(y)/M, π(y)/M} = π(y)/M, using π₀(y) = π(y)/w(y)
  28| ≥ π(y)/M and w(x) ≤ M. For y = x: K_I(x, x) ≥ π₀(x) (the proposal x is accepted with probability 1) ≥ π(x)/M. So
  29| K_I(x, ·) ≥ M⁻¹π. *Round.* Fix σ and let k be the position of I; write K_σ = K_pre K_I K_post. Every elementary kernel is
  30| π-invariant at φ = 1 (KERNEL), so πK_post = π and K_σ(x, ·) = Σ_z K_pre(x, z)Σ_y K_I(z, y)K_post(y, ·) ≥
  31| Σ_z K_pre(x, z)·M⁻¹(πK_post)(·) = M⁻¹π(·). Averaging over the order law preserves the bound. *Doeblin.* Write
  32| K₁ = M⁻¹π + (1 − M⁻¹)Q with Q a Markov kernel (Q := (K₁ − M⁻¹π)/(1 − M⁻¹) if M > 1; if M = 1 then π = π₀ and K₁ = π
  33| already). Since πK₁ = π, for any law μ: μK₁ − π = (1 − M⁻¹)(μQ − πQ), and ‖μQ − πQ‖_TV ≤ ‖μ − π‖_TV. Induction gives
  34| ‖μK₁^L − π‖_TV ≤ (1 − 1/M)^L‖μ − π‖_TV ≤ e_L.
  35| 
  36| (TR-b) Fix c. Work island by island: let 𝓗 be island r's own history up to the end of its bridge (stage-T round) and 𝓗′
  37| island r's history before its measured round 1 (conditioning on other islands' histories is not used; under SI alone it
  38| could carry information about island r's stream — SW1 #28). The displayed bounds are the averages of the conditional ones.
  39| For a particle, let φ_i := ¼Σ_{q=1}^{4}1{(q, i) bad} with "bad" as in `LT_theorem.md` Step 1 (enters round q away from S₀,
  40| or enters at S₀ and leaves during it). By (1) of `LT_theorem.md`, ‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ min{1, κ₀ + (1/N_e)Σ_iφ_i}.
  41| *Per-particle chain.* By T12 (R3) (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)), given 𝓗′ each particle's subsequent rounds form a Markov chain
  42| with kernel K₁ started at its entering state (orders fresh and independent of the past); hence E[φ_i | 𝓗′] = ψ(X_i′), with
  43| X_i′ particle i's state entering measured round 1 and ψ(x) := E_x[¼Σ_q 1{round q bad}] ∈ [0, 1].
  44| *Stationary value.* Under X′ ~ π the entering state of every measured round is π-distributed (πK₁ = π); round q is bad
  45| with probability ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) + π(S₀)λ₀ = δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ (ST-c applies to a particle entering at S₀, whatever happened
  46| before). So π(ψ) ≤ δ + (1 − δ)λ₀.
  47| *Burn-in.* Given 𝓗, X_i′ ~ K₁^L(X_i^{(T)}, ·) (L rounds at φ = 1, R3), so E[ψ(X_i′) | 𝓗] = (K₁^Lψ)(X_i^{(T)}) ≤ π(ψ) + e_L by
  48| (TR-a), since ψ ∈ [0, 1]. Hence E[(1/N_e)Σ_iφ_i] ≤ δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ + e_L, and by concavity of min{1, ·},
  49| E‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ min{1, κ₀ + δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ + e_L} ≤ g + e_L. For the endpoints apply (TR-a) to K₁^{L+q} directly:
  50| E[1 − A_{r,q} | 𝓗] = (1/N_e)Σ_i K₁^{L+q}(X_i^{(T)}, Ω∖S₀) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) + e_{L+q} = δ + e_{L+q} ≤ δ + e_L (C1 Opus #3). These are bounded measurable functionals of the record, so the freezing lemma transfers them to
  51| "given 𝓒" in localised form (as in `MR_identities.md` Step 4). No weighting by W and no independence across particles are
  52| used.
  53| 
  54| (TR-c) ‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ ¼Σ_r‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞; MPM ≠ S₀ forces this ≥ ½ (`LT_theorem.md` Step 4), so Markov gives
  55| 2(g + e_L). Every particle state was evaluated (CC1–CC2), so {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {A_{r,0} = 0} and P ≤ E[1 − A_{r,0}] ≤ δ + e_L.
  56| 
  57| (TR-d) e_L ≤ e^{−L/M}, so 1_𝒜e_L ≤ e^{−Q} → 0 in probability (Q as in P-OVL∞), and 1_𝒜g ≤ 21·1_𝒜o₁ → 0; integrate the truncated conditional bounds
  58| (bounded convergence). HPM via Lemma PC and `D_theorem.md` §3: P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) +
  59| E[1_𝒜 min(1, δ + e_L)] → 0, where S† := the hpm_better-maximiser of F over Ω and P(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) → 0. ∎
  60| 
  61| ## Remarks (honest label)
  62| 
  63| - P-OVL∞ involves no final-particle statistic; it is a condition on (π, π₀) relative to the executed burn-in L (on (π, π₀)
  64|   alone once L is the production budget; MP1 issue 2). It is a **global overlap** condition: M is a
  65|   maximum over all of Ω, not computed by the method. Since M ≥ w(S₀) = π(S₀)/π₀(S₀), on 𝒜 P-OVL∞ forces π₀(S₀) ≥ π(S₀)/M, i.e. localised to 𝒜, π₀(S₀)·L → ∞ in probability under P-CONC (SW1 #11).
  66| - Abstract positive-target example (BT1 §2; **not** a realisation of the coded regression target — on a coded 3-state
  67|   space p = 2, K = 1 and d ≡ 0, so π₀ = π; SW1 #2): with π(s) = π₀(s) = 1 − ε, a second state of posterior mass ε/2 and
  68|   start mass εe^{−H}, M ≥ e^{H}/2 for any H. So, for abstract targets, start mass alone does not control M and the
  69|   conditions of C (π₀(S₀) → 1) and TR (M = o(L)) are not nested. Converse (abstract; C1 Opus #9): given π, M_n → ∞ with
  70|   M_n = o(L) and δ < 1, put π₀(s) := (1 − δ)/M_n and π₀(S) := c·π(S) for S ≠ s with c := (1 − (1 − δ)/M_n)/δ; then
  71|   w(s) = M_n, w(S) = 1/c ≤ 1 elsewhere, so M = M_n = o(L) while π₀(s) → 0. Whether coded regression targets separate them is open.
  72| - TR does not repair W: the evidence is not updated in the terminal rounds. In the "near" example
  73|   (`numerics/RESULTS_v1_sec4b.txt`) the PIPs are repaired while W stays collapsed.
  74| - Improves BLIND_astra2 Thm 5 in the concentrating regime: no log(p+1)/N_e → 0 condition and no union over coordinates.
  75| 
  76| ## Numerical falsification
  77| 
  78| `numerics/RESULTS_v3.txt` (run_checks_v3.py): exact minorization min_{x,y} K_σ(x, y)/π(y) ≥ 1/M for 200 random fixed orders
  79| σ on three targets (no violation); E‖p̂_r − 1‖_∞ ≤ min(1, g + e_L) by simulation. In the "near" case the tested bound is
  80| vacuous (min(1, g + e_L) = 1, M = 1.3e6): it shows repair **outside** TR's sufficient regime, not a validation of TR with
  81| collapsed W (SW1 #19). LC2's reviewer additionally enumerated all orders (up to 720) on 12 small targets.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W3-SCR — code check: what `local_certified` means in the coded output
   2| 
   3| Source: `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/` as read at main @ 2252d57 (identical files copied to `numerics/core_copy/`, hashes in
   4| `numerics/core_copy/SHA256SUMS_source.txt`). The core files were last changed at commit 72785fe and are byte-identical
   5| at the later HEAD 2ac3896 (hashes re-verified by the lead and by the Opus council seat). Every line reference below is to that tree.
   6| 
   7| ## The local search (`cpp/v3_engine.h:379-419`)
   8| `local_search(centre, ell, …)` keeps a current centre C and repeats:
   9| 1. **Complete scan of the coded neighbourhood of C** (lines 394-406): every flip j = 1..p — a deletion if j ∈ C, an
  10|    addition if j ∉ C **unless |C| ≥ K, in which case the addition is skipped** (line 397) — then every swap
  11|    (j ∈ C out, l ∉ C in). Every scanned model is scored (`eval`, line 391).
  12| 2. `best` = the scanned neighbour with the largest F (exact ties by lexicographic order, line 392).
  13| 3. If `best.F > C.F` (strict, line 408): if `moves ≥ ell`, stop with `local_limit = true`,
  14|    `termination = "move_limit"`, `returned = best.S` (a model that was scored as a neighbour but was **not** scanned as a
  15| centre by this search),
  16|    `local_certified` stays false (line 410). Otherwise move to `best` and repeat (line 412).
  17| 4. Else (no scanned neighbour has F strictly larger than F(C)): stop with `termination = "no_improvement"`,
  18|    **`local_certified = true`, `returned = C.S`** (line 414).
  19| 
  20| **CC1.** A search archive has `local_certified = TRUE` if and only if it stopped at a centre C whose complete coded
  21| neighbourhood was scanned and contains no model with F strictly larger than F(C); `returned` is that C.
  22| 
  23| The two searches of a final run (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:453-481`):
  24| - **final local search** from the best scored model so far, cap ℓ_n (line 456) → archive `fit$local_search`;
  25| - **LS0** from the start mode S̃₀, cap ℓ_n + |S̃₀| (lines 469-476) → archive `fit$ls0`.
  26| 
  27| ## The reported flag (`v3_run.R:143-149, 174-200`)
  28| - `fit$hpm` = the best model of the whole ledger (all scored models), line 142.
  29| - Status ≠ `completed` ⇒ `local_certified <- FALSE` (line 146). Early returns of `v3_fit.R` keep the initial
  30|   `local_certified = FALSE` (`v3_fit.R:76`).
  31| - Completed run (v3.1, `ls0` on): `cert_final` = final archive certified **and** `hpm` identical to its `returned`
  32|   (line 179); `cert_ls0` = LS0 archive certified **and** `hpm` identical to its `returned` (line 193);
  33|   `local_certified = cert_final || cert_ls0` (line 194); `local_certified_by ∈ {both, final, ls0, none}` (line 195).
  34| - `local_limit = final_local_limit || ls0_local_limit` (line 197): a move cap was hit in either search. It is *not*
  35|   the negation of `local_certified` (e.g. LS0 capped while the HPM is the certified final-search endpoint).
  36| - Enumeration branch (`v3_exact.R:15`): `local_certified = (status == "exact")`; the HPM is then the exact maximiser of
  37|   F over Ω = {|S| ≤ K}, hence has no strictly better neighbour in Ω.
  38| 
  39| **CC2 (the coded meaning).** `fit$local_certified = TRUE` ⇒ (i) the fit has status `completed` or `exact`, so the
  40| output event 𝒪 holds; (ii) the **reported HPM Ŝ = `fit$hpm`** is *locally optimal*: no model obtained from Ŝ by one
  41| deletion, one addition (when |Ŝ| < K) or one swap has F strictly larger than F(Ŝ). The certificate refers to the
  42| reported model itself: a displaced centre's certificate does not transfer to the HPM (e.g. after an exact-F tie
  43| change), and the top-level flag requires one of the certified archives to return the HPM itself (ruling RULINGS_2 #8,
  44| test `tests/changed_units.R:56-72`).
  45| 
  46| **CC3 (the archives).** On a completed run, independently of the top-level flag, `fit$local_search$returned` is
  47| locally optimal whenever `fit$local_search$local_certified`, and `fit$ls0$returned` is locally optimal whenever
  48| `fit$ls0$local_certified` (CC1). These are printed too, so the theorem can be stated for every certified endpoint.
  49| 
  50| **CC4 (cap).** At |C| = K additions are not scanned. Any statement that uses "no improving addition" needs
  51| |Ŝ| ≤ K − 1; the theorem's size condition |Ŝ| ≤ q_n with q_n ≤ K − 1 ensures it.
  52| 
  53| **CC5 (score).** F(S) = `logprior[|S|]` + `logm(S)` with `logm = logCn − ½(ldH − ldA) − ν log(2b₀ + Q)`
  54| (`cpp/v3_score.h:223`), ν = a₀ + n/2, a₀ = b₀ = 0.01 (`cpp/v3_score.h:14`, `cpp/v3_score.h:57`), `logprior[k] = log w(k) − log W_K`,
  55| `log w(k) = −log 2 − log C(2p−1, k)` (`cpp/v3_score.h:64-70`). X columns and y are standardised with the (n−1) sample SD
  56| (`v3_preprocess.R:37-68, 118-123`), so ‖x_j‖² = n−1 and y′y = n−1. This is the score of
  57| `Theory_work/Wave1C/FINAL/sections/s1_setting.tex:9-13`. The scorer has numerical branches (Q recomputed in a
  58| non-negative form when Q < 1e-8·y′y, `cpp/v3_score.h:218-219`; Cholesky / refactor / QR routes, `cpp/v3_score.h:231-234`);
  59| under EX-A they return the same Q and determinants, so they do not change F.
  60| 
  61| **CC6 (scanned models reach the ledger; what the archives print).** Every model evaluated in a scan goes through
  62| `eval` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:391`), which emits a ledger event (`v3_engine.h:89-99`); the ledger offers every freshly
  63| scored model to the HPM running best (`cpp/v3_ledger.h:84-95, 99-112`), and a cache hit is a model that this run's
  64| ledger already processed (`v3_ledger.h:96-98`; the final run builds a new cache and ledger together, inherited models
  65| are rescored and offered to this ledger, and final search and LS0 use the same ledger and cache,
  66| `cpp/v3_core.cpp:395-481`). The one non-emitting evaluation is the initial centre of the final search
  67| (`eval(C, …, false)`), which is the current HPM and was therefore already offered. Hence, on a completed run and under EX-A, **F(Ŝ) ≥ F(N) for every N in the coded
  68| neighbourhood of every completely scanned centre** of each search that was run (the final search; LS0 when
  69| enabled, which is the default — with `ls0 = FALSE` there is no `fit$ls0`). Each archive prints its scanned centres with
  70| their scores and completeness flags (`scanned_centres`, `scanned_F`, `scan_complete`; `cpp/v3_core.cpp:351-353`,
  71| `v3_engine.h:407`), its path, and `returned`. When a search stops on its move cap (`termination = "move_limit"`),
  72| `returned` is the best scanned neighbour of the last scanned centre, with strictly larger F (`v3_engine.h:408-410`).
  73| 
  74| ## Numerical confirmation (N0)
  75| `numerics/n0_fidelity.py` on a production fit (iid design, n = 100, p = 400; `numerics/n0_out.txt`): the independent
  76| Python score agrees with the core's F with
  77| a maximum absolute difference of 6.0e-13 over 16,004 core-scored models of sizes 4-8 (after aligning the prior normaliser W_K = Σ_k C(p,k) w(k)); the reported certified HPM is locally optimal under the
  78| independent Python scan of the coded neighbourhood.
  79| 
  80| ## Consequence for the statement
  81| The theorem is stated for **locally optimal models** (LO) of the coded neighbourhood; CC2-CC3 map the printed flags to
  82| LO. Premise EX-A (exact scores and arithmetic) is needed, as in every reported-model theorem of the chapter. No premise
  83| on uniforms, calibration, the start mode or LS0's centre is used: the argument never looks at how the search arrived.

   7| **PROVED-CHECKED.** Council passed in round 1: gpt-6-astra **9.3**, Claude Opus 5.5 **8.9**, all six gates PASS on

  11| ## 2. The statement as proved (`STATEMENT.md`, v3.4) and changes vs the card
  12| 
  13| **Code check first (`CODE_CHECK.md`, CC1-CC6).** `fit$local_certified = TRUE` means: the fit completed (so 𝒪 holds)
  14| and the **reported HPM Ŝ itself** is a scanned endpoint of the final local search or of LS0 (or, on the enumeration
  15| branch, the enumerated maximiser) with **no strictly better model among all single deletions, all single additions
  16| (only when |Ŝ| < K) and all swaps**. `local_certified_by` says which search; `local_limit` (a move cap was hit in
  17| either search) is *not* its negation. Each search archive also prints its scanned centres with scores, and every
  18| scanned neighbour reaches the ledger, so F(Ŝ) ≥ F(N) for every neighbour N of every scanned centre (CC6).
  19| 
  20| **Results** (fixed standardised design, Gaussian errors, exact arithmetic EX-A; no premise on the start mode, leakage,
  21| blocks, uniforms or calibration; every seed):
  22| - **SCR-A (screening, non-asymptotic).** If the sparse visibility Γ_n(q) — the noiseless one-step gain of the best
  23|   missing truth, minimised over all models of size ≤ q missing a truth — satisfies the explicit margin MC(q, x), then
  24|   with probability ≥ 1 − 3e^{-x} **every** locally optimal model of size ≤ q ≤ K−1 contains S₀. Hence
  25|   P(𝒪 ∩ {certified} ∩ {|Ŝ| ≤ q} ∩ {S₀ ⊄ Ŝ}) ≤ 3e^{-x}, and the same for every certified search endpoint.
  26|   Asymptotic form (A∞): it suffices that √Γ_n(q_n) ≥ (1+δ)[τ_n√(2 log p + log n) + σ√(2 q_n log p)].
  27| - **Corollary A1 = the card.** Sparse eigenvalue floor κ on sets of size q_n + s₀ (or only the weaker directional
  28|   floor), fixed coefficients (θ_min ≥ b, ‖θ*‖₁ ≤ M), (q_n + 1) log p + log n ≤ c₁n with c₁ = κ²b²/(200(M² + σ²)):
  29|   the probability → 0. Covers p ≤ n^A with any q_n = o(n/log n), and q_n up to order n/log(p ∨ n).
  30| - **SCR-A° / A1° (self-normalised).** Each missing truth competes against the residual scale of the model at hand,
  31|   not the total signal: beta-min θ_min ≥ 16σκ^{-1}√(((q_n+1) log p + log n)/n) suffices (no fixed coefficients).
  32| - **SCR-M (master gap theorem) and SCR-G (uncertified runs).** On one event of probability ≥ 1 − 4e^{-x}, every model
  33|   S of a deterministic family that misses a truth has a truth-addition improving F by at least an explicit
  34|   deterministic gap δ_S; under A1's hypotheses δ_S > c₂n, c₂ = κ²b²/(104(M² + σ²)). Consequences, with probability → 1:
  35|   (i) every **scanned centre** of size ≤ q_n whose score is within c₂n of the reported score contains S₀ — no
  36|   certificate needed; (ii) if a search **stops on its move cap**, its returned model contains S₀ whenever its last
  37|   scanned centre is within c₂n of the best score (so an uncertified reported model can still be covered);
  38|   (iii) the coded search never drops a truth while sizes stay ≤ q_n. The model-count entropy is replaced by a
  39|   geometric complexity (Gaussian width of the witness directions).
  40| - **Excess set and exact recovery.** Lemma L5.1: every locally optimal strict superset of S₀ satisfies an explicit
  41|   inequality (EC′) in the conditional lengths α(S) and the dual-direction factor ω(S) of its excess columns.
  42|   **SCR-C:** with s₀ bounded and a floor φ ≥ 2 log p/(2 log p + log n) + ε on supersets of S₀ of size ≤ q_n (for
  43|   p ≤ n^A: φ ≥ 2A/(2A+1) + ε), a sparse certified model **equals** S₀ with probability → 1.
  44| - **SCR-R** (least-squares refit on a certified model: prediction error ≤ σ²(√k + √(2k log(ep/k) + 4 log n))², no
  45|   floor needed) and **SCR-N** (sharpness: just below the threshold τ_n√(2 log p + log n), the empty model is locally
  46|   optimal with probability → 1 — the constant 1 of (A∞) cannot be lowered at q = 0).
  47| 
  48| **Changes vs the card** (all strengthenings; the card is Corollary A1): floor on all (q_n+s₀)-sets → visibility /
  49| directional floor (non-true columns may be arbitrarily collinear); q_n = o(n/log n) → c₁n/log(p ∨ n); fixed
  50| coefficients → beta-min at rate σ√(𝐋_n/n); reported model only → every certified endpoint **and uncertified runs**;
  51| "contains S₀" → "= S₀" under a near-orthogonality floor, plus an explicit inequality on the excess set in general.
  52| **Answers to the brief's questions:** "= S₀ up to a controlled set" — yes in the form (EC′) and SCR-C; no general bound
  53| on |Ŝ∖S₀| is possible from the certificate alone (reviewers' constructions of locally optimal strict supersets);

 214| ## 3. What is and is not claimed
 215| - Claimed: SCR-A (+A∞), SCR-A° (+A°∞), SCR-M (M1-M6), SCR-G, Lemma B (B1-B3, B2°, B2d), A1, A1°, Lemma L5.1 (EC′),

 219|   argument is not attempted) or outside the family 𝓗 / the size q_n; exact recovery outside the floor of SCR-C
 220|   (supersets of S₀ can be LO under correlation — numerics N2, R01's and R04's constructions); a bound on |Ŝ∖S₀| in
 221|   general designs; any statement about a reported model that is neither certified nor covered by SCR-G; any statement

 103| and Corollary L5.2 (with CC2-CC3) gives the claim. For p ≤ n^A, ϑ_n ≤ 2A/(2A+1). ∎
 104| 
 105| **Remark (what is and is not claimed beyond the floor).** The floor φ_n(q_n) enters twice: as a lower bound for the
 106| conditional lengths α(S) (the determinant penalty, Step 1) and through ω(S) ≤ 1/φ (Step 2). A condition on ω alone is
 107| **not** sufficient (R04 finding 1: two nearly collinear excess columns have ω ≤ 2 but conditional lengths ≈ 11/n, their
 108| determinant penalty is O(1) instead of ½ log n, and S₀ plus that pair is LO with probability bounded away from 0).
 109| The general tool is (EC′), which keeps both α(S) and ω(S); no asymptotic theorem in terms of (α, ω) is claimed here.
 110| 
 111| ## SCR-R (refit accuracy)
 112| Let 𝓔_R := E3a(q_n, 2 log n), failure probability ≤ 2q_n n^{-2} → 0. Work on 𝓔_R intersected with the screening event
 113| supplied by SCR-A or SCR-A° (whichever hypothesis is assumed). Let C ∈ 𝒞 with 1 ≤ |C| = k ≤ q_n; then C ⊇ S₀, so
 114| μ ∈ span X_C and, the columns being centred, the least-squares fitted mean satisfies
 115|  P_Cy_c − μ = P_CCε = P_Cε,  ‖P_Cy_c − μ‖² = ‖P_Cε‖² ≤ σ²U(k, 2 log n) ≤ σ²(√k + √(2k log(ep/k) + 4 log n))²
 116| (log C(p,k) ≤ k log(ep/k)); **this prediction bound needs no eigenvalue floor.** If moreover λ_min(G_C) ≥ φ(n−1) > 0,
 117| G_C is invertible, θ̂_C − θ*_C = G_C^{-1}X_Cᵀε, X(θ̂_C − θ*) = P_Cε, and
 118|  ‖θ̂_C − θ*‖₂² = εᵀX_CG_C^{-2}X_Cᵀε ≤ ‖P_Cε‖²/λ_min(G_C) ≤ the same bound /(φ(n−1)),
 119| using X_CG_C^{-2}X_Cᵀ ⪯ λ_min(G_C)^{-1}P_C. ∎

   2| 
   3| Uses L1 (L1.2-L1.4), L2 ((T1), E2⁻).
   4| 
   5| **Statement.** Model G, EX-A, n ≥ 3, p ≥ 1. Let L_n := 2 log(2p−1) + log n,
   6| B_n := ((n+1)/n)(n − 0.98)(1 − exp(−L_n/(n + 0.02))), and x > 0 with 4a_x ≤ 1 (a_x = √(x/(n−1))). If
   7|  (i) √γ(t|∅) + σ√(2 log(2s₀) + 2x) ≤ τ_n(1 − 4a_x)√B_n for every t ∈ S₀, and
   8|  (ii) √γ(j|∅) + σ√(2 log(2p) + 2x) ≤ τ_n(1 − 4a_x)√B_n for every j ∉ S₀,
   9| then P(∅ is LO) ≥ 1 − 4e^{-x}. Here γ(j|∅) = (x_jᵀμ)²(n+1)/n², and
  10| (1 − n^{-2})(1 − u_n/2)L_n ≤ B_n ≤ L_n with u_n := L_n/(n + 0.02); so B_n = L_n(1 + o(1)) when log p = o(n).
  11| 
  12| *Proof.* *At the empty model.* R_∅ = I, a(j|∅) = n − 1 + 1/(n+1) = n²/(n+1), a_1(j|∅) = n, so D(j|∅) = n,
  13| γ(j|∅) = (x_jᵀμ)²(n+1)/n², Q_∅ = n − 1 and (n/(n+1))g_y(j|∅) = (x_jᵀy)²/n. K ≥ 1, so 𝒩(∅) is the set of the p
  14| singletons, and by L1.4 (k = 0)
  15|  F({j}) − F(∅) = −log(2p−1) − ½ log n + ν·log[(n − 0.98)/(n − 0.98 − (x_jᵀy)²/n)].
  16| Since (log(2p−1) + ½ log n)/ν = L_n/(n + 0.02), F({j}) ≤ F(∅) iff (x_jᵀy)²/n ≤ (n − 0.98)(1 − exp(−L_n/(n+0.02))),
  17| i.e. (using (x_jᵀy)²/n = (n/(n+1))·g_{y_c}(j|∅)/τ̂²) iff
  18|  g_{y_c}(j|∅) ≤ τ̂²·B_n.   (★)
  19| The bounds on B_n: put c_n := (n+1)(n − 0.98)/(n(n + 0.02)) = 1 − 0.98/(n² + 0.02n) ∈ [1 − n^{-2}, 1), so
  20| B_n = c_n(n + 0.02)(1 − e^{-u_n}). Upper: 1 − e^{-u} ≤ u gives B_n ≤ c_nL_n ≤ L_n. Lower: if u_n ≥ 2 the claimed lower
  21| bound is ≤ 0 < B_n; if u_n < 2, 1 − e^{-u} ≥ u(1 − u/2) ≥ 0 gives B_n ≥ c_n(1 − u_n/2)L_n ≥ (1 − n^{-2})(1 − u_n/2)L_n.

  23| v = (n−1)(n+1)/n² < 1 (x_j is centred, so x_jᵀCε = x_jᵀε). By (T1) and union bounds, with probability ≥ 1 − 2e^{-x}:
  24| |ζ_t| ≤ σ√(2 log(2s₀) + 2x) for all t ∈ S₀ and |ζ_j| ≤ σ√(2 log(2p) + 2x) for all j ∉ S₀. On E2⁻(x) (probability
  25| ≥ 1 − 2e^{-x}; it is an event about the noncentral quantity ‖μ + Cε‖², see L2), τ̂² ≥ τ_n²(1 − 4a_x) ≥ τ_n²(1 − 4a_x)².

  28| no other neighbour. ∎

  30| **Consequence 1 (the constant of (A∞) at q = 0, for the statement about LO models).** Fix A > 0, δ ∈ (0, 1), σ > 0
  31| and take the sequence: p = ⌈n^A⌉ ∨ 2, s₀ = 1, S₀ = {1}, x_1 orthogonal to all other columns (the other columns are

  36| B_n = (2 log p + log n)(1 + o(1)), τ_n ≥ σ and 2 log(2p) + 2x_n = 2 log p + o(log n). (i):

  38| probability → 1 there is an LO model of size 0 missing S₀, although √Γ_n(0) is within the factor 1 − δ of the
  39| threshold of (A∞). So in (A∞) the constant 1 multiplying τ_n√(2 log p + log n) cannot be replaced by a smaller one
  40| (as a statement about all LO models of size ≤ q_n; whether the code then reports ∅ is not claimed — N1 shows that it
  41| does report certified sparse models missing truths when signals are below the threshold).
  42| 
  43| **Consequence 2 (a margin condition Δ_n(0) ≥ C log(p ∨ n) alone does not give screening).** Take p = s₀ = 2,
  44| S₀ = {1, 2}, x_1ᵀx_2 = (n−1)r with 1 − r = 1/n, θ* = (b, −b) with b² = (log n)², σ fixed. Then μ = b(x_1 − x_2),

  46| x_1ᵀμ = −x_2ᵀμ = (n−1)b(1−r), so γ(1|∅) = γ(2|∅) = (n−1)²(n+1)b²(1−r)²/n² ~ (log n)²/n → 0. With x_n = √(log n),

  49| bound Δ(√Δ − c_θ)²/(n‖θ*‖₁²) ~ (log n)²/n is asymptotically equal to Γ_n(0) (their ratio tends to 1, since

   1| # L7 — the master gap theorem SCR-M and its corollaries (geometric noise complexity; uncertified runs)
   2| 
   3| Origin: proposals 1, 2 and 4 of the better-theorem review R02 (adopted). Notation: g⁻_S denotes the scalar lower bound for the gain defined below (the Gram matrix of L1 is not used here).
   4| Uses L1 (L1.1-L1.4, L1.7), L2 (E2⁺; tools
   5| T1-T3), CODE_CHECK (CC1-CC6). SCR-A and SCR-A° (L3) are special cases (M3 below); their direct proofs are kept.
   6| 
   7| ## Setting
   8| **Family and witnesses.** Let 𝓗 be a family of subsets of [p], each of size ≤ K−1, that is a function of (X, θ*, σ)
   9| only; 𝓗⁻ := {S ∈ 𝓗 : S ⊉ S₀}, M_𝓗 := |𝓗⁻| (if 𝓗⁻ = ∅ everything below is vacuous). For S ∈ 𝓗⁻ let t(S) ∈ S₀∖S be a
  10| witness that is a function of (X, θ*, σ) only. The **default (maximising) witness** is the smallest index maximising
  11| γ(·|S) over S₀∖S (L2); it is the one used in M3, M4 and SCR-G, where γ(t(S)|S) ≥ Γ_n(q) is needed. Write t = t(S),
  12| k = |S|, m_S² = μᵀR_Sμ, and
  13|  d_S := −s_S·R_Sx_t / a(t|S)^{1/2}, s_S := sgn(x_tᵀR_Sμ) (sgn 0 := 1);  e_S := R_Sμ/m_S (e_S := 0 if m_S = 0).
  14| These are centred vectors of R^n with ‖d_S‖ ≤ 1, ‖e_S‖ ≤ 1 (R_S² ⪯ R_S, L1.1).
  15| 
  16| **Noise complexity.** For a finite set 𝓓 ⊂ R^n of vectors of norm ≤ 1 and g ~ N(0, I_n) let
  17| w(𝓓) := E max_{d∈𝓓∪{0}} dᵀg (Gaussian width; 0 ≤ w(𝓓) ≤ √(2 log(|𝓓| + 1)) and w(𝓓) ≤ √(dim span 𝓓)). For x > 0:
  18|  b_𝓗(x) := min{ √(2 log M_𝓗 + 2x), w({d_S : S ∈ 𝓗⁻}) + √(2x) },
  19|  c_𝓗(x) := min{ √(2 log M_𝓗 + 2x), w({e_S : S ∈ 𝓗⁻}) + √(2x) }.
  20| For 𝓗 = 𝓗_q := {S : |S| ≤ q} (q ≤ K−1): M_𝓗 ≤ N_q, so b_𝓗(x) ≤ r_n(q, x) and c_𝓗(x) ≤ r_n(q, x).
  21| 
  22| **Deterministic gap.** For S ∈ 𝓗⁻ (with a_x = √(x/(n−1)), τ̄_n(x) = τ_n(1 + 2a_x)):
  23|  B_S := log((2p−1−k)/(k+1)) + ½ log D(t|S)  (≥ 0, since 2p−1−k ≥ k+1 and D ≥ 1);
  24|  g⁻_S := (√γ(t|S) − σ b_𝓗(x))₊²;
  25|  U_S := 1.02 τ̄_n(x)² + (n/(n+1))·[m_S² + 2σ m_S c_𝓗(x) + σ²(n−1)(1 + 2a_x + 2a_x²)];
  26|  Ū_S := min{U_S, (n − 0.98)τ̄_n(x)²};  u_S := n g⁻_S / ((n+1) Ū_S);
  27|  **δ_S := −ν log(1 − u_S) − B_S** if u_S < 1, and δ_S := +∞ if u_S ≥ 1;  δ_𝓗 := min_{S∈𝓗⁻} δ_S.
  28| Conventions: δ_S := +∞ for S ∈ 𝓗∖𝓗⁻; if 𝓗⁻ = ∅, δ_𝓗 := +∞ and b_𝓗, c_𝓗 are not used.
  29| All of these are functions of (X, θ*, σ, x) only.
  30| 
  31| ## Theorem SCR-M (master gap theorem)
  32| Model G, EX-A, x > 0. There is an event 𝓔_M with P(𝓔_M) ≥ 1 − 4e^{-x} on which, for **every** S ∈ 𝓗⁻,
  33|  F(S ∪ t(S)) − F(S) ≥ δ_S,   and S ∪ t(S) ∈ 𝒩(S).
  34| (If Ū_S is replaced by (n − 0.98)τ̄_n(x)² for all S, the event E4_𝓗 below is not needed and the bound is 1 − 3e^{-x}.)
  35| 
  36| *Proof.* **Events.** E1_𝓗 := {max_{S∈𝓗⁻} d_Sᵀε ≤ σ b_𝓗(x)}; E4_𝓗 := {max_{S∈𝓗⁻} e_Sᵀε ≤ σ c_𝓗(x)}; E2⁺(x) (L2).
  37| P(E1_𝓗ᶜ) ≤ e^{-x}: b_𝓗(x) is the smaller of two deterministic numbers, so it suffices that each of
  38| {max_S d_Sᵀε ≤ σ√(2 log M_𝓗 + 2x)} and {max_S d_Sᵀε ≤ σ(w + √(2x))} has probability ≥ 1 − e^{-x}. First: d_Sᵀε is
  39| N(0, σ²‖d_S‖²) with ‖d_S‖ ≤ 1 (identically 0 if d_S = 0), so P(d_Sᵀε > σ√(2 log M_𝓗 + 2x)) ≤ e^{-x}/M_𝓗 (one-sided
  40| bound P(Z > r) ≤ e^{-r²/(2v²)}); sum over the M_𝓗 sets. Second: ε = σg and f(g) := max_{d∈𝓓∪{0}} dᵀg is 1-Lipschitz
  41| (norms ≤ 1), so by Gaussian concentration (Tsirelson–Ibragimov–Sudakov; Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, Thm 5.6)
  42| P(f(g) > E f(g) + √(2x)) ≤ e^{-x}. The same argument gives P(E4_𝓗ᶜ) ≤ e^{-x}, and P((E2⁺)ᶜ) ≤ 2e^{-x}. Put
  43| 𝓔_M := E1_𝓗 ∩ E4_𝓗 ∩ E2⁺ (intersected with the probability-one event τ̂ > 0).
  44| 
  45| **Numerator.** Fix S ∈ 𝓗⁻, t = t(S). Since R_Sx_t is centred, x_tᵀR_SCε = (R_Sx_t)ᵀε, and
  46|  s_S·x_tᵀR_Sy_c / a(t|S)^{1/2} = |x_tᵀR_Sμ|/a(t|S)^{1/2} + s_S(R_Sx_t)ᵀε/a(t|S)^{1/2} = √γ(t|S) − d_Sᵀε ≥ √γ(t|S) − σ b_𝓗(x)
  47| on E1_𝓗. If the right side is ≥ 0 this gives g_{y_c}(t|S) ≥ (√γ(t|S) − σ b_𝓗)²; otherwise g⁻_S = 0 ≤ g_{y_c}(t|S). So
  48| g_{y_c}(t|S) ≥ g⁻_S.
  49| 
  50| **Denominator.** By L1.1, 0.02τ̂² + q_S(y_c) = [0.02 + (n−1)/(n+1)]τ̂² + (n/(n+1))y_cᵀR_Sy_c, and (R_Sμ centred, R_S ⪯ I)
  51| y_cᵀR_Sy_c = m_S² + 2μᵀR_SCε + (Cε)ᵀR_S(Cε) ≤ m_S² + 2m_S·e_Sᵀε + ‖Cε‖² ≤ m_S² + 2σ m_S c_𝓗(x) + σ²(n−1)(1 + 2a_x + 2a_x²)
  52| on E4_𝓗 ∩ E2⁺ (μᵀR_Sε = m_S e_Sᵀε, also when m_S = 0). With τ̂ ≤ τ̄_n(x) on E2⁺: 0.02τ̂² + q_S(y_c) ≤ U_S. Also
  53| 0.02τ̂² + q_S(y_c) = (0.02 + Q_S)τ̂² ≤ (n − 0.98)τ̄_n(x)² (Q_S ≤ n−1, L1.1). Hence 0.02τ̂² + q_S(y_c) ≤ Ū_S.
  54| 
  55| **Gap.** By L1.4 (k ≤ K−1) and L1.2(iii),
  56|  F(S∪t) − F(S) = −B_S − ν log(1 − u),  u := (n/(n+1))·g_{y_c}(t|S)/(0.02τ̂² + q_S(y_c)) = 1 − (0.02 + Q_{S∪t})/(0.02 + Q_S) ∈ [0, 1).
  57| On 𝓔_M, u ≥ n g⁻_S/((n+1)Ū_S) = u_S; in particular u_S < 1 there, and −ν log(1 − u) ≥ −ν log(1 − u_S). So
  58| F(S∪t) − F(S) ≥ δ_S. (If u_S ≥ 1 for some S the event 𝓔_M is empty and the claim is void.) |S| < K gives S∪t ∈ 𝒩(S). ∎
  59| 
  60| ## Corollaries (all on 𝓔_M; "scanned centre" = completely scanned centre of `fit$local_search` or `fit$ls0`
  61| ## on a completed run)
  62| 
  63| **M1 (screening; any deterministic family).** If δ_S > 0 for every S ∈ 𝓗⁻, then every LO model that belongs to 𝓗
  64| contains S₀; in particular every certified model C ∈ 𝒞 ∩ 𝓗, and Ŝ when `local_certified` and Ŝ ∈ 𝓗.
  65| *Proof.* An LO model S ∈ 𝓗⁻ would have F(S∪t(S)) ≤ F(S) with S∪t(S) ∈ 𝒩(S), contradicting the theorem. CC2-CC3. ∎
  66| 
  67| **M2 (near-best scanned centres; no certificate needed).** Every scanned centre C ∈ 𝓗⁻ satisfies
  68| F(Ŝ) − F(C) ≥ δ_C. Hence every scanned centre C ∈ 𝓗 with F(Ŝ) − F(C) < δ_C (in particular with F(Ŝ) − F(C) < δ_𝓗)
  69| contains S₀.
  70| *Proof.* If C ∈ 𝓗⁻ then |C| ≤ K−1, so the addition C∪t(C) ∈ 𝒩(C) was scanned, scored and reached the ledger; hence
  71| F(Ŝ) ≥ F(C∪t(C)) ≥ F(C) + δ_C (CC6 and the theorem). ∎
  72| 
  73| **M5 (the coded search does not drop truths; capped searches).** Assume δ_S > 0 for every S ∈ 𝓗⁻. Let C be a
  74| scanned centre with C ⊇ S₀ (C need not belong to 𝓗), and let N be the best scanned neighbour of C, with F(N) > F(C)
  75| (the model the search moves to, or returns when it stops on its move cap). If N ∈ 𝓗, then N ⊇ S₀. Consequently: (i) along the path of a
  76| search, once a scanned centre contains S₀, every later model of the path that belongs to 𝓗 — as long as all models in
  77| between do — contains S₀; (ii) if a search stops on its move cap with last scanned centre C ∈ 𝓗, returned model N ∈ 𝓗
  78| and F(Ŝ) − F(C) < δ_C, then C ⊇ S₀ and N ⊇ S₀ — in particular when Ŝ = N, a reported model that this capped search
  79| did not certify (N was scored as a neighbour of C but not scanned as a centre of this search).
  80| *Proof.* N arises from C by one addition, deletion or swap. If N ⊉ S₀ while C ⊇ S₀, N is a deletion C∖{t} or a swap
  81| C∖{t}∪{l} with t ∈ S₀, and S₀∖N = {t}, so t(N) = t. Then N∪t is C (deletion) or C∪{l} (swap). F(C) < F(N); and for
  82| a swap |C| = |N| ≤ K−1, so C∪{l} ∈ 𝒩(C) was scanned and F(C∪{l}) ≤ F(N) (N is the best scanned neighbour of C). In
  83| both cases F(N∪t(N)) ≤ F(N), contradicting F(N∪t(N)) ≥ F(N) + δ_N > F(N) (N ∈ 𝓗⁻). (i) is induction; (ii) is M2
  84| followed by the first statement (CC6: `returned` on a capped search is that best neighbour). ∎
  85| 
  86| **M3 (SCR-A and SCR-A° are special cases).** Let 𝓗 = 𝓗_q, q ≤ K−1, with the default witness. If MC(q, x) holds, or
  87| if MC°(q, x) holds, then δ_S > 0 for every S ∈ 𝓗⁻.
  88| *Proof.* Put L′ := 2 log(2p−1) + log(n+1), so T_n = (n+1)L′/n, and note 1 − e^{-B_S/ν} ≤ B_S/ν ≤ (L′/2)/ν = L′/(n+0.02)
  89| (L1.3). δ_S > 0 iff u_S ≥ 1 or u_S > 1 − e^{-B_S/ν}; so it suffices that u_S > L′/(n + 0.02).
  90| Under MC: √γ(t|S) − σ b_𝓗 ≥ √Γ_n(q) − σ r_n > τ̄_n(x)√T_n > 0, so g⁻_S > τ̄_n(x)²T_n and, using Ū_S ≤ (n − 0.98)τ̄_n(x)²,
